// Performance measurements (MPES §14, §17): time to interactive and showcase update of the built file and of a
// 40 MB stress variant (the embedded renders replicated to full-production size), on the reference profile
// (Chromium, 4x CPU throttling) and with GPU disabled (software compositing, the WARP stand-in).
//   node art/tools/measure-spike.ts <report.json>
import { mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { chromium, type Page } from '@playwright/test';

process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH ??= resolve('.artifacts/ms-playwright');
const TARGET_BYTES = 40 * 1024 * 1024;
const RUNS = 3;

function stressFile(): string {
  const html = readFileSync('dist/index.html', 'utf8');
  const match = /(<script type="application\/json" id="sea-renders">)([^<]*)(<\/script>)/.exec(html);
  if (!match) throw new Error('renders block not found');
  const entries = Object.entries(JSON.parse(match[2]!) as Record<string, unknown>);
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = Object.fromEntries(entries);
  for (let copy = 1; Buffer.byteLength(html) + Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(out)) - match[2]!.length < TARGET_BYTES; copy++) {
    for (const [id, value] of entries) out[`${id}~${copy}`] = value;
  }
  const stressed = html.replace(match[0], () => match[1] + JSON.stringify(out) + match[3]);
  const path = resolve('.artifacts/perf/stress-40mb.html');
  mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
  writeFileSync(path, stressed);
  return path;
}

async function throttled(page: Page, rate: number): Promise<void> {
  const cdp = await page.context().newCDPSession(page);
  await cdp.send('Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate', { rate });
}

async function chooserMs(page: Page, url: string): Promise<number> {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    new MutationObserver((_, observer) => {
      if (!document.querySelector('h1')) return;
      observer.disconnect();
      requestAnimationFrame(() => { (window as unknown as { seaPainted: number }).seaPainted = performance.now(); });
    }).observe(document, { childList: true, subtree: true });
  });
  await page.goto(url + '?lang=en');
  await page.waitForFunction(() => (window as unknown as { seaPainted?: number }).seaPainted !== undefined);
  return Math.round(await page.evaluate(() => (window as unknown as { seaPainted: number }).seaPainted));
}

/** Join as RECOVERY, enter the auction, then time "record win" until the new showcase layer is decoded. */
async function showcaseMs(page: Page, url: string): Promise<{ startMs: number; updateMs: number; heapMB: number; scrubMs: number; decodedMB: number }> {
  const t0 = Date.now();
  await page.goto(url + '?role=student&lang=en');
  await page.locator('#join-code').waitFor();
  const startMs = Date.now() - t0;
  await page.fill('#join-code', 'SEA3-T2-0123456789ABCDEF');
  await page.selectOption('#join-mission', 'RECOVERY');
  await page.click('#join'); await page.click('#record-practice'); await page.click('#student-planning');
  await page.check('#plan-confirm'); await page.click('#student-start-auction');
  await page.locator('dialog button[data-value="ok"]').click();
  await page.locator('#showcase img[data-layer="base"]').waitFor();
  await page.selectOption('#pos-lot', '7'); await page.fill('#card-id', 'ACC-F'); await page.click('#load-card'); await page.fill('#paid', '350000');
  const updateMs = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const start = performance.now();
    document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('#record-win')!.click();
    const img = document.querySelector<HTMLImageElement>('#showcase img[data-layer="ACC-F"]');
    if (!img) throw new Error('layer missing');
    await img.decode();
    return performance.now() - start;
  });
  const heapMB = await page.evaluate(() => (performance as unknown as { memory: { usedJSHeapSize: number } }).memory.usedJSHeapSize / 1048576);
  // Turntable: time from a scrub step to the new frame being decoded (budget 50 ms, MPES §10.3).
  await page.check('#showcase-view-turntable');
  await page.locator('#showcase-turn').waitFor();
  await page.waitForTimeout(300); // let the neighbour pre-decode settle, as a person pausing would
  const scrub: number[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
    scrub.push(await page.evaluate(async () => {
      const input = document.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#showcase-turn')!;
      const start = performance.now();
      input.value = String((Number(input.value) + 1) % (Number(input.max) + 1));
      input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
      await document.querySelector<HTMLImageElement>('#showcase img[data-frame]')!.decode();
      return performance.now() - start;
    }));
    await page.waitForTimeout(120);
  }
  // Decoded pixels currently shown (estimate: width × height × 4 bytes per image in the showcase).
  const decodedMB = await page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLImageElement>('#showcase img, .card-render, .hero-still')]
    .reduce((n, img) => n + img.naturalWidth * img.naturalHeight * 4, 0) / 1048576);
  return { startMs, updateMs: Math.round(updateMs), heapMB: Math.round(heapMB), scrubMs: Math.round(Math.max(...scrub)), decodedMB: Math.round(decodedMB * 10) / 10 };
}

const median = (values: number[]) => [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)[Math.floor(values.length / 2)]!;

const files = { built: resolve('dist/index.html'), stress40: stressFile() };
const profiles = [{ name: 'reference (4x CPU)', args: [] as string[] }, { name: 'reference, GPU disabled', args: ['--disable-gpu'] }];
const results: Record<string, unknown>[] = [];
for (const profile of profiles) {
  const browser = await chromium.launch({ args: profile.args });
  for (const [label, path] of Object.entries(files)) {
    const url = pathToFileURL(path).href;
    const runs: { chooser: number; start: number; update: number; heap: number; scrub: number; decoded: number }[] = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < RUNS; i++) {
      const a = await (await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })).newPage();
      await throttled(a, 4);
      const chooser = await chooserMs(a, url);
      const b = await (await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })).newPage();
      await throttled(b, 4);
      const s = await showcaseMs(b, url);
      runs.push({ chooser, start: s.startMs, update: s.updateMs, heap: s.heapMB, scrub: s.scrubMs, decoded: s.decodedMB });
      await a.context().close(); await b.context().close();
    }
    results.push({
      profile: profile.name, file: label, bytes: readFileSync(path).length,
      chooserMs: median(runs.map(r => r.chooser)), studentStartMs: median(runs.map(r => r.start)),
      showcaseUpdateMs: median(runs.map(r => r.update)), heapMB: median(runs.map(r => r.heap)), turntableScrubMaxMs: median(runs.map(r => r.scrub)), decodedImageMB: median(runs.map(r => r.decoded)), runs: RUNS,
    });
  }
  await browser.close();
}
writeFileSync(resolve(process.argv[2] ?? '.artifacts/perf/spike-measure.json'), JSON.stringify(results, null, 2) + '\n');
console.table(results);
```

### art/tools/pack-models.ts

Paths: `art/tools/pack-models.ts`. SHA-256 `2fa6f9d0484179b9b988a1b1e93aa2c17825ccf022bbed10a4cb3042a6414031`, 3132 bytes.

```ts
// Packs the Blender glTF exports (art/blender/export.py) into the one model file the game embeds (MPES §10).
//
//   node art/tools/pack-models.ts <dir of <stem>.glb> <out .glb>
//
// One scene; a group node per vehicle (named by its stem) holding `base` and one node per part card. Identical
// meshes and materials are shared, vertices welded and reordered for locality (meshoptimizer: the deflated file is
// smaller and draws the same), and attributes quantised (KHR_mesh_quantization), which three.js GLTFLoader reads
// natively, so the game needs no decoder beyond the browser's own DecompressionStream. Measured and rejected (G2):
// simplification at an error of 0.001 visibly changed the hull's shading; 8-bit normals together with the reorder
// made a purchase's model update about 30 ms slower on the reference profile.
import { readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, basename } from 'node:path';
import { deflateRawSync } from 'node:zlib';
import { NodeIO, type Document } from '@gltf-transform/core';
import { KHRMaterialsEmissiveStrength, KHRMeshQuantization } from '@gltf-transform/extensions';
import { dedup, mergeDocuments, prune, quantize, reorder, unpartition, weld } from '@gltf-transform/functions';
import { MeshoptEncoder } from 'meshoptimizer';

const [dir, out] = process.argv.slice(2);
if (!dir || !out) throw new Error('usage: pack-models.ts <dir> <out.glb>');
const io = new NodeIO().registerExtensions([KHRMaterialsEmissiveStrength, KHRMeshQuantization]);

const files = readdirSync(dir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.glb') && f !== basename(out)).sort();
const doc: Document = new (await import('@gltf-transform/core')).Document();
const root = doc.getRoot();
const scene = doc.createScene('showcase');
for (const file of files) {
  const source = await io.read(join(dir, file));
  const map = mergeDocuments(doc, source);
  const group = doc.createNode(file.replace(/\.glb$/, ''));
  scene.addChild(group);
  for (const s of source.getRoot().listScenes()) {
    const merged = map.get(s);
    if (!merged) continue;
    // three.js renames repeated node names (base, base_1, ...), so each node also carries its layer in extras.
    for (const child of (merged as typeof scene).listChildren()) {
      child.setExtras({ ...child.getExtras(), layer: child.getName() });
      group.addChild(child);
    }
    (merged as typeof scene).dispose();
  }
}
root.setDefaultScene(scene);
await MeshoptEncoder.ready;
await doc.transform(
  unpartition(),
  dedup(),
  weld(),
  reorder({ encoder: MeshoptEncoder }),
  quantize({ quantizePosition: 14, quantizeNormal: 10, quantizeColor: 8 }),
  dedup(),
  prune({ keepAttributes: false }),
);
const glb = await io.writeBinary(doc);
writeFileSync(out, glb);
const meshes = root.listMeshes();
const tris = meshes.flatMap(m => m.listPrimitives()).reduce((n, p) => n + (p.getIndices()?.getCount() ?? 0) / 3, 0);
console.log(JSON.stringify({ vehicles: files.length, meshes: meshes.length, materials: root.listMaterials().length,
  uniqueTriangles: Math.round(tris), glb: glb.byteLength, deflated: deflateRawSync(glb, { level: 9 }).byteLength }));
```

```ts
// Review aid: composite transparent render masters over a war-room HUD backdrop (dark gradient, grid).
// Usage: node art/tools/preview.ts <dir-with-pngs> [<out-dir>]   Output: <name>.preview.jpg
import { mkdirSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs';
import { basename, join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import sharp from 'sharp';

function backdrop(width: number, height: number): Buffer {
  const step = Math.round(width / 32);
  const lines: string[] = [];
  for (let x = 0; x <= width; x += step) lines.push(`<line x1="${x}" y1="0" x2="${x}" y2="${height}"/>`);
  for (let y = 0; y <= height; y += step) lines.push(`<line x1="0" y1="${y}" x2="${width}" y2="${y}"/>`);
  return Buffer.from(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="${width}" height="${height}">
    <defs><radialGradient id="g" cx="50%" cy="62%" r="70%"><stop offset="0" stop-color="#26302a"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="#0a0e0d"/></radialGradient></defs>
    <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="url(#g)"/>
    <g stroke="#7fd8b0" stroke-opacity="0.07" stroke-width="1">${lines.join('')}</g></svg>`);
}

const dir = resolve(process.argv[2] ?? '.');
const out = resolve(process.argv[3] ?? dir);
mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
for (const name of readdirSync(dir).filter(f => f.endsWith('.png'))) {
  const image = sharp(join(dir, name));
  const { width = 0, height = 0 } = await image.metadata();
  await sharp(backdrop(width, height)).composite([{ input: join(dir, name) }]).jpeg({ quality: 88 })
    .toFile(join(out, basename(name, '.png') + '.preview.jpg'));
}
console.log(`previews written to ${out}`);
```

### build/build.ts

```ts
// Build CLI (MPES §5.5, D-12). Usage: node build/build.ts [--check]
//   (no flag)  write dist/index.html (dist/ is generated and never committed)
//   --check    build twice from source and fail unless both builds are byte-identical
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname } from 'node:path';
import { OUT, render } from './render.ts';

const describe = (html: string) => `${Buffer.byteLength(html, 'utf8')} bytes, sha256 ${createHash('sha256').update(html, 'utf8').digest('hex')}`;

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const html = await render();
  if (process.argv.includes('--check')) {
    const again = await render();
    if (again !== html) {
      console.error('Two builds from the same source differ: the build is not deterministic.');
      process.exit(1);
    }
    console.log(`Two builds are byte-identical (${describe(html)})`);
    return;
  }
  mkdirSync(dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
  if (existsSync(OUT) && readFileSync(OUT, 'utf8') === html) {
    console.log(`dist/index.html unchanged (${describe(html)})`);
    return;
  }
  writeFileSync(OUT, html, 'utf8');
  console.log(`dist/index.html written (${describe(html)})`);
}

main().catch((error: unknown) => { console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : error); process.exit(1); });
```

### build/render.ts

Paths: `build/render.ts`. SHA-256 `9e148892b450fe7309593091db5aeb25ed8de9d252f28e9e0808c2681a119484`, 5430 bytes.

```ts
// Deterministic single-file renderer (MPES §5.5). The CLI is build/build.ts.
import { build } from 'esbuild';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, relative } from 'node:path';
import { deflateRawSync } from 'node:zlib';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

export const MAX_BYTES = 50 * 1024 * 1024; // MPES §14
export const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL('..', import.meta.url));
export const OUT = join(ROOT, 'dist', 'index.html');
const REQUIRED_NOTICES = ['three.js', 'MIT License', 'Blender'];

function read(path: string): string {
  return readFileSync(join(ROOT, path), 'utf8');
}

/** Builds must not depend on the checkout's line endings. */
function assertLf(dir: string): void {
  for (const name of readdirSync(join(ROOT, dir))) {
    const path = join(dir, name);
    if (statSync(join(ROOT, path)).isDirectory()) { assertLf(path); continue; }
    if (/\.(ts|css|json|html|md|svg)$/.test(name) && read(path).includes('\r')) {
      throw new Error(`CRLF line ending in ${relative(ROOT, join(ROOT, path))}`);
    }
  }
}

export function sha256(text: string): string {
  return createHash('sha256').update(text, 'utf8').digest('base64');
}

interface RenderEntry {
  readonly file: string; readonly id: string; readonly kind: string; readonly sha256: string; readonly depth: number | null; readonly slot?: string;
  readonly frame: { width: number; height: number }; readonly offset: { left: number; top: number }; readonly size: { width: number; height: number };
}
export const RENDERS_DIR = 'content/renders';

/** Committed renders (MPES §11) as one inert JSON object: id -> data URI and placement. Hashes are checked. */
function renders(): string {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(read(`${RENDERS_DIR}/manifest.json`)) as { format: string; entries: RenderEntry[] };
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
  for (const e of manifest.entries) {
    const bytes = readFileSync(join(ROOT, RENDERS_DIR, e.file));
    if (createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex') !== e.sha256) throw new Error(`Render hash mismatch: ${e.file}`);
    out[e.id] = { src: `data:image/${manifest.format};base64,${bytes.toString('base64')}`, kind: e.kind, depth: e.depth, ...(e.slot ? { slot: e.slot } : {}), frame: e.frame, offset: e.offset, size: e.size };
  }
  const json = JSON.stringify(out);
  if (json.includes('<')) throw new Error('Unsafe renders content');
  return json;
}

export const MODELS_DIR = 'content/models';

/**
 * The real-time showcase models (MPES §10): one glTF binary, hash-checked against its manifest, raw-deflated
 * (deterministic at a fixed level) and base64-encoded into an inert block the game inflates with DecompressionStream.
 */
function models(): string {
  const manifest = JSON.parse(read(`${MODELS_DIR}/manifest.json`)) as { file: string; sha256: string };
  const bytes = readFileSync(join(ROOT, MODELS_DIR, manifest.file));
  if (createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex') !== manifest.sha256) throw new Error(`Model hash mismatch: ${manifest.file}`);
  return deflateRawSync(bytes, { level: 9 }).toString('base64');
}

export async function render(): Promise<string> {
  for (const dir of ['source', 'content', 'build']) assertLf(dir);
  for (const file of ['LICENSE', 'THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md']) if (read(file).includes('\r')) throw new Error(`CRLF in ${file}`);
  const version = (JSON.parse(read('package.json')) as { gameVersion: string }).gameVersion;
  const notices = read('THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md');
  for (const needle of REQUIRED_NOTICES) if (!notices.includes(needle)) throw new Error(`Missing notice: ${needle}`);

  const common = { bundle: true, write: false, minify: true, legalComments: 'none', charset: 'utf8', logLevel: 'silent' } as const;
  const script = await build({
    ...common,
    entryPoints: [join(ROOT, 'source', 'main.ts')],
    format: 'iife',
    target: 'es2022',
    define: {
      __SEA_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(version),
      __SEA_NOTICES__: JSON.stringify(notices),
      __SEA_LICENSE__: JSON.stringify(read('LICENSE')),
    },
  });
  const style = await build({ ...common, entryPoints: [join(ROOT, 'source', 'ui', 'styles.css')], loader: { '.css': 'css' } });
  const js = script.outputFiles[0]!.text.trim().replace(/<\/(script)/gi, '<\\/$1').replace(/<!--/g, '<\\!--');
  const css = style.outputFiles[0]!.text.trim();
  if (css.includes('</style')) throw new Error('Unsafe style content');

  const csp = [
    "default-src 'none'",
    `script-src 'sha256-${sha256(js)}'`,
    `style-src 'sha256-${sha256(css)}'`,
    "img-src data:",
    "font-src 'none'",
    "connect-src 'none'",
    "media-src 'none'",
    "object-src 'none'",
    "frame-src 'none'",
    "worker-src 'none'",
    "manifest-src 'none'",
    "base-uri 'none'",
    "form-action 'none'",
  ].join('; ');
  const template = read('build/template.html');
  const html = template
    .replace('{{CSP}}', () => csp)
    .replace('{{VERSION}}', () => version)
    .replace('{{STYLE}}', () => css)
    .replace('{{RENDERS}}', () => renders())
    .replace('{{MODELS}}', () => models())
    .replace('{{SCRIPT}}', () => js);
  if (/\{\{[A-Z]+\}\}/.test(html)) throw new Error('Unfilled template placeholder');
  const bytes = Buffer.byteLength(html, 'utf8');
  if (bytes > MAX_BYTES) throw new Error(`dist/index.html is ${bytes} bytes; limit ${MAX_BYTES}`);
  return html;
}

```

```markdown
# Classroom quick start / Guide de démarrage en classe

[English](#english) · [Français](#français)

## English

SEA Game is one file, `index.html`. It works offline and needs no installation or account. The instructor and the student teams each open the same file in their own browser tab. **The apps do not connect to each other**: the instructor announces everything aloud, and the instructor's screen is the official record.

Supported: Windows 11 with a current Chrome, Edge or Firefox, for the instructor and every team. Other systems and Safari are not supported.

### Before class (10 minutes)

1. Give every device the same `index.html` (USB key, shared drive, email) or the web link your school uses.
2. On each device, open the file and check that the role chooser appears. Try **Français / English** once. On a projector or a bright room, choose **Projector theme** (first screen, or **Menu → Projector theme**); **War-room theme** switches back.
3. Instructor: open **Instructor**. Students: open **Student team**. Use one tab per role; keep the tab open for the whole session.
4. Use fictional team names only. Do not enter personal or operational information.
5. Each team shares four roles: a planner (fills in the plan), a bidder (the only voice in the auction), a card tracker (records wins in the team's tab) and a presenter (answers the presentation questions at the debrief).

### Run the session

| Step | Instructor | Students |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Setup | Choose the number of teams, then **Generate session**. The defaults suit most classes; **More options** changes how lots are revealed, the timer and the bid increment. Write the session code on the board and give each team its number. | Enter the session code, your team number and your mission, then **Start**. |
| 2. Practice | **Start practice**, then do the four practice steps with the training card. Announce "Team 1 wins the practice lot". **Open planning**. | **Record practice win**, then **Continue to planning**. |
| 3. Planning | Confirm each team's mission in the table. When everyone is ready: **Close planning and start the auction**. | Check the mission minimums, write priorities and risks, and tick **We confirmed this mission with the instructor**. When the instructor starts the auction: **The instructor started the auction**. |
| 4. Auction (7 rounds × 10 lots) | For each lot: announce the round, lot and card ID, **Open bidding**, click the team that bids (each click accepts the next offer: the start price, then up by the bid increment you chose at setup, $50,000 by default), then **Sell to Team N** or **No sale**, and **Next lot**. Keyboard: digits for teams, S sell, U no sale, O open, R reveal, N next, P pause, E +30 s. | Enter the announced card ID and **Show card**. If the instructor announces that you won, enter the price and **We won this card**; otherwise **Not ours, next lot**. |
| 5. Build | Show the results table so teams can check their records. **Open submissions**. | Compare your purchases with the instructor's results. Fix only recording mistakes, then **Our records match. Continue to the bid**. |
| 6. Submit | **Enter submissions privately** (do not project). Enter each team's profit and tick **Submitted**. **Leave private mode**, then **Close submissions**. | Choose a profit (amount or percent of cost), then **Done: tell the instructor** and tell the instructor your profit privately. |
| 7. Debrief | Show the results: the lowest bid per score point wins; ties go to the lower bid, then the higher score. Discuss gaps and trade-offs. **Close the room**. | Compare your plan with what you built. **Close** after the results. |

Rules in one breath: a team can win at most 2 lots per round; prices go up by the bid increment chosen at setup ($50,000 by default) and are always the start price plus whole $50,000 steps; a build must meet every mission minimum and score above 0 to be eligible.

### Corrections during the auction

- Wrong winner or price: **Correct the result…** before closing the lot, with a short reason.
- Already closed: **Void this result…** with a reason, then open bidding again and record the right result.
- Timer: **Pause**, **Resume**, **Add 30 s**. When time is up nothing is sold automatically; you decide.

### Keep a backup

Export a backup from **Menu → Export backup** after setup, after each round and at the end. Each role exports only its own data. If something goes wrong, see the [recovery guide](RECOVERY_GUIDE.md).

## Français

SEA Game tient en un seul fichier, `index.html`. Il fonctionne hors ligne, sans installation ni compte. L’instructeur et les équipes ouvrent le même fichier, chacun dans son onglet. **Les applications ne sont pas reliées** : l’instructeur annonce tout à voix haute et son écran fait foi.

Configuration prise en charge : Windows 11 avec une version récente de Chrome, Edge ou Firefox, pour l’instructeur et chaque équipe. Les autres systèmes et Safari ne sont pas pris en charge.

### Avant la séance (10 minutes)

1. Remettez le même `index.html` à chaque appareil (clé USB, lecteur partagé, courriel) ou utilisez le lien Web de votre établissement.
2. Sur chaque appareil, ouvrez le fichier et vérifiez que le choix du rôle s’affiche. Essayez une fois **Français / English**. Avec un projecteur ou dans une salle claire, choisissez **Thème projecteur** (premier écran, ou **Menu → Thème projecteur**) ; **Thème salle de crise** revient au thème sombre.
3. Instructeur : **Instructeur**. Équipes : **Équipe étudiante**. Un onglet par rôle, gardé ouvert toute la séance.
4. Utilisez seulement des noms d’équipe fictifs. N’inscrivez aucune information personnelle ou opérationnelle.
5. Chaque équipe se partage quatre rôles : un planificateur (remplit le plan), un enchérisseur (seule voix pendant l’enchère), un responsable des cartes (enregistre les gains dans l’onglet de l’équipe) et un présentateur (répond aux questions de présentation au bilan).

### Déroulement

| Étape | Instructeur | Équipes |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Configuration | Choisissez le nombre d’équipes, puis **Générer la séance**. Les réglages par défaut conviennent à la plupart des classes ; **Plus d’options** change la révélation des lots, le chronomètre et le palier d’enchère. Écrivez le code au tableau et donnez à chaque équipe son numéro. | Entrez le code de séance, votre numéro d’équipe et votre mission, puis **Commencer**. |
| 2. Pratique | **Commencer la pratique**, puis les quatre étapes avec la carte d’entraînement. Annoncez « l’équipe 1 gagne le lot de pratique ». **Ouvrir la planification**. | **Enregistrer le gain de pratique**, puis **Passer à la planification**. |
| 3. Planification | Confirmez la mission de chaque équipe dans le tableau. Quand tout est prêt : **Fermer la planification et lancer l’enchère**. | Vérifiez les minimums, notez priorités et risques et cochez **Nous avons confirmé cette mission avec l’instructeur**. Au lancement : **L’instructeur a lancé l’enchère**. |
| 4. Enchère (7 rondes × 10 lots) | Pour chaque lot : annoncez la ronde, le lot et l’identifiant de carte, **Ouvrir les offres**, cliquez sur l’équipe qui offre (chaque clic accepte l’offre suivante : prix de départ, puis le palier d’enchère choisi à la configuration, 50 000 $ par défaut), puis **Vendre à l’équipe N** ou **Pas de vente**, et **Lot suivant**. Clavier : chiffres pour les équipes, S vendre, U pas de vente, O ouvrir, R révéler, N suivant, P pause, E +30 s. | Entrez l’identifiant annoncé et **Afficher la carte**. Si l’instructeur annonce votre gain, entrez le prix et **Nous avons gagné cette carte** ; sinon **Pas à nous, lot suivant**. |
| 5. Construction | Montrez le tableau des résultats pour que les équipes vérifient. **Ouvrir les soumissions**. | Comparez vos achats aux résultats. Corrigez seulement les erreurs de saisie, puis **Nos registres concordent. Passer à l’offre**. |
| 6. Soumission | **Saisir les soumissions en privé** (ne pas projeter). Entrez le profit de chaque équipe et cochez **Soumis**. **Quitter le mode privé**, puis **Fermer les soumissions**. | Choisissez un profit (montant ou pourcentage du coût), puis **Terminé : informer l’instructeur** et dites-lui votre profit en privé. |
| 7. Bilan | Montrez les résultats : l’offre la plus faible par point de score gagne ; en cas d’égalité, l’offre la plus faible puis le score le plus élevé. Discutez des écarts et des compromis. **Fermer la salle**. | Comparez votre plan à votre véhicule. **Fermer** après l’annonce. |

Règles en bref : 2 lots gagnés au plus par équipe et par ronde ; les prix montent du palier d’enchère choisi à la configuration (50 000 $ par défaut) et valent toujours le prix de départ plus des tranches entières de 50 000 $ ; un véhicule doit atteindre tous les minimums et un score supérieur à 0 pour être admissible.

### Corrections pendant l’enchère

- Mauvais gagnant ou mauvais prix : **Corriger le résultat…** avant de fermer le lot, avec un motif.
- Lot déjà fermé : **Annuler ce résultat…** avec un motif, puis rouvrez les offres et enregistrez le bon résultat.
- Chronomètre : **Pause**, **Reprendre**, **Ajouter 30 s**. À la fin du temps, rien n’est vendu automatiquement : vous décidez.

### Sauvegarder

Exportez une sauvegarde par **Menu → Exporter une sauvegarde** après la configuration, après chaque ronde et à la fin. Chaque rôle n’exporte que ses propres données. En cas de problème, consultez le [guide de récupération](RECOVERY_GUIDE.md).
```

# Handover

Updated 2026-10-14 (America/Toronto). Specification: [MPES](MPES.md) 4.5.0. Evidence: [verification/0.6.0.0.md](verification/0.6.0.0.md) (in progress), [verification/0.5.2.0.md](verification/0.5.2.0.md), [verification/0.5.1.0.md](verification/0.5.1.0.md), [verification/0.5.0.0.md](verification/0.5.0.0.md), [verification/spike-visual.md](verification/spike-visual.md).

## 1. Version and milestone

Version 0.5.2.0 beta (four-part MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.BUILD, MPES §19.2; 1.0.0.0 only once out of beta: MPES §19.2 exit criteria, including every owner gate). M0–M4, V1, V2 (goal G1, tag `v0.5.0.0`) and G2 (owner fixes and the docs regime, tag `v0.5.1.0`, owner GO 2026-10-12) are complete. 0.5.2.0 (tag `v0.5.2.0` on `c2932eb`, owner GO 2026-10-13) is owner FIX 4 on G2: showcase zoom, framing of the full kit at every turn and height, sign controls, and phone tables as labelled cards (`docs/verification/0.5.2.0.md`). G3 (0.6.0.0, branch `g3/proxy-runtime`, draft PR #27) is in progress. The rollback is tag `v4.1.0-dev.1`.

**Plan to beta exit (MPES §17), one PR and one tag per goal:**

| Goal | Version | Content |
|---|---|---|
| G3 proxy + runtime | 0.6.0.0 | `npm run perf:ref` on the Intel UHD 770 proxy (D-16), every §14 gate, baked lighting, adaptive tiers, context-loss recovery, touchpad and panel safety |
| G4 hyper-real assets | 0.7.0.0 | vehicles, parts and cards raised towards the Codex concepts within budgets; textures and decals where they pay |
| G5 classroom | 0.8.0.0 | UX, workload, teaching aids, game feel §7.7, projector mode §7.8, fault tests |
| G6 hardening | 0.9.0.0 | manual accessibility, Windows 11 matrix, egress, security and content review, `npm run package` |
| G7 release candidate | 0.9.1.0 | freeze, three release passes (§21), beta handoff package |
| G8 beta exit | 1.0.0.0 | only when every MPES §19.2 criterion holds, owner results included |

Shared rules for every goal: `AGENTS.md`. KPIs and priority: MPES §1.4.

## 2. What works

- **Game:** all of MPES §6 for both roles, all eight phases, EN/FR, schema-3 saves and backups, private entry, degraded states. Legacy 4.1 backups import.
- **V2:** war-room HUD on every view with a projector theme; setup defaults first; bid increment chosen at setup; live lot fits 1280×720; debrief chart and questions; `dist/` not committed, `npm run check` compares two builds, CI deploys `main` to Pages for QA only.
- **G2:**
  - creator credit (owner, 2026-10-12): "Created by Shafiqur Rahman Khan, with AI assistance." in About and "created by Shafiqur Rahman Khan" on the chooser's version line (EN/FR), the README and the instructor guide, nowhere else; `LICENSE` and `library/LICENSE` read "Copyright (c) 2026 SEA Game authors", `package.json` has no author, no account handle in the game (`tests/unit/build.test.ts` "credits the creator");
  - About shows the licence and notices reflowed (`source/ui/reflow.ts`, `tests/unit/reflow.test.ts`, visual baselines at 1366×768 and 320 px);
  - the chooser shows all six vehicles as a lineup of hero stills, selected one large, keyboard and touch, EN/FR (`tests/e2e/chooser.spec.ts`, visual baselines);
  - `DecodedImages` never evicts an image on screen or a prepared one (`tests/unit/showcase.test.ts`);
  - `npm run gallery` writes the offline review page `.artifacts/review/<version>.html` (`tests/unit/gallery.test.ts`);
  - MPES has no code and names every file, script, pin, CSP directive and goal (`tests/unit/mpes.test.ts`); a Codex session given only MPES wrote a rebuild plan and its gaps were fixed (`docs/verification/0.5.1.0.md`);
  - `npm run codebase` writes `docs/CODEBASE.md`, which rebuilds every tracked file (`tests/unit/codebase.test.ts`);
  - `npm run archive:prep` (dry run; `--apply` only on the owner's cleanup request) and `RESTORE.md` (`tests/unit/archive.test.ts`);
  - `AGENTS.md` rule 21: driving Codex headless;
  - owner FIX 1: build stills at yaw 30° pitch 6° and 210° pitch 6°, chosen by `art/tools/angles.ts`; `art/blender/fit.py` fails any part inside or outboard of a tyre or not attached, and the art passes it and `overlap.py` (MOB-D rebuilt inboard, rack, troop rear kit, recovery sensors, fasteners; `docs/verification/0.5.1.0.md`);

```markdown
# Recovery guide / Guide de récupération

[English](#english) · [Français](#français)

## English

### How saving works

- The game saves automatically **in the current browser tab** after every change. Reloading the tab keeps your game.
- Closing the tab, using a private window, or moving to another device can lose that copy. A downloaded **backup file** is the portable copy: **Menu → Export backup**.
- A backup holds only your role's data. A student backup never contains other teams' work or the instructor's lot order.
- Backups are plain JSON files of at most 1.5 MB. Do not edit them: an edited file is refused.

### Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "This browser tab cannot save automatically" | The browser blocks storage (private mode or a policy). Keep playing, and export a backup after every important change. |
| The tab was closed or the device changed | Open the game in the same role, then **Menu → Import backup** and choose the latest backup. Check the summary, then **Replace with backup**. |
| Imported the wrong file | Use **Undo import** before doing anything else. |
| "The saved game in this tab could not be read" | The game started empty and kept the unreadable data. Use **Download unreadable data** to keep it, then import your latest backup. |
| The browser refuses the download | The game shows the backup text instead. Select all of it and save it in a file ending in `.json`. |
| An import is refused | The message says why: wrong role, unreadable file, other version, or too large. Nothing in the current game changed. |
| The instructor's backup was taken during an open lot | After import the lot is **paused for review**. Check the leader and price, then **Resume**. |
| A student's records differ from the instructor's | In the Build step, remove mistaken entries and add missing purchases. The instructor's results are official. |

If nothing works, the instructor's spoken announcements and the results table remain the official record: continue on paper and re-enter later.

## Français

### Fonctionnement de la sauvegarde

- Le jeu sauvegarde automatiquement **dans l’onglet du navigateur** après chaque changement. Recharger l’onglet conserve la partie.
- Fermer l’onglet, utiliser une fenêtre privée ou changer d’appareil peut faire perdre cette copie. Le **fichier de sauvegarde** téléchargé est la copie portable : **Menu → Exporter une sauvegarde**.
- Une sauvegarde ne contient que les données de votre rôle. Celle d’une équipe ne contient jamais le travail des autres équipes ni l’ordre des lots de l’instructeur.
- Les sauvegardes sont des fichiers JSON de 1,5 Mo au plus. Ne les modifiez pas : un fichier modifié est refusé.

### Situations courantes

| Situation | Que faire |
|---|---|
| « Cet onglet ne peut pas sauvegarder automatiquement » | Le navigateur bloque le stockage (mode privé ou règle). Continuez et exportez une sauvegarde après chaque changement important. |
| L’onglet a été fermé ou l’appareil a changé | Ouvrez le jeu dans le même rôle, puis **Menu → Importer une sauvegarde** et choisissez la plus récente. Vérifiez le résumé, puis **Remplacer par la sauvegarde**. |
| Mauvais fichier importé | Utilisez **Annuler l’importation** avant toute autre action. |
| « La partie sauvegardée dans cet onglet est illisible » | Le jeu a démarré à vide et a conservé les données illisibles. Utilisez **Télécharger les données illisibles**, puis importez votre dernière sauvegarde. |
| Le navigateur refuse le téléchargement | Le jeu affiche le texte de la sauvegarde. Sélectionnez-le en entier et enregistrez-le dans un fichier terminé par `.json`. |
| Une importation est refusée | Le message indique pourquoi : mauvais rôle, fichier illisible, autre version ou fichier trop volumineux. La partie en cours n’a pas changé. |
| La sauvegarde de l’instructeur a été faite pendant un lot ouvert | Après l’importation, le lot est **mis en pause pour vérification**. Vérifiez l’équipe en tête et le prix, puis **Reprendre**. |
| Les registres d’une équipe diffèrent de ceux de l’instructeur | À l’étape Construction, retirez les erreurs et ajoutez les achats manquants. Les résultats de l’instructeur font foi. |

Si rien ne fonctionne, les annonces de l’instructeur et le tableau des résultats restent le registre officiel : continuez sur papier et saisissez plus tard.
```

# Art review (owner, about 5 minutes)

**Why:** realism is your judgement (MPES §1.4, D-14). The agent has already checked the renders for clipping, floating parts, framing and exposure.

**You need:** this PC or any Windows 11 laptop, with Edge or Chrome.

1. Open the QA build: `https://shfqrkhn.github.io/SEA-Game/`, or `dist/index.html` from the handoff folder.
2. On the first screen, look at the hero vehicle. Ask yourself: does it look like a real armoured vehicle photographed in a studio?
3. Click **Student team**, join with any code the instructor screen gives you (or follow the quick-start guide), and choose any mission.
4. Watch the vehicle turn for about 10 seconds. Drag it with the mouse, and press **Pause**.
5. Record two or three purchases. Each part should appear on the vehicle, sitting on it, not floating or poking through.
6. Optional: open `.artifacts/contact/cards.jpg` (all 71 cards) and `.artifacts/contact/builds-A.jpg` (each vehicle with a full set of parts).

**Reply with one line:**

- `GO`, or
- `FIX: <what looks wrong>`, for example "FIX: tyres too shiny", or "FIX: the combat turret looks like a toy".

Rough notes are fine. The agent turns them into changes and asks for nothing else.
```

### docs/owner/instructor-review.md

Paths: `docs/owner/instructor-review.md`. SHA-256 `cb186b5ccceedb5aab30b1d3d14a07ce3996a6f714c8063f292fb9cacbffb2e7`, 2503 bytes.

```markdown
# Instructor review of the prototype (about 20 minutes)

**What this is:** a beta prototype of SEA Game, a classroom auction game about systems engineering trade-offs. It is one file, `index.html`, that runs offline in Chrome, Edge or Firefox on Windows 11. Nothing is installed and nothing is sent anywhere. Everything you see is fictional.

**What we would like from you:** your judgement as an instructor. Is it clear, is it teachable in one session, and does it make students think about trade-offs? Look and polish are still being worked on.

## Open it

1. Open `index.html` (double-click it) or the web link you were sent.
2. Choose **English** or **Français**. In a bright room, choose **Projector theme**.

## Try it on your own (one computer, two tabs)

The two tabs do not connect: in class the instructor announces each result aloud and the students record it on their own screen. You play both sides.

1. First tab: choose **Instructor**, keep the defaults and click **Generate session**. Note the session code.
2. Second tab (open the same file again): choose **Student team**, enter the session code, team 1 and any mission, then **Start**.
3. Instructor tab: **Start practice** and do the four practice steps. Student tab: **Record practice win**, then **Continue to planning**.
4. Instructor tab: **Open planning**, then **Close planning and start the auction**. Student tab: tick **We confirmed this mission with the instructor**, then **The instructor started the auction**.
5. A few lots. Instructor tab: **Open bidding**, click team 1, **Sell to Team 1**, **Next lot**. Student tab: enter the card ID shown, **Show card**, enter the price and **We won this card**; the part appears on the vehicle.
6. Optional: `CLASSROOM_QUICK_START.md` walks through a full session (setup, practice, planning, 7 auction rounds, build, sealed bid, debrief).

## Questions for you

1. Could you run a full class with it after reading the quick-start guide once? What would stop you?
2. Do students get enough guidance at each step without the instructor explaining everything?
3. Does it teach what it should: trade-offs between capability, cost and mission requirements?
4. Is anything confusing, too small to read on a projector, or too slow?
5. What one change would make it most useful in your classroom?

**Reply** with rough notes, a few lines are fine, or screenshots of anything that looks wrong.

SEA Game is created by Shafiqur Rahman Khan, with AI assistance. Prototype version 0.5.2.0.
```

**CI failure found and fixed (run 38089382489, the first CI run of the 3D tests):** on the GitHub runner's software WebGL, every Playwright action took 5–17 s once the model was showing, and 7 showcase tests timed out. The stage drew at 30 fps whatever a frame cost, and drew synchronously on every drag or key event. The fix, MPES §10.3 and `source/showcase/pace.ts`: a drawn frame is timed by the gap to the next animation frame, the next draw waits at least twice that (1 s at most), and every redraw goes through that one paced frame. Locally the failure did not reproduce, even with SwiftShader pinned to one core, so the runner is the oracle for this fix.

**Second CI run red (run 38097185474, commit `043fba9`): two root causes, read from the downloaded traces** (`gh run download 38097185474 -D .artifacts/ci-38097185474`):

1. *Firefox, Node 24, three showcase tests* (`showcase.spec.ts` lines 37, 82, 155): the trace console reads "Failed to create WebGL context: AllowWebgl2:false restricts context creation on this system". Firefox refuses WebGL on that GPU-less runner, so the page correctly showed the stills and the 3D tests waited for a mode that could not come. Fix: `playwright.config.ts` launches Firefox with `webgl.force-enabled`, giving it a software context as Chromium has. No oracle or timeout changed; the stills fallback keeps its own tests.
2. *Perf, Node 22* (stills, no WebGL): showcase update 245 ms (budget 100), angle change 108 ms (50), turntable step 122 ms (50). Each update built new `<img>` elements, so every unchanged layer was decoded again, and the warmed turntable frames were separate images the page never used. Decoding runs off the main thread, so 4× (and even 12×) CPU throttling here did not reproduce it (12×: 132 / 38 / 24 ms). Fix (MPES 4.1.1 §10.3 "Still decoding"): `DecodedImages` in `source/showcase/showcase.ts` keeps decoded images and reuses them (24 at most, never one on screen); when the page is idle the other angle, the turntable and the frames either side are decoded ahead, and `#showcase[data-prepared]` reports it. Node 24 perf was skipped because its browser projects failed.

| Pool unit tests: one decode per source, least recently used dropped, on-screen never dropped | `npx vitest run tests/unit/showcase.test.ts` | PASS, 6 tests |

**Third CI run red (run 38106258905, commit `aca9d45`, docs only): an intermittent turntable spike on Node 24.** Perf, Node 24: turntable step 665 ms (budget 50); update 67 ms, angle change 25 ms, 3D ready 2,602 ms, all within budget. Node 22 passed (turntable step 19 ms). The trace (`gh run download 38106258905 -D .artifacts/ci-38106258905`) shows the first two steps after the turntable opened taking about 410 and 720 ms, and the next four fast. Root cause: the frames either side were prepared in `requestIdleCallback` (500 ms timeout), and on the busy runner no idle time came within the 300 ms pause, so the first steps decoded their frames on demand. Locally idle time comes at once, so the fault showed only on CI; the test now reproduces it by making idle callbacks wait for their timeout. Fix (MPES 4.1.2 §10.3): preparation starts as soon as the shown view has decoded, never on idle; the images exist at once, so a step never creates one; an angle view also prepares the turntable frames either side of the entry frame; while turning, the frames ahead in the direction of travel come first. No budget, pause or wait changed. Version 5.0.0-dev.1.

Cards and heroes are shown whole, so they keep the old trim and are byte-identical. The previous renders are in `_archive/recycle/2026-10-11/content-renders-pre-trim/`. No budget, pause or wait changed. The version stays 0.5.0.0 (not yet tagged, rule 17).

## Owner FIX 1: still angles and physical fit

The owner asked for the best still angles and then spotted dampers modelled outside the tyres; they asked that sibling issues be found and fixed too.

- Angles: `art/tools/angles.ts` renders the packed model from a yaw and pitch grid, framed as a build still, and counts each part's visible pixels with only the base in front. Yaw 30° pitch 6° (front) with yaw 210° pitch 6° (rear) hides the fewest parts across both stills and frames the vehicle larger than the former 38°/10° and 218°/12°.
- Fit: `art/blender/fit.py` builds every vehicle with one part at a time and reports geometry inside a tyre or outboard of its sidewall beyond the hub, and any object more than 15 mm from the hull or from an attached object of its part. Its first run found the MOB-D dampers and a set of siblings: floating fasteners and straps (CAP-A, B, D, F front and bow panels; ACC-D and ACC-G cases, jerrycans and bands), wheel lugs and studs off their faces, FP, COM and SA parts on air, rack feet beside the hull, and the recovery hull's rear sensor seats over the roof chamfer.
- Fixes: MOB-D rebuilt inboard (hub, ventilated brake, upright, double wishbones, canted coil-over); its card shows the station from inboard. Every fastener and strap now sits on its face. The roof rack's front bracket bolts to the flat roof outboard of the turret-mount flange; its rear bracket stands on a pad on the roof chamfer, behind the pioneer tools and clear of the module deck; both are braced from the sponson. The recovery rear sensors stand on the flat roof between cabin and crane.
- Troop carrier: its rear ramp is lowered in the stills, so rear-slot parts were checked against the doorway. ACC-A's legs stand off the door pillars with the ropes over them and the towing eye trails behind the head, below the deck's radio masts; ACC-B's drawbar splits to a receiver on each pillar.
- Codex review of this change (`.artifacts/codex/review-fit/review.md`, five findings): (1) `fit.py` treated a batched object as one piece, so one attached piece could carry floating ones: confirmed, it now splits every mesh into connected pieces, which found three more floaters per hull (FP-C roof bolts off the sloping roof, an FP-F louvre above the rear door, PRO-C end-bracket bolts off the light plate), all fixed; (2) MOB-D's inboard brake had no spindle to the hub: added; (3) the trailer lunette lies flat: rejected, a lunette drops over a vertical pintle, so its ring is horizontal by design; (4) the tyre test used vertices only: confirmed, it now samples surfaces (no new finding); (5) the rotor wear face stood 3.5 mm off the rotor: fixed; the calliper straddling the rotor edge is how a calliper fits, not a clash.
- Results: `fit.py` all vehicles, all parts: PASS, 0 findings. `overlap.py`: PASS, 0 intersecting pairs (its first run after the rack change found 67 pairs between the rack feet and the modules, and 2 between ACC-A's towing eye and the COM-D and COM-E masts; all fixed). Close-ups were inspected for MOB-D, the troop carrier's rear, the rack and the recovery sensors.

### Overhang check and its sweep

A final Codex review (`.artifacts/codex/review-final/`) found the SA-G hub foot half over the recovery hull's roof chamfer (accepted) and asked for the ramp towing eye to face aft (rejected: on the ramp the eye's loop already trails aft). `fit.py` gained a check for that class: a downward face seated on a level surface must not have more than 10% of its sole more than 40 mm over a slope or an edge, unless the part's own bracing (a knee, a strut) stands within 300 mm beneath it; running gear on the base's wheels is exempt. Its first run found the same fault on other parts, all fixed:

| COM-A to COM-G | Rear trays' shoes cantilevered over the rear face | A knee under each shoe to its end, on the hull's rear face (2 mm off it, clear of the troop compartment); the outer trays inboard of the roof edge, the recovery left tray 40 mm further in to clear the crane ram |

A second Codex review (GPT-6.1 Sol, medium; `.artifacts/codex/review-final/review2.md`, `disposition2.md`) found five more faults, all accepted and fixed: FP-D's ammunition box into its camera on the vehicle (camera to the other side, as on the card); a COM-E whip floating beside the radio (back on the lid); SA-F and SA-G front corner feet 25 mm over the chamfer (45 mm inboard); and two loopholes in the overhang check (a sole split into faces is now judged as one sole; only solid bracing touching the sole holds it, not a loose surface lower down), proved on a synthetic case.

## Owner FIX 3: a part read as the end of a barrel

The owner, on the combat vehicle's hero still in the chooser (2026-10-12): the heavy gun's barrel "looks obscured by the other part and looks like a part of the gun barrel". The crew cupola (SA-A) stood on a cantilever over the glacis, where the eye carries the barrel on.

- Check: `art/blender/sightline.py` builds every vehicle and part at the stills' full detail and frames the hero and both build stills exactly as `render.py` does. For every barrel (axis from the bored barrel, muzzle at the far face of a muzzle brake) it fails any part from another slot, at any depth, that comes within 1% of the frame width (13 px in a build still, 16 px in a hero) of the muzzle or of the barrel's line 4% of the frame width beyond it. Projected triangles of negligible area count by their edges only. `--selftest` covers a crossing triangle, one clear above, and edge-on triangles off and on the line.
- First round (depth-limited rule: only parts nearer the camera than the muzzle): it failed the owner's still (FP-C against SA-A, 11.2 px) and one sibling hero (mine clearer, FP-D against SA-E). Moving the optics heads to the right of the roof cleared both. The re-rendered combat hero still misled, though: the cupola, now behind the muzzle, still stood at the barrel's end. A part behind a muzzle reads as the barrel carried on just as one in front does, so the rule now judges every depth (MPES §10.2, §10.5 lessons).
- Third round (hull fittings): a look at the re-rendered combat hero found the driver's mirror, a hull fitting the check did not judge, standing at the cannon's muzzle like a brake. The check now judges the hull's small fittings (no larger than 0.8 m) like parts; on the heroes it found that pair (0.0 px) and no other. The mirrors on every vehicle now stand 0.22 m lower; heroes PASS. The base is a holdout and shadow catcher in every layer, so every build layer, hero and turntable was re-rendered.
- Cause shared by the siblings: the optics heads (SA-A cupola, SA-C camera, SA-E thermal sight) stood low on the roof front, in the band of the stills where the main guns' and the auxiliary gun's barrels end; the sensor mast (FP-C) stood just behind the roof front, in the same band.
- Placements tried, each run through `overlap.py`, `fit.py` and `sightline.py`:
  - optics 1.2 m further back: hit the powerpack covers of MOB-A and MOB-F (overlap 40 pairs) and overhung the roof (fit 18);
  - sensor mast on the left: overlapped the auxiliary guns FP-D and FP-E;
  - first raised head: the crossplate and riser offsets left the sight parts floating up to 543 mm off their support (fit), fixed before any render;
  - sensor mast 1.35 m back on the recovery vehicle: overlapped its turret kits SA-B and SA-D, so the recovery vehicle keeps the forward spot (`_mast_x`).
- Fix: the optics head stands high on a steep strut on the right of the roof, short of the glacis, out of the auxiliary gun's line of fire and above every gun's line in the stills; the sensor mast stands 1.35 m back from the roof front (0.7 m on the recovery vehicle).
- Results (any depth): hero stills clean (0 failing pairs; 2 before the fix, and the combat mirror in the third round); build stills 574 pairs under the any-depth rule with hull fittings (251 front, 323 rear; 4 of them hull fittings), all recorded. `fit.py`: PASS, 0 findings. `overlap.py`: PASS, 0 pairs. `tris.py`: PASS, 0 layers over budget.
- Build stills are not yet clean: any of a team's combinations may be shown, and parts remodelled in G4 cannot all move now. The 574 remaining pairs are recorded with their clearance in `art/blender/sightline-baseline.json`; a run fails on any pair new to the record or more than 0.5 px closer than recorded, filtered runs included, and `--write-baseline` refuses to add a pair, so the record only shrinks. MPES §17 makes an empty record a G4 exit criterion.
- Imagery: the optics and mast layers and the four heroes with optics were re-rendered first and checked by eye (which found the mirror). The showcase model was re-exported and re-packed. After the mirror moved, every build layer, hero and turntable was re-rendered (`--only hero,turntable,build`); cards do not show the hull.

Owner FIX 4 (2026-10-12): "Vehicle showcase needs zoom in, out function. It needs to fit the fully kitted out model in the view. On mobile, not all dropdown menu are showing. ## Items and their tests

| Item | What | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Zoom in and out by buttons, 1.25 per press, 0.4 to 1.6 times the fitted distance; the wheel never zooms (page scroll kept) | `tests/unit/frame.test.ts`; `tests/e2e/showcase.spec.ts` "3D showcase at 1280/360 px" | PASS |
| 2 | The vehicle as fitted, however fully kitted out, framed within 92% of the frame at every turn and every drag height; refitted on a purchase or a window change; a purchase keeps the player's turn and zoom | `tests/unit/frame.test.ts` (long, tall, off-centre kits; wide, square, tall windows; every 5° turn; heights 0.6 to 1.45 rad); `tests/e2e/showcase.spec.ts` buys ACC-B, COM-E, ACC-C and SA-D on the troop carrier and turns it fully at 1280 and 360 px | PASS |
| 3 | Sign controls: ‖ or ▷ (pause, resume), ↺, ↻, −, +; each named for assistive technology and in its tooltip, at least 44 px, inside the window at 360 px; EN and FR names | `tests/e2e/showcase.spec.ts`; axe in the existing showcase test | PASS |
| 4 | Phone tables: below 40 rem each row is a card and every cell is labelled with its column header (`labelCells`), so no column is cut off; the desktop header is unchanged; swept over all eight table kinds | `tests/e2e/mobile.spec.ts` (320 and 360 px, EN and FR, planning with every section open and the tracker after a purchase; 1280 px header) | PASS |
| 5 | Pause stops the model where it is, at once (CI found the turn coasting on after pause); every control (pause, turn, zoom) and every refit reports the view at once, not on the next paced draw | `tests/e2e/showcase.spec.ts` "paused means still" (the reported turn unchanged for 600 ms) and the zoom limit read straight after the last press, at 1280 and 360 px, in Chromium, Firefox and Edge | PASS |

Root cause of item 4: the "dropdown menus" were the collapsible sections of the planning and tracker views; their tables were wider than a phone and their right-hand columns were clipped behind a sideways scroll that nothing showed.

Root cause of item 5: CI run 38341255504 failed the turn check at 1280 px (the view still moving 0.023 rad between readings after a pause). The orbit controls ease every movement: switching off the automatic turn leaves the remaining eased turn to run out, which on a slow software renderer takes many seconds. A new check (the reported turn must not change for 600 ms after pause) failed before the fix (0.463 then 0.387; 0.653 then 0.577) and passes after it: pause applies one update without easing, keeping the camera where it is. The check then failed in Edge at 360 px by 0.002 to 0.003 rad, and the zoom read 0.8, its zoomed-in value, after 12 Zoom out presses: the stage reported its view only on its next paced draw, and not at all while scrolled off screen, so the reading lagged the camera. Now every control reports at once. A further trap: these runs had loaded a `dist/index.html` built before the change, so item 6 makes that impossible.

Framing notes: framing every part in the catalogue (−7.3 to 5.6 m long, 5.6 m tall) left a bare vehicle at about half the frame, so the stage frames the vehicle as fitted. The camera distance is fitted per drag height (nine heights, interpolated), because a single distance for the highest view leaves the low views loose.

# Verification record: 0.6.0.0 beta (G3 proxy and runtime) — in progress

Branch `g3/proxy-runtime`, from `main` at the 0.5.2.0 release. Specification: MPES 4.4.3 until this goal's changelog row. Environment: Windows 11 Enterprise, Node 24.20.0, Playwright browsers from `npm run browsers`.

## First item: CI `showcaseUpdateMaxMs` 109, 162, 168 > 100 ms (verify (22))

Root causes found so far, each with its fix:

| Cause | Evidence | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Every command rendered the view twice: once through the controller's subscription and again in the view | `tests/e2e/render.spec.ts` counted two rebuilds per command before the fix | A command, saved field or status message rebuilds once (`source/ui/view.ts`) |
| The perf project recorded a trace, whose DOM snapshots ran inside the timed window | Click-to-paint fell with tracing off, same build | Trace off for the perf project (`playwright.config.ts`) |
| The frame pacer counted page work after a draw as drawing cost, so a purchase waited for the next paced frame | Phase probe: purchase handled at about 30 ms, drawn one to two paced frames later | A change the player asked for draws in the next animation frame (urgent invalidate, `source/showcase/model.ts`) |
| Attaching the 3D stage forced a layout | Profile of the attach | The attach only starts the loop |
| The first draw compiled every shader in one task: 0.25 to 2.7 s, once 35.8 s, on a software renderer | Long-task timings of the first draw | The stage compiles in the background before it is shown (stills stay up), the bare vehicle first, then every part |
| The shadow map was drawn again in every frame | Renderer inspection | Shadows are baked: drawn again only when the vehicle or its parts change |
| A software renderer draws a full-resolution frame in about 50 ms, more than a 30 fps frame | Draw gap 104 ms at tier 0, 84 ms at tier 1 | Adaptive tiers (full, 0.75, 0.5 of the pixel ratio), one step down whenever the cheapest of the last eight draws exceeds a 30 fps frame (`source/showcase/pace.ts`, `tests/unit/pace.test.ts`) |

### Red run 38571533524 (verify (22), head d0763a7): 3D update p95 331.6 ms > 100

Diagnosed before any rerun. The stills update was within budget (p95 78.8 ms), so the first item's stills cause is fixed in CI; the 3D update was not. Every CI tracker opens in a fresh context, so the stage started at full quality each time and needed eight slow draws per step down: the tiers never reached the timed purchases (data-tier 2 only at the end, about 170 ms a draw on CI's software renderer).

Draw-cost probe (`.artifacts/tmp/drawcost/`, three.js r0.186.1, SwiftShader, recovery vehicle with three parts: 40 draw calls, 69k triangles), one draw in ms:

| Setting | 0.75 ratio | 4x CPU throttle |
|---|---|---|
| As shipped (multisampled canvas, shadow, environment, tone mapping) | 62 | 62 (ratio 1) |
| No multisampling | 22 | 24 (ratio 1), 16.5 (0.75), 11-12 (0.5) |
| No shadow | 56 | |
| No environment | 26-30 | 6.7 (0.5, no multisampling) |
| No tone mapping | 57-61 | |
| Lambert instead of standard material | 22 | |
| Ratio 1.5 | 113 (54 without multisampling) | |

Multisampling made a draw about 3.6 times dearer; the cost is GPU-process work, so CPU throttling barely changes it. Fixes:

| Cause | Fix | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Multisampling was fixed in the canvas, so no tier could drop it | Canvas without multisampling; tiers 0 and 1 draw into a multisampled half-float target resolved to the canvas with tone mapping (three.js OutputPass); tiers 2 and 3 draw straight at 0.75 and 0.5 (`source/showcase/pace.ts` TIERS) | `tests/unit/pace.test.ts` |
| A fresh page started at full quality | Before the stage is shown, one timed draw per tier at the stage's size picks the first tier within a 30 fps frame (startTier); a tier differing only in resolution is skipped when its pixel share cannot bring the cost in budget | `tests/unit/pace.test.ts` starting tier |
| A paced turning draw could start just before a click and delay its answer | The player's input anywhere else on the page holds paced draws for one second; the purchase's own draw still goes in the next frame | `tests/unit/pace.test.ts` hold |
| A lost graphics context (driver reset, GPU switch, sleep) left the stage blank | Drawing stops on loss; on restore the environment and shadow are made again and the current parts drawn | `tests/e2e/showcase.spec.ts` context-loss test (all engines) |

The measurement protocol was also corrected (tests/perf/): every timing runs from the trusted input event to after the next paint, with the nearest-rank p95 of at least 30 samples (`tests/unit/perf-measure.test.ts`); the 3D update is timed to the frame that draws the purchased part, the 3D ready time from the tracker's opening click to the first drawn model (MPES §14), each tracker in a fresh context.

Local timings on 2026-10-14 are void: another job held the processor at about 80% (AGENTS.md: a busy PC voids a measurement). CI is the gate.

## Lane: caching (merged from `g3/caching`)

- CI: a newer push to the same pull request cancels the superseded run (pushes to main and tags never cancel); npm downloads cached by `actions/setup-node` keyed on `package-lock.json`; the Playwright browser folder cached per OS, engine set and exact `@playwright/test` version, with `npx playwright install` kept. Matrix, commands, budgets, timeouts and the Pages deploy unchanged; `actions/cache` pinned by commit (v4.2.4).
- Render encoder (`art/tools/encode-renders.ts`): each master trimmed and encoded once into `.artifacts/cache/encode/`, keyed on the master's bytes, every output setting and the sharp and libvips versions; a damaged entry is re-encoded; writes are atomic; `--no-cache` bypasses it. Evidence: `tests/unit/encode-cache.test.ts`; a two-image smoke run gave byte-identical manifests with, without and from the cache.

`npm run perf:ref`, `playwright.perf-ref.config.ts`, `tests/perf-ref/`. Its protocol is written into MPES §14 in this goal; Codex's findings on both lanes are dispositioned below.

# Legibility practices: lighting, angle, shading, pedagogy, UI

Research fragment, 2026-10-12. Sources were found by web search; weakly sourced points are marked (unverified). Project facts used: `art/blender/sea/scene.py` already uses AgX (Medium High Contrast look), exposure -0.25, key/fill/rim area lights plus reflection cards.

## 1. Offline product rendering (Blender stills)

- Three-point roles: key shapes, fill lifts shadows, back/rim separates from background. Key:fill about 2:1 (1.5:1 light, up to 4:1 dramatic); fill about 50% of key or the image goes flat; raise rim until a crisp edge shows without clipping. Photo/video sources, so starting points only. https://vidpros.com/three-point-lighting-setup/ ; https://riverside.com/blog/3-point-lighting
- AgX vs Filmic: both are view transforms only; AgX holds highlights better, but may shift hue (an indigo shifted about 11 degrees) and wash out some scenes. Render a swatch of the part palette in both and compare against reference. https://blenderartists.org/t/agx-changes-hue/1527123.md ; https://cgcookie.com/community/17899-filmic-vs-agx
- Exploded views: separate along true assembly directions, stagger, keep part count per view modest (vendor figure 30-50), thicker outline on the main body and thinner on small fasteners, stable callout numbers. https://3d.irpr.agency/glossary/exploded-view/ ; https://racklify.com/encyclopedia/how-to-create-exploded-views-for-assembly-instructions-and-maintenance/ ; https://grail.cs.washington.edu/projects/exview3D/exview3D-SIG08.pdf (Li et al., SIGGRAPH Asia 2008, explosion layout).
- Not found by search (general industry practice, unverified): 3/4 view with 50-85 mm equivalent focal length, material breakup via roughness/metal variation, cavity/edge wear, inverted-hull or Freestyle outlines.

Recommended numbers (starting points to tune):
- Key:fill 2.5:1 to 3:1 (projector washout compresses shadows, so do not go darker than 4:1). Rim about 0.6-1.0 x key, placed behind-opposite the key.
- Adjacent parts: aim for at least 12 L* (CIELAB) or 1.3:1 relative-luminance ratio between touching parts in the final tonemapped image, otherwise separate by hue, roughness (matte vs glossy) or a dark panel-gap line.
- Camera: 3/4 (yaw 30-45, pitch 15-25), 60-85 mm equivalent to avoid wide-angle distortion; per-part hero cards pitched so the part's most distinctive silhouette faces the camera.
- Dark panel-gap/outline: 2-3 px at 1280x720 (Freestyle or inverted hull), tone about 25% of the part's value, not black. Thin 1 px lines vanish on projectors.
- AO: keep a strong contact AO (strength about 1.0) but floor shadows at about 10% luminance so parts do not merge into black.

Automatable check (ID-mask render): render a flat Cryptomatte/object-index pass at the same camera. Per part compute mean L* inside mask and in a 6 px ring of each neighbouring mask. FAIL if |dL*| < 8 AND hue difference < 15 degrees AND roughness class equal. Edge contrast: Sobel gradient mean along each mask boundary must exceed a threshold (start 0.04 in display-referred 0-1). Also check in grayscale and with a deuteranopia simulation (same test). Runs offline from a mask pass; no Blender change to the product.

## 2. Real-time three.js on iGPU

- OutlinePass is a screen-space post pass costing per pixel; `downSampleRatio` defaults to 2 and is the main lever; it has no anti-aliasing with a multisampled composer target (needs FXAA/SMAA after). Official doc: https://threejs.org/docs/pages/OutlinePass.html ; AA thread: https://discourse.threejs.org/tag/antialiasing/302.md ; alternative: https://discourse.threejs.org/t/outlinepass-with-effectcomposer-or-outlineeffect/19790
- Tone mapping runs once at output (OutputPass last); per-frame cost is small. No iGPU benchmark was found, so measure. https://discourse.threejs.org/tag/tone-mapping/609
- No authoritative source found for SSAO cost; general knowledge (unverified): SSAO is a multi-sample full-screen pass, several times the cost of a vertex-colour AO bake. Keep baked AO.

Recommendations:
- Use `renderer.toneMapping = NeutralToneMapping` (keeps part albedo hues faithful, no hue skew) or AgX if highlights clip; test both on the swatch. Exposure 0.9-1.1.
- Hemisphere (sky/ground contrast about 1.6:1) + one directional key + cheap Fresnel rim in `onBeforeCompile` (about 4 ALU ops per pixel, no extra pass). Rim colour a cool tint at 0.25-0.35 strength.
- Hover/selection: avoid a full OutlinePass at 30 fps on UHD 770. Prefer (a) inverted-hull mesh for the single selected part (one extra draw of that mesh, scale 1.02, backface, flat colour of at least 3:1 against the background), or (b) emissive/Fresnel boost on the selected material. Use OutlinePass only if measured under budget with downSampleRatio 2-4.
- Check: frame-time test on the UHD 770 proxy with selection on/off; delta must stay within MPES §14 budget. Screenshot test: selected part's boundary ring vs neighbours contrast at least 3:1 (same ID-mask idea, via a flat-colour debug render of the scene).

## 3. Pedagogy and multimedia learning

- Mayer principles (Cambridge Handbook): coherence (remove extraneous material; 23/23 tests, median d 0.86), signalling (cues pointing at essentials; 24/28, d 0.41), spatial contiguity (labels next to the thing they name), temporal contiguity, redundancy (do not repeat the same text in several channels). https://resolve-he.cambridge.org/core/books/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/CD5B7AE1279A9AB81F8EEBB53DBEC86E ; https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10639-022-11283-2
- Pre-attentive attributes (Ware): colour, orientation, size, motion pop out, but pop-out weakens as distractors grow, so one highlight per still. https://faculty.cc.gatech.edu/~john.stasko/4460/Notes/perception.pdf ; https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2601.20080
- Figure-ground: contrast, closure and relative size make the figure; the chosen part should be the figure and the rest recede. https://www.coreldraw.com/en/blog/gestalt-principles/figure-ground/ ; https://oreilly.com/library/view/universal-principles-of/9781592535873/xhtml/ch42.html

Recommendations:
- Chosen/new part in the still: render it full-colour with the rim and outline, other parts at about 75% saturation and 85% value (desaturate, do not dim to dark), plus a leader-line callout with its name placed within one callout-length of the part (spatial contiguity). Maximum 1 highlighted part and 3-5 callouts per still (coherence, signalling).
- No decorative text or duplicate labels (redundancy): the caption beside the image carries the effect, the callout carries only the name.
- Check: count highlighted parts per still (metadata) is exactly 1; callout anchor-to-part distance below 15% of image width; callout text not overlapping other labels (bounding-box test).

## 4. UI/UX/GUI

- WCAG 2.2: text 4.5:1 (large 3:1); UI components and graphics 3:1 (1.4.11); focus not fully obscured (2.4.11, AA); focus appearance (2.4.13, AAA): indicator at least 2 CSS px perimeter and 3:1 against unfocused state and neighbours. Colour never the sole signal (1.4.1). https://tetralogical.com/blog/2023/10/05/whats-new-wcag-2.2 ; https://adrianroselli.com/2023/10/2-4-11-adversarial-conformance.html ; https://w3c.github.io/wcag/understanding/use-of-color.html
- Projectors: ambient light lifts blacks, so dark-tone differences collapse; sources are AV vendors (weigh accordingly). https://blog.draperinc.com/2026/09/what-is-the-best-projection-screen-material-for-a-classroom-with-the-lights-on/ ; https://www.ravepubs.com/?p=16743
- Colour-blind safe: Okabe-Ito eight-colour set (e.g. #E69F00, #56B4E9, #009E73, #F0E442, #0072B2, #D55E00, #CC79A7). https://plotstyle.readthedocs.io/en/stable/guides/palettes.html

Recommendations: target text at least 7:1 and non-text at least 4.5:1 (projector margin); minimum stroke 2 px (3 px for focus ring, offset 2 px, dual-tone light+dark so it works on any background); no body text below 16 px at 1280x720; pair every colour code with an icon/shape/letter; use Okabe-Ito for team and category colours and verify via grayscale.
Checks: axe-core in Playwright (`color-contrast`, `focus-visible` style), a custom computed-style contrast test at 7:1 for text and 4.5:1 for borders, a Tab-through test asserting the focused element's bounding box is inside the viewport and not covered (`elementFromPoint` at its centre), and a CVD-simulation screenshot test (deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia matrices) re-running the ID/neighbour palette distinctness check.

## Prioritised top 10

1. ID-mask neighbour test (Section 1) as a new check next to `art/blender/sightline.py`; fails on near-equal adjacent parts. Biggest return, no runtime cost.
2. Highlight the chosen/new part in each still (full colour + outline, others at 75% saturation) via `art/blender/sea/scene.py` layer/material override.
3. One callout per still, within spatial contiguity, rendered in the HTML gallery/UI layer.
4. Raise rim and add dark panel-gap lines (2-3 px) in `art/blender/sea/materials.py`; rim light 0.6-1.0 x key in `scene.py`.
5. Material breakup: roughness and metal variation between neighbouring parts (`materials.py`), edge/cavity darkening by vertex colour.
6. Camera: 3/4, 60-85 mm, per-part pitch override in `scene.py`; confirm against the existing "best still angles" sweep.
7. Real-time: selection via inverted hull or Fresnel boost, not OutlinePass; Neutral or AgX tone mapping chosen from a swatch test (three.js showcase code; see docs/CODEBASE.md).
8. UI contrast margins: 7:1 text, 4.5:1 non-text, 3 px dual-tone focus ring (MPES §7 tokens).
9. Okabe-Ito team/category colours plus a shape or letter, with a CVD screenshot check.
10. Playwright axe + Tab-through focus-obscured test added to the e2e suite (`tests/e2e/`).
```

# Source fidelity: the original course game vs this rebuild

Recorded 2026-10-10 from owner-supplied material placed in `_archive/SEA-Contents/` (git-ignored and deleted after release, so the findings that matter are kept here). Those files are evidence, not requirements; [MPES](../MPES.md) governs.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SE--Systems-Engineering-Awareness--v1.3.1.md` | Distillation of the original course and its card game (§18 to §20): vehicle specifications, scoring, auction structure, Design Options Report, presentation questions, and what the source does not specify. |
| `SE--Card-Game-MPES--v0.15.0.md` | An earlier draft specification for a networked multiplayer version (Cloudflare Worker, rooms, up to 60 learners). Superseded by this project's offline single-file design (MPES §2, D-01). |
| `SE--Awareness-Instructor-Master--v3.0.0-local.html`, `SE--Awareness-Student-Companion--v3.0.0-local.html`, `SE--Candidate-Index.md` | Earlier local app candidates using the same ruleset (`STANDARD`) and deck (`synthetic-v1`), with deck and balance approval recorded as open. |

## Matches (no change needed)

- **Missions and mandatory minimums:** all six vehicles and every minimum in `content/missions.json` equal the source (§18.11), including Recovery ≥ 3 ways and Mine Clearing ≥ 3 ways.
- **Scoring:** `source/domain/missions.ts` equals the source formulas exactly, including whole increments (Combat mobility per 10 km/h, RECCE and Command Post communications per 25 km).
- **Award:** compliance first, then the lowest bid price (cost + profit) per point (§18.9, §18.10). The source leaves a compliant zero-score design undefined (§18.17); MPES decides it is not eligible (score must be above 0).
- **Auction shape:** per round, one lot in each of seven categories plus three SE process lots; at most two wins per team per round; printed cost is the starting bid (§18.8). The source does not specify increments, timing, ties or unsold cards (§18.16); MPES decides them.
- **Cost:** the amount actually paid at auction, never the printed price (§18.9).

## Differences and gaps (for the owner)

1. **Deck values.** The source deck is lost (§18.15); `synthetic-v1` was balanced against the source minimums. Its magnitudes differ from the source's Design Options Report (§18.5): mobility parts give +50 to +90 km/h (source: propulsion around 160 km/h on a light hull); protection parts +3 to +5 (source: scale 1 to 10); start prices $150K to $700K (source examples up to about $1.1M; planning budget around $6.5M). Communications (+25 to +125 km) and SA (1 to 4 ways per system) match. Changing the deck changes balance, the oracle and the fixtures; it needs an owner decision (G-CONTENT).
2. **Presentation questions (§18.18): added.** The source asks each team to explain compliance, priorities, trade-offs, profit, cost per point, its three biggest risks and the purpose of one purchased SE process, and says a digital version should keep them or an equivalent debrief. Both debriefs now show them (`presentationQuestions` in `source/ui/components.ts`).
3. **Design Options Report (§18.5): covered.** The source gives teams a qualitative market report because players never see the deck in advance. The student planning view already has a category guide listing every `synthetic-v1` card with its effects and start price, which is more precise than the report.
4. **Team roles (§18.7): added.** The quick-start guide names the planner, bidder, card tracker and presenter.
```
