```markdown
# V1 visual spike: evidence for the owner's GO/NO-GO (MPES 3.0.0 §17)

Date: 2026-10-10. Machine: Windows 11, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti (16 GB), Node 24, Playwright 1.63.0 (Chromium, Firefox, Edge). Status: **PROTOTYPE**, awaiting the owner's decision.

## What the spike proves

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Can the agent author an original, fictional, photoreal-style vehicle and parts by script? | Yes, with limits. The RECOVERY vehicle and parts CAP-B, COM-E and ACC-F are built entirely by `art/blender/` scripts in Blender 5.2.2 LTS: procedural geometry and materials with edge wear, crevice dust and road dust; studio lighting; Cycles on the GPU. The look is a polished game asset. It is not yet the concept images (see "Quality ceiling"). |
| Do pre-rendered part layers stack correctly on the vehicle? | Yes. Each part renders from the build camera with the base vehicle as a shadow catcher. The hull hides the part where it is in front, the part casts shadows on the hull, and stacking base and parts in order gives the composed build (front and rear angles checked). |
| Does it fit in one file and run on weak laptops? | Yes, with a wide margin (numbers below). |
| Does the HUD work with the real game? | Yes, behind `?hud=1`: the chooser hero, instructor live lot and student tracker, with the showcase following recorded purchases (`tests/e2e/hud.spec.ts`). |

## Format: AVIF vs WebP (`node art/tools/encode-renders.ts measure`)

| Format, quality | Kind | Files | Average bytes | Average PSNR (dB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AVIF 55 | card | 3 | 6,408 | 47.71 |
| AVIF 55 | build-layer | 6 | 3,980 | 58.6 |
| AVIF 55 | build-base | 2 | 15,287 | 47.69 |
| AVIF 55 | hero | 1 | 24,319 | 47.27 |
| AVIF 55 | turntable | 24 | 14,494 | 45.65 |
| AVIF 65 | card | 3 | 7,590 | 49.39 |
| AVIF 65 | build-layer | 6 | 4,734 | 60.03 |
| AVIF 65 | build-base | 2 | 18,733 | 49.27 |
| AVIF 65 | hero | 1 | 30,008 | 48.93 |
| AVIF 65 | turntable | 24 | 17,661 | 47.36 |
| WEBP 85 | card | 3 | 19,998 | 48.45 |
| WEBP 85 | build-layer | 6 | 23,389 | 64.65 |
| WEBP 85 | build-base | 2 | 62,048 | 47.85 |
| WEBP 85 | hero | 1 | 94,994 | 46.7 |
| WEBP 85 | turntable | 24 | 50,560 | 45.91 |
| WEBP 92 | card | 3 | 22,796 | 51.54 |
| WEBP 92 | build-layer | 6 | 24,609 | 67.16 |
| WEBP 92 | build-base | 2 | 70,267 | 50.61 |
| WEBP 92 | hero | 1 | 109,630 | 50.43 |
| WEBP 92 | turntable | 24 | 58,038 | 48.38 |

PSNR compares each encoded image with its 16-bit master, both flattened onto the HUD panel colour. Above about 45 dB the difference is not visible.

Decision: **AVIF, quality 65, 4:4:4**. It is 2.6–4.9× smaller than WebP at quality 85, depending on subject kind, at equal or better quality. Chrome, Edge and Firefox on Windows 11 all decode it.

## Sizes: performance over looks (owner, 2026-10-10)

The hero is 1600×900, the build angles 1280×720, the turntable 24 × 960×540 and the card renders 512×512 (art/README.md). These are enough pixels for the panels they fill and no more. Compared with a 1920×1080 / 1280×720 / 768² variant measured earlier the same day, the spike set fell from 748 KB to 543 KB, and the chooser became faster (below).

The chooser always shows the embedded hero still, so no WebGL runs on the first screen. Background: one CI run on a GPU-less runner measured the chooser at 2,121 ms while the WebGL hero was starting; three earlier runs measured 90–125 ms. The pre-rendered hero removes that risk. Everything stays embedded in the single HTML file; nothing is fetched.

## Size projection for all 77 subjects

| Item | Count | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Vehicle set (hero, turntable 24 frames, 2 build bases) | 6 | 2.9 MB |
| Card renders | 71 | 0.5 MB |
| Part layers (70 parts × 6 vehicles × 2 angles, trimmed) | 840 | 4.0 MB |
| Total images | | 7.5 MB |
| With 20% margin | | 9.0 MB |
| **HTML file** (base64 + about 1.2 MB of code, styles, notices) | | **13.1 MB** of the 40 MB target and 50 MB limit |

## Performance (`node art/tools/measure-spike.ts`, median of 3 runs)

| Profile | File | Bytes | Chooser interactive (ms) | Student start (ms) | Showcase update (ms) | Turntable scrub, worst (ms) | JS heap (MB) | Decoded images shown (MB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reference (4x CPU) | built | 1,548,001 | 128 | 269 | 32 | 8 | 10 | 2 |
| reference (4x CPU) | stress40 | 42,442,685 | 753 | 811 | 31 | 6 | 48 | 2 |
| reference, GPU disabled | built | 1,548,001 | 135 | 271 | 30 | 7 | 10 | 2 |
| reference, GPU disabled | stress40 | 42,442,685 | 767 | 824 | 31 | 5 | 48 | 2 |

Budgets (MPES §10.3, §14): chooser ≤ 2,000 ms; student start ≤ 3,000 ms; showcase update ≤ 100 ms; turntable change ≤ 50 ms; decoded images ≤ 250 MB. All PASS on both files and both profiles.

Reference profile: Chromium with 4× CPU throttling (MPES §14). "GPU disabled" forces software compositing, the stand-in for GPU-less machines. The stress file replicates the spike renders until it reaches the 40 MB target, about three times the projected production file. The first parse of the whole render table costs about 100 ms at 4× throttling (once, when the showcase first opens).

## Accessibility

axe (WCAG 2.2 A/AA rules) passes on the HUD student tracker and the HUD instructor auction view (`hud.spec.ts`). HUD contrast:
- body text `#e3ece6` on `#0b100e`: about 15:1;
- muted text `#a3b8ad` on panel `#121a17`: about 8:1;
- focus ring: amber `#ffd166`, 3 px.

The showcase has `role="img"` with a build summary, a text list of installed parts, keyboard radio buttons and a slider. There is no autoplay.

## Screenshots (local, `.artifacts/screenshots/spike/`)

`chooser.png`, `instructor-live-lot.png`, `student-tracker.png`, `student-tracker-preview.png`, `showcase-front.png`, `showcase-rear.png`.

## Quality ceiling and what V2 would improve

The spike is a scripted, procedural model. Its strengths are consistency, originality and fast iteration (a preview renders in about 3 s, the whole spike set in a few minutes). Compared with the concept images it still lacks:
- sculpted organic detail (tyre sidewall lettering, cast surfaces, welded seams);
- decals and stencils;
- richer cab interiors seen through the glass;
- a varied environment.

V2 would add stencils, panel lines, rivet and bolt patterns, mud splatter and interior detail through the same pipeline. Each change is reviewed on Pages.

## Residual risks

- No measurement on a physical integrated-graphics laptop; 4× throttling is the stand-in.
- Art quality is judged by the owner, not by a test.
```

```markdown
# Lessons learned

Each entry: what happened, the rule it produced, and the check that now enforces it. Newest first. Examples come from SEA Game (a classroom auction game with photoreal vehicle renders and a real-time 3D showcase, one offline HTML file).

## 2026-10-14 · An unchanged attribute that restyled the page; a restore that was not one

- **What happened:** a purchase's 3D update ran over budget on CI. Splitting its timing into phases (input to handled, to draw start, the draw, to paint) and profiling one purchase showed the cause: every command wrote the page's `lang` attribute, unchanged. Writing an attribute on the document root restyles the whole page, even with the same value; with the focused button just replaced, it forced a full style and layout inside the command and slowed the next one. On the same run, Firefox on a software renderer announced a restored WebGL context while it was still lost, then restored it later without any event.
- **Rule:** write to the document root only what changed. Split a slow timing into its phases before guessing at a fix. Trust an object's own state over the events that report it: ignore a "restored" event while the context still says lost, and while lost, check the state now and then and act on a silent return.
- **Check (as built in SEA Game):** a helper writes the language and title only when they differ; the performance scenario reports the 3D update's phases beside the gated total; the context-loss browser test covers an early announcement (nothing may draw) and a silent restore (the next purchase must still draw).

## 2026-10-13 · Green branch, red main

- **What happened:** after two green CI runs, a small docs-only commit was added and the pull request merged straight away. The generated codebase document embeds every doc, so it went stale; CI on `main` failed and the Pages deploy was skipped, leaving the old site live.
- **Rule:** every commit, docs-only included, regenerates what is generated from it and runs the fast tests; merge only the head whose own CI is green. Let the host enforce it: require the CI checks on the main branch, administrators included.
- **Check (as built in SEA Game):** the codebase test fails any stale generated document; branch protection on `main` requires both CI checks on the up-to-date head, administrators included (set with the owner's permission).

## 2026-10-13 · Paused, yet still turning; fixed, yet still failing

- **What happened:** pausing a 3D turntable stopped its automatic turn, but the orbit controls' easing carried the turn on, for seconds on a slow software renderer; only CI's slow machine showed it. The fix then seemed not to work: the test read the view from an attribute updated only on the next paced draw (and never while the stage was off screen), and ran against a build made before the fix.
- **Rule:** a pause, and every control, takes effect at once and reports its new state at once; a test reads current state, not a value cached for drawing; refuse to test a build older than its source.
- **Check (as built in SEA Game):** the end-to-end test pauses and requires the reported turn to stay unchanged for 600 ms, and reads the zoom straight after the last of 12 presses; a Playwright global setup renders the build from source and refuses to start unless the built file is that build.

## 2026-10-12 · Framed for one view, cut off at the others

- **What happened:** a 3D showcase framed the vehicle for its opening view; once fully kitted (a trailer behind, a blade in front, a tall mast), parts left the frame as it turned, and there was no zoom. Framing every part in the catalogue instead shrank a bare vehicle to a speck. On a phone, wide tables inside collapsible sections lost their right-hand columns, unseen because tests opened only the first screen.
- **Rule:** frame what is shown, at every view the user can reach (each turn, each drag height, each window shape), with a margin; zoom by buttons with limits, not the wheel, so the page still scrolls. Below a phone breakpoint, show each table row as a card whose cells carry their column headers. Test the worst case (the full kit) and every section opened at phone width.
- **Check (as built in SEA Game):** a unit test projects the bounds of long, tall and off-centre kits at every 5° turn and every drag height in wide, square and tall windows (inside the frame, and tight); an end-to-end test buys the most extreme parts, turns the model fully at 1280 and 360 px, and reads the drawn extent and zoom; another opens every section at 360 px in both languages and fails any cell outside its table or without a label.

## 2026-10-12 · Two ways to publish, one stale site

- **What happened:** the built game was uploaded by hand to the repository root, and Pages (serving from the branch) published it. Minutes later CI's own Pages job, still running on the commit before the merge, deployed a build of the older source over it. The tracked copy also broke the checks that every tracked file is reproducible.
- **Rule:** one deployer. Set the Pages source to the CI workflow, never commit a build, and publish only what passed the checks. After each release, compare the live file's hash with the local build.
- **Check:** a unit test fails on any tracked page carrying a built payload; the release checklist compares the Pages SHA-256 with the build.

## 2026-10-12 · A part read as the end of a gun barrel

- **What happened:** in a still, a roof sight stood where the eye carried a barrel on, so it looked like part of the barrel. A first check judged only parts in front of the muzzle; the fixed still still misled, because a part *behind* a barrel's end reads the same way. Then a hull mirror (not a "part", so not judged) did the same in another still.
- **Rule:** in a picture, the eye continues lines (good continuation). Nothing may touch the end of a line-like component or its extension, at any depth, whatever kind of object it is.
- **Check (as built in SEA Game):** project each weapon's muzzle and every part from another slot, plus small base fittings (no larger than 0.8 m), into the exact camera of each still; fail any within 1% of the frame width of the muzzle or of its extension 4% beyond. Proposed: extend to every line-like component (poles, aerials, cables). See `practices/asset-checks.md`.

## 2026-10-12 · A count ceiling hides regressions

- **What happened:** known failures were held "at or below 97 and 182". Fixing one and adding another kept the count, so a new defect could pass; filtered runs skipped the ceiling entirely; rewriting the record could let each entry creep 0.5 px worse.
- **Rule:** record known exceptions *by identity with their measured value*; fail any new entry or any worse value, in every run; rewriting keeps the better of old and new; the record only shrinks, with a dated goal of empty.
- **Check:** the record file is versioned, and the check refuses to add to it.

## 2026-10-12 · A check that does not see what the viewer sees

- **What happened:** the first check built the models at real-time detail while the stills render at full detail, and took the muzzle at the bored barrel instead of the brake beyond it; a degenerate (edge-on) triangle produced false hits.
- **Rule:** a visual check must use the same geometry, camera, resolution and framing as the image it judges. Give geometric checks a self-test with the edge cases (crossing, clear, edge-on off the line, edge-on on the line).
- **Check:** a self-test of those cases runs automatically before every check run.

## 2026-10-12 · Fix one, find all

- **What happened:** the owner reported one still; the same cause was in other vehicles, other angles and other slot types.
- **Rule:** for any reported defect, find the class, sweep every instance (all variants, angles, languages, themes), fix them all and add a check that would have caught the first one.
- **Check:** the evidence record lists the sweep and the new check.

## 2026-10-12 · Moving one thing breaks another

- **What happened:** relocating a sight 1.2 m back hit an engine cover (40 overlaps) and overhung the roof (18 fit failures); a mast moved left hit a gun; a raised head floated 543 mm off its support.
- **Rule:** every geometry change runs the whole check suite (overlap, fit, budgets, sightline) on the whole fleet before any render. Renders are the slowest step; checks are cheap.

## 2026-10-12 · The base is in every picture

- **What happened:** lowering a mirror on the base meant every layered still had to be re-rendered, because the base is a holdout and shadow catcher in each layer.
- **Rule:** know which outputs depend on which sources before changing a shared component; estimate re-render cost first and batch base changes.

## 2026-10-12 · Ignore tool folders

- **What happened:** the linter scanned agents' worktrees in `.claude/` and reported 241 errors that were not in the project.
- **Rule:** exclude agent and tool folders (`.claude/`, `.artifacts/`, `_archive/`) from lint, tests and typecheck from day one.

## 2026-10-11 · Timeouts are evidence, not knobs

- **What happened:** tests timed out when other work loaded the PC; once, test scratch had piled up and slowed a test 16-fold.
- **Rule:** never raise a timeout or budget to pass. Find the cause (here: scratch not cleaned up), fix it, add a check (scratch is removed after each run), and record the evidence of any one-off with the date.
```

```markdown
# Reusable library

Practices, lessons, starter files and a catalogue of candidate free and open-source building blocks (audit the exact version before shipping), drawn from SEA Game and meant for every other project. Copy the whole `library/` folder into a new project (or read it in place); nothing in it depends on SEA Game's code.

MIT licence: see `LICENSE` in this folder, which travels with it. Third-party material is only referenced here, with its own licence (see `catalogue.md`).

## Contents

| Path | What it gives you |
|---|---|
| `LESSONS.md` | Dated lessons learned, each with what went wrong, the rule it produced and how to check it. Read first. |
| `catalogue.md` | Verified FOSS components, themes, icons, fonts, charts, 3D runtime, render assets, media tools, test and accessibility tools, with licences and when to use each. |
| `practices/delivery-loop.md` | The goal loop: failing check first, sibling sweep, reviews, docs, two green CI runs, visual GO/FIX, tag, handoff. |
| `practices/visual-legibility.md` | Making every component readable in stills, 3D and on a projector: geometry, light, value, camera, signalling, measured checks. |
| `practices/asset-checks.md` | Automated checks for generated 3D assets and renders: fit, overlap, budgets, sightlines; how to write them so they cannot be gamed. |
| `practices/classroom-apps.md` | Teaching apps: pedagogy, workload, projector, offline single file, bilingual, accessibility. |
| `practices/performance.md` | Budgets for old integrated-GPU laptops and how to measure them on a proxy. |
| `practices/agents.md` | Working with AI agents: headless Codex reviews, parallel lanes, evidence rules, one heavy job at a time. |
| `practices/docs.md` | Documents that let anyone rebuild and maintain the project: a code-free specification, a lossless code file, a handover. |
| `LICENSE` | The MIT licence for this library. |
| `ui/tokens.css` | Two tested themes (dark "war-room" and light "projector") as CSS custom properties, with contrast notes. |

## How to use it in a new project

1. Copy `library/` in. Read `LESSONS.md`, then the practice files that apply.
2. Pick building blocks from `catalogue.md`; record each one you ship in the project's `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
3. Start the stylesheet from `ui/tokens.css` and re-check contrast for any colour you change.
4. When the project teaches you something new, add a dated entry to `LESSONS.md` and fold the rule into the practice file it belongs to. Keep the library generic: project details only as marked examples.

## Library version

0.1.0 (2026-10-12): first cut from SEA Game 0.5.1.0, corrected after an independent review (licences, reduced motion, agent trust boundaries, accessibility, colour management, GPU resource ownership, flakiness).
```

```markdown
# Reusable building blocks catalogue

Date: 2026-10-12

## How to use this catalogue

Pick a section, scan the table, then check "Fit" before adding anything. Entries are candidates, not audited dependencies: before shipping, audit the exact version you ship, including bundled components and release artefacts (npm metadata alone does not settle these), and keep the licence evidence. Each entry says how it was checked. **(V)** = licence and version read on the official page or repository on 2026-10-12. **(unverified)** = not confirmed in this pass; it comes from earlier knowledge, so re-check the official licence file before shipping. Licences outside MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, CC0, OFL-1.1, public domain or Unlicense are marked **FLAG**. Anything shipped goes into the project's THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (see the last section). Sizes are rough and drift between releases: measure in your own build.


## Registry check (2026-10-12)

Licence and latest version as published on the npm registry (`npm view <package> license version`), run on 2026-10-12. Where a table below says "(unverified)" for one of these packages, this check settles its licence. Re-run the command before shipping; a licence can change between versions.

## 1. Design tokens, colour and themes

| Name | Purpose | URL | Licence | Checked | Fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Leonardo (Adobe) | Generates colour scales that hit a target contrast ratio | https://github.com/adobe/leonardo | Apache-2.0 (V) | 2026-10-12; package `@adobe/leonardo-contrast-colors` | Use at build time to make light, dark and high-contrast scales. Embeddable. |
| Radix Colors | 12-step accessible scales, light and dark pairs | https://www.radix-ui.com/colors | MIT (unverified) | not checked | Ready-made dark/light pairs. Steps 11-12 are text colours. Copy only the values you use. |
| Open Props | CSS custom-property tokens (sizes, easings, shadows) | https://open-props.style | MIT (unverified) | not checked | Cherry-pick files. The whole set is larger than a single-file app wants. |
| USWDS design tokens | US gov tokens and components | https://github.com/uswds/uswds | Mostly CC0 / public domain with some MIT parts (unverified) | not checked | The colour "grade" idea (grade gap gives contrast) is useful. Check the notice for fonts and third-party parts. |
| GOV.UK Frontend | Accessible components, focus style, spacing | https://github.com/alphagov/govuk-frontend | MIT (unverified). Crown and logo assets are NOT open: **FLAG**, never use them. | not checked | Good HTML patterns. Strip branding. |
| Pico CSS | Classless CSS with light/dark | https://github.com/picocss/pico | MIT (unverified) | not checked | Fast prototypes. Prefer your own tokens for shipped apps (size). |
| Tailwind palette | Widely used colour names | https://tailwindcss.com | MIT (unverified) | not checked | Values may be copied with the notice. Not tuned for contrast; test every pair. |

Theme notes. `ui/tokens.css` ships two sets: dark for screens and a light "projector" set (high contrast, 7:1 text, no subtle greys); add a separate high-contrast set only if testing shows the need, and honour `forced-colors`. ---

## Licence rules for shipping

1. **Can be embedded in a single HTML file:** MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC, Zlib, CC0, public domain, Unlicense, and OFL-1.1 fonts. Keep the copyright and licence text for each.
2. **Attribution.** MIT, BSD, ISC and Apache-2.0 need the notice kept. Apache-2.0 also needs the NOTICE file if the project has one. CC-BY needs credit, a licence link and a note of changes. The W3C licence needs its notice kept and changes marked.
3. **Copyleft.** GPL and AGPL: do not embed in a shipped app unless the whole app can be GPL. LGPL: do not statically embed. MPL-2.0 (axe-core): file-level; anyone shipping MPL files, changed or not, must keep the notices and tell recipients how to get the source form, and changed MPL files stay MPL. Library policy (stricter than the licence): keep them as build and test tools only. Keep these as build and test tools only.
4. **Fonts under OFL-1.1.** May be embedded and subset. Keep the licence and copyright. Do not sell the font alone. Respect Reserved Font Names on modified versions.
5. **CC0 assets (Poly Haven, ambientCG).** No obligation. Record the source in the notices anyway.
6. **Not FOSS or restricted (flagged above):** Web Awesome Pro, Quixel/Fab, BlenderKit Royalty Free items, GOV.UK crown and brand assets, CAST UDL text, book content. Do not embed.
7. **Rendered output.** Images you render from CC0 or your own models belong to you. Renders that use restricted assets need that asset's licence checked first.
8. **Every shipped third-party item goes into the project's THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:** name, version, URL, SPDX licence id, copyright line, and where it appears in the build. Remove the entry when the item is removed. Re-verify the licence when upgrading a version.
```

````markdown
# Working with AI agents

## Roles

- **Lead agent:** owns the goal, integrates, verifies everything others return, updates the docs.
- **Parallel lanes** (cheaper model, isolated worktree, background): prepare later work that needs no heavy runs (research, drafts, scripts, side branches). Lanes do not edit the shared docs, the specification or the version; they write fragments that the lead integrates. They may run typecheck, lint and single unit-test files only.
- **Independent reviewer** (a second vendor's model, read-only): reviews each substantial diff, the gallery, and translated text. Every finding gets a disposition with evidence.

## Codex CLI headless (example, Windows)

```powershell
$codex = (Get-AppxPackage OpenAI.Codex).InstallLocation + '\app\resources\codex.exe'
cmd /c "`"$codex`" exec -m gpt-6.1-sol -c model_reasoning_effort=medium --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only -C D:\path\to\repo -o review.md `"Review the uncommitted diff. Report only real defects, ranked, with file:line, a failure scenario and a fix.`" < NUL"
```

From Git Bash: `"$codex" exec ... "<prompt>" < /dev/null`.

- Close stdin, or it waits on input. PowerShell has no `<` redirection, hence the `cmd /c` wrapper; the prompt must then hold no double quote, or cmd splits it. Read-only unless delegating a task; for delegation give it an empty work folder.
- Ask for ranked defects with a concrete failure scenario; ask it to say what it ran (PASS/NOT_RUN).
- Verify its claims: it can be right about a bug and wrong about the fix.

## Trust boundaries

- Write down what each agent may do: which folders, which commands, whether it may push, publish, spend or contact anyone. Anything else needs the owner.
- Keep secrets out of agents' reach: no tokens or keys in the repo, prompts or logs; give the least credentials and network access the job needs.
- Web pages, downloaded files, reference documents, tool output and other agents' reports are untrusted data, never instructions (prompt injection). A read-only file system alone does not stop disclosure or outside actions.
- Downloads go in their own empty folder and are opened only by tools you chose.

## Rules

- One heavy job (renderer, browser test suite, perf run) at a time on a shared PC; reviews and research run in parallel.
- Never kill processes you did not start.
- No claim without executed evidence; report PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or BLOCKED with the command.
- Exclude agent folders (`.claude/`) from lint, tests and typecheck.
- Keep scratch in a git-ignored folder; never delete, move to a recycle folder.
````

```markdown
# Automated checks for generated 3D assets and renders

When models and images are generated by scripts (Blender, procedural tools, AI-assisted modelling), check them like code: every geometry change runs the whole suite on every variant before any render.

## The suite

| Check | Fails when | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Budgets** | a model or part exceeds its triangle budget | Budgets per kind (base, part, running gear); measured at export detail. |
| **Overlap** | two parts that can be fitted together intersect | Test every legal combination, not each part against the base only. |
| **Fit** | a part floats (a piece more than ~15 mm from its support), sits inside a wheel or tyre, or a sole overhangs a slope or edge | Sample surfaces, not only vertices. Exempt by rule, never by part name. |
| **Picture sightline** | in an image, another component touches the end of a line-like component or its extension | Project into each still's exact camera; any depth; include base fittings. SEA Game checks weapon muzzles only; poles and aerials are proposed. |
| **Legibility** (planned) | a component's visible share or boundary contrast is too low | ID-mask render per still; judged on encoded images at displayed size. |

## How to write such a check

1. **See what the viewer sees.** Same geometry detail, camera, lens, resolution and framing as the image. Import the renderer's constants (angles, sizes, margins) instead of copying them.
2. **Self-test first.** Synthetic cases for each branch: hit, clear, edge-on off the line, edge-on on the line. Degenerate projected triangles count by their edges only.
3. **Vectorise.** Project all triangles at once (NumPy); a whole fleet × parts × shots check should run in minutes, so it runs on every change.
4. **Fail per item, never on an average.** Print one line per failing pair with its measured value and the limit.
5. **Known exceptions by identity.** When some failures must wait (for a later art pass), record each `subject shot item other → value` in a versioned JSON file. Fail anything new, anything worse than recorded (allow float noise, e.g. 0.5 px), in every run, filtered or not. A filtered run checks every pair a selected item is in. Rewriting keeps the better of old and new values, refuses to add entries, and runs only on the whole set. Give the record a dated target of empty.
6. **Exit codes.** 0 pass, 1 fail; run headless (`blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P check.py -- args`).
7. **One heavy job at a time** on a shared machine; chain checks, then renders.

## Pipeline order

model change → budgets, overlap, fit, sightline (whole set) → look at a quick render of the changed views → full render of only the dependent outputs (know what depends on what: a base change touches every layer that holds it out) → encode → export and pack the real-time model → app tests → visual gallery.

## Render notes

- Render layered stills (base plus each part) so an app can composite any combination; the base acts as holdout and shadow catcher in each part layer.
- Encode stills to AVIF (or WebP), trimmed, with a manifest of id, frame, offset, size, draw order and SHA-256.
- Export real-time models as glTF binary with vertex-colour AO, no image textures where budgets are tight; pack and hash them. Vertex-colour "AO" multiplies the base colour under all light, while glTF's occlusion texture darkens only indirect light, so the two look different: tune in the target viewer.
- Colour textures in sRGB, data maps (normal, roughness, metalness, occlusion) as non-colour; render and export in the same colour pipeline.
```

### library/practices/classroom-apps.md

Paths: `library/practices/classroom-apps.md`. SHA-256 `2814b82c8614bd7b71683220e0bc159dab17fb68e4a8cb869b1088b2aab43e24`, 3784 bytes.

```markdown
# Classroom and teaching apps

## Priorities when goals conflict

Teaching and reliability first; then learnability and instructor workload; then performance and "works in any classroom" (floors never traded away); then realism; then maintainability. Every effect must teach or confirm something.

## Design

- **Safe defaults, progressive disclosure.** The first screen works with the defaults; options sit behind "More options". The "grandma test": someone who has never seen it finishes a round without help.
- **The instructor's screen is the record.** If apps do not connect (offline), the instructor announces results aloud and students record them; build in a correction path ("Void this result" with a reason).
- **Practice round first** with a training item, then the real thing.
- **Workload:** keyboard shortcuts for every repeated instructor action; one primary action per step; nothing that needs a second person.
- **Debrief built in:** results, a chart, and discussion questions so the session ends in reflection, not a score.

## Pedagogy

- Multimedia principles (Mayer): signalling, coherence (no decoration that competes), spatial contiguity (labels by what they describe), segmenting (one step at a time), pre-training (practice round).
- Keep cognitive load low: plain words over codes ("+2 km/h Mobility", not "MOB +2"); effects written the same way everywhere.
- Retrieval and comparison: students plan, commit, then compare plan with outcome.
- State measurable learning objectives first and check learners against them (a debrief question or short quiz per objective), not only whether they enjoyed it.
- Retrieval throughout, with corrective feedback and spaced revisits, not only at the end.
- Universal Design for Learning: multiple means of representation (text, picture, 3D), action (mouse, keyboard, touch) and engagement.

## Delivery

- Choose the delivery form from your classrooms' constraints. Example (SEA Game): one offline HTML file, no installation, no network, no account; runs from a USB stick or email attachment, with a size budget (≤ 50 MB).
- Every language you serve from the start (example: English and French) with parity tests: every string in both, no truncation, no overflow at 320 px.
- WCAG 2.2 AA in full, not only contrast: semantic HTML and landmarks; text alternatives and captions; logical focus order, focus restored after dialogs and never hidden by sticky bars (2.4.11); status messages announced (4.1.3); errors identified with a way to recover (3.3.1, 3.3.3); page and passage language set (3.1.1, 3.1.2); text resizable to 200% and robust to text-spacing changes (1.4.4, 1.4.12); a single-pointer alternative to dragging (2.5.7); targets at least 24 by 24 CSS px or spaced, with the listed exceptions (2.5.8); pause for anything that moves (2.2.2); screen-reader names from the same source as the visible text. Turning off interaction-triggered animation (2.3.3) is AAA: do it anyway. Automated tools catch only part of this; test by hand with a keyboard and at least one screen reader.
- Two themes: dark for screens, light "projector" for bright rooms; a 7:1 text target on the projector theme.
- Fit 1280×720 without scrolling for the live views; test at 1366×768 and 320 px reflow.

## Usability testing

- Task-based tests with real or proxy users: give a task ("run one auction round"), watch without helping, note where they stall or err, fix, test again. About five people find most problems in a round.
- Run a scripted rehearsal before the first class.

## Review by an instructor

Send the file with a one-page guide: how to open it, a solo walk-through (two tabs), and five questions (could you run it, is guidance enough, does it teach the trade-off, what is confusing, the one change you would make).
```

```markdown
# Delivery loop

A loop that ships one goal at a time with evidence, so any person or agent can pick up where the last one stopped.

## Per goal

1. **Branch from the last release** (SEA Game: from main at the last tag). One goal, one branch, one PR, one tag. Bump the version once by the scale of the change and add a changelog row.
2. **Each exit criterion and each open item: failing check first, then green.** Write the test or check that fails on the defect, make the minimal change, see it pass. Never weaken a test, a budget or a timeout to get green; find the cause.
3. **Sweep siblings.** For every defect, name its class and search every instance: every variant, angle, language, theme, viewport, role. Fix all; add a check that would have caught the first (see `../LESSONS.md`).
4. **Independent review of each substantial diff.** A second model or person reviews it read-only. Record every finding with a disposition (fixed, superseded, rejected with evidence) in the version's verification record.
5. **Docs in the same change.** Handover, readme, specification, verification record, guides. A status claim is withdrawn as soon as evidence contradicts it.
6. **Verify locally, then CI.** The local verify command is authoritative. Require two consecutive green CI runs on the same commit (re-run for the second): a cheap gate that catches some flakiness, not proof of its absence. Prevent flakiness at the source: isolated tests with their own data, controlled clocks and seeds, waits on conditions (never fixed sleeps), traces kept on failure, and any pass-on-retry investigated as a defect.
7. **Visual check by the owner.** Build a self-contained screenshot gallery of every view, before and after, with plain notes on what changed. Ask one question: GO or FIX. On FIX, apply every item and its siblings and repeat 5–7.
8. **Close.** Merge commit, tag, push the tag, confirm the deployed file's SHA-256 equals a local build of the tag, set the handover's next action.

## Evidence rules

- Report every check as PASS, FAIL, NOT_RUN or BLOCKED, with the exact command. No claim without executed evidence.
- Things only a person can do are BLOCKED-owner with a one-page script in `docs/owner/`, never a vague request.
- Keep budgets, timeouts and oracles in one place, with the reason for each number.

## Versioning

Example (SEA Game): four parts, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.BUILD`; beta starts at 0.5.0.0; 1.0.0.0 only when every written beta-exit criterion has evidence, never because a milestone was reached.

## Hand-off

The final deliverable is a local package that does not depend on any hosting: a git bundle with tags, the built file with SHA256SUMS, content and art sources, render masters, docs and a RESTORE guide. A fresh restore must reproduce the build hash.

## Safety

- Never delete: move unwanted files to `_archive/recycle/<date>/`. Scratch lives in a git-ignored `.artifacts/`.
- Stage named files only; never stage local governance files or build outputs.
- Do not overwrite anyone's uncommitted work.
```

### library/practices/docs.md

```markdown
# Documents that keep a project alive

Write so that another person or agent can resume development, operations and maintenance from the files alone.

| Document | Purpose | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `AGENTS.md` | Working rules, short and numbered. | Read first by every agent. |
| `docs/HANDOVER.md` | State: done, not done, in progress, next action for agent and owner. | Updated at milestones, failures and before stopping. |
| Specification (e.g. `docs/MPES.md`) | Everything needed for a clean-room rebuild: behaviour, rules, budgets, files, goals with exit criteria, changelog. | No code at all, prose and tables only; a test checks it names every tracked file and script. |
| Code file (e.g. `docs/CODEBASE.md`) | Every tracked file, text verbatim, binaries by hash; generated, never hand-edited. | A test rebuilds the tree from it and fails when stale. |
| `docs/verification/<version>.md` | Evidence for each version: every check with command and result, review findings and dispositions. | Text only, never links to CI runs that will disappear. |
| `docs/owner/*.md` | One-page scripts for anything only a person can do. | Plain words, a few steps, the reply expected. |
| `README.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `LICENSE` | Entry point, third-party licences, copyright. | Kept current in the same change. If the owner prefers not to be named, write "Copyright (c) <year> <project> authors" in `LICENSE`, leave the package author empty, and add a test that fails on the owner's name in any tracked file or build output. Keep a copyright line: MIT needs one, and its text already disclaims warranty and liability. |

## Habits

- Same change, same PR: code, specification, handover, verification, guides.
- Withdraw a status claim as soon as evidence contradicts it.
- Test that the specification is code-free and complete; a model given only the specification should be able to plan the rebuild (try it and fix the gaps).
- Plain English: short sentences, active voice, no jargon a newcomer would need to look up.
```

### library/practices/performance.md

```markdown
# Performance on ordinary laptops

## Reference machine

Example (SEA Game): assume the lowest common denominator of business laptops up to three years old: Core i3/i5 U-series or Ryzen 5 U, Intel UHD/Iris Xe or Radeon Vega 7, 8 GB single-channel memory, 1366×768 or 1080p at 125–150%, a touchpad, Edge, battery saver on.

## Proxy when you have no such laptop

Chromium and Edge forced onto an Intel integrated GPU (`--use-angle=d3d11 --enable-gpu --ignore-gpu-blocklist --force_low_power_gpu`) with 4× CPU throttling. Fail the run unless the WebGL renderer string names the expected integrated GPU, so a run never silently measures the discrete GPU. Residual risk: a proxy is not the real machine (thermal limits, drivers, memory bandwidth and battery saver differ); confirm on one real low-end laptop when you can, and say in the evidence that a proxy was used.

## Budgets (example project; keep yours in one table with reasons)

| Metric | Budget |
|---|---|
| Single HTML file | ≤ 50 MB hard, ≤ 40 MB target; embedded imagery ≤ 40 MB |
| Time to interactive | ≤ 2 s first screen; ≤ 3 s with maximum saved state |
| Click to result | ≤ 100 ms p95; INP ≤ 200 ms; no long task over 200 ms after load |
| 3D | ready ≤ 3 s; ≤ 30 fps cap; p95 frame ≤ 33 ms, GPU ≤ 16 ms; ≤ half the machine |
| Memory | ≤ 400 MB after a full session, no growth across cycles |
| Idle | ≤ 3% CPU over 60 s |

## Techniques

- Pace drawing: render only when something changes or while turning, capped at 30 fps; stop when hidden.
- Parse only the model shown; decode images lazily and never evict one on screen.
- Small procedural environment map (e.g. 64 px PMREM) instead of HDR files; one shadow map; extra lights unshadowed.
- Bake ambient occlusion into vertex colours; avoid image textures where size is tight.
- Fall back to layered stills when WebGL 2 is missing or the context is lost; recover from context loss, trusting `isContextLost()` over the events (a browser may announce a restore early, or restore silently).
- Never write the document root's attributes (`lang`, `data-theme`, title) unless the value changed: even an unchanged write restyles the whole page.
- Split a slow interaction timing into phases (handled, draw start, draw, paint) before fixing; profile one instance on an unminified build.
- Own every GPU resource: dispose of geometries, materials, textures and render targets when a view closes (three.js does not free them for you); give shared resources a clear owner or a reference count; cancel loads no longer wanted; test repeated open and close for memory growth.
- Count GPU memory, not file size: a 200 KB AVIF of 2048 px still takes about 16 MB decoded (more with mipmaps).
- Measure on a quiet machine. Timing failures under load are evidence to investigate, never a reason to raise budgets.
```

### library/practices/visual-legibility.md

```markdown
# Visual legibility

Every component must read as a separate object at a glance: in a still, in real-time 3D, and on a classroom projector. Numbers marked *start* are starting settings to calibrate on your own renders.

## 1. Geometry first

- **Good continuation:** the eye carries lines on. Nothing may touch the end of a barrel, pole, cable or edge, or its extension, in front of it or behind it. Check it in the camera of each image (`asset-checks.md`).
- Parts keep visible gaps and their own silhouettes. Physical checks (overlap, fit) keep them apart in 3D; the picture check keeps them apart in 2D.
- Small fittings of the base (mirrors, lamps, aerials) count as much as add-on parts.

## 2. Light relative to the camera

- Three-point lighting placed relative to the camera, not the world, so each view gets the same roles: key 45° camera-left and 35° up; fill 35° camera-right, 20° up; rim (back light) about 145° and 25° up.
- Key:fill about 2.5–3:1 (*start*). Projectors lift shadows, so do not go darker than 4:1.
- Rim light draws outlines against the background and against parts behind. In real-time 3D, parent a weak, unshadowed directional light to the camera (about half the key, slightly cool) so the outline holds as the model turns. Cost: one extra light per fragment, no extra shadow pass.
- Keep the rig fixed across all layers of one angle; scale card rigs to the subject's size. Fewer than 1% clipped pixels on non-emissive parts.
- Colour management: light and shade in linear space; colour textures and final output in sRGB; normal, roughness, metalness and AO maps as non-colour data; check that the exported model looks the same in the target viewer as in the renderer.
- Tone mapping: AgX or ACES; compare exposures on identical subjects; check hue shifts on the palette.

## 3. Value and material

- Neighbouring parts differ in value (about 20–30% linear luminance, *start*; at least 1.3:1 or 12 L* between touching parts in the final image) or in material, not in hue alone.
- Roughness separates materials: paint 0.60–0.70, bare metal 0.40–0.50, glass and optics 0.08–0.15 (*start*).
- Ambient occlusion marks joints without black holes: remap to `0.4 + 0.6 × AO` (*start*). Dust and grime no more than about a third of a cavity's colour.
- Edge wear only on real convex edges, 2–6 mm wide.

## 4. Camera

- Three-quarter views: yaw 25–45° (or 205–225° for the rear), pitch 6–18°. Moderate telephoto (55–85 mm full-frame equivalent) to limit distortion. No depth of field in teaching images.
- Frame on everything the image may show (the base plus every possible attachment), with a 6% margin and the aspect ratio considered.
- Choose angles by sweeping candidates and scoring the *worst-visible* component, not only the total.

## 5. Signalling (multimedia learning)

- One highlighted subject per view: the figure; everything else is ground.
- Labels stand next to what they describe (spatial contiguity); nothing decorative competes (coherence); highlight with shape, position and value, never colour alone.
- Group with proximity: about 8 px within a group, 16 px between groups; explicit signs (+/−) and words for gains and penalties.

## 6. Projector and classroom

- Projectors wash out light colours and lift blacks. Aim for 7:1 text contrast (4.5:1 is the floor), essential non-text cues at least 3:1 and 2 px wide.
- No thin, low-contrast lines carry meaning. Pair every colour code with an icon, letter or shape.
- Offer a light "projector" theme beside the dark one; test both.

## 7. Measured, not judged by eye alone

- In force (example project): picture sightline check, overlap, fit, triangle budgets, WCAG contrast in end-to-end tests.
- Next: render a per-component ID mask for each still; fail a component whose visible area falls below a share of its own (start 35% in at least one angle), or whose boundary contrast with neighbours is under 1.5:1 along 70% of its edge; judge the encoded images at displayed sizes, in greyscale and under colour-vision simulation. Simulate projector washout (start: 15% white veil) on the interface.

## Sources

Three-point lighting (Blender manual), PBR reflection (pbr-book.org), tone mapping (Blender colour management), Gestalt proximity (NN/g), Mayer's signalling and coherence principles (Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning), WCAG 2.2 use of colour and contrast (W3C). Full list with links: SEA Game `docs/verification/legibility.md` (not copied into this library; search the titles above).
```

```css
/* Reusable theme tokens (library 0.1.0, from SEA Game 0.5.1.0). MIT licence, see library/LICENSE.
   Two themes: dark "war-room" (default, screens) and light "projector" (bright rooms), switched with
   <html data-theme="light">. Contrast against --surface (WCAG 2.x ratio), measured 2026-10-12:
     dark : ink 14.7, muted 8.4, accent 11.4, ok 10.8, warn 9.9, bad 8.1, focus 12.3, field-line 3.5, line 1.7
     light: ink 18.6, muted 10.4, accent 9.2, ok 7.3, warn 8.4, bad 8.0, focus 6.8, field-line 6.5, line 3.2
   Every text colour clears the 7:1 projector target; --field-line clears 3:1 for form borders (WCAG 1.4.11);
   --line is decorative only (in the dark theme it is under 3:1, so never let it carry meaning).
   Re-measure any colour you change. Pair ok/warn/bad with an icon or word: never colour alone. */
:root {
  --paper: #0b100e; --surface: #121a17; --sunken: #18221e; --ink: #e3ece6; --muted: #a3b8ad;
  --line: #2f4339; --accent: #8fe0b8; --accent-ink: #04130c; --ok: #82dd9d; --warn: #f2b84b; --bad: #ff9184;
  --focus: #ffd166; --bar-track: #22302a;
  --panel-bg: rgb(18 26 23 / .9); --bar-bg: rgb(10 15 13 / .92); --field-bg: #0d1412; --field-line: #5d7468;
  --hover-bg: #1d2a25; --stage: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 70%, #1c2823, #0d1412 70%);
  --grid-line: rgb(143 224 184 / .045); --glow: rgb(143 224 184 / .07);
  --hud-glow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(143 224 184 / .18), 0 0 18px rgb(143 224 184 / .08);
  --primary-glow: 0 0 14px rgb(143 224 184 / .25);
  --radius: 2px;
  --gap: 1rem;            /* 8 px within a group is --gap / 2; 16 px between groups is --gap */
  --font: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;
  --mono: ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", "SF Mono", Consolas, monospace;
  color-scheme: dark;
}
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --paper: #eef1ee; --surface: #ffffff; --sunken: #e3e9e5; --ink: #0b1510; --muted: #34433b;
  --line: #7f968a; --accent: #0d5236; --accent-ink: #ffffff; --ok: #17632d; --warn: #6e4400; --bad: #9c1f16;
  --focus: #1b4fd1; --bar-track: #d3dcd7;
  --panel-bg: #ffffff; --bar-bg: #ffffff; --field-bg: #ffffff; --field-line: #4d6357;
  --hover-bg: #dfe8e2; --stage: radial-gradient(ellipse at 50% 70%, #ffffff, #dfe6e1 70%);
  --grid-line: rgb(13 82 54 / .06); --glow: rgb(13 82 54 / .05);
  --hud-glow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(13 82 54 / .25); --primary-glow: none;
  color-scheme: light;
}

/* Base that goes with the tokens. */
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { margin: 0; background: var(--paper); color: var(--ink); font: 1rem/1.5 var(--font); overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
p { max-width: 68ch; }
a { color: var(--accent); }
:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
}
/* CSS cannot stop JavaScript or WebGL motion (auto-rotation, canvas effects): read matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')
   in script, stop or replace that motion, and offer an in-app pause control as well. */
```

### playwright.config.ts

Paths: `playwright.config.ts`. SHA-256 `14fdbbff372def5088a3d721df70b6cb78625a419e6faf193fb5265aae152f09`, 2602 bytes.

```ts
import { defineConfig, devices } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'node:path';

// Keep downloaded browsers inside the project root (MPES C-13) unless CI provides its own.
if (!process.env.CI && !process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH) {
  process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH = path.resolve('.artifacts/ms-playwright');
}

// Support is Windows 11 only (MPES §4.3): Chrome and Edge (Chromium) and Firefox. `msedge` drives the
// Edge installed with Windows rather than a downloaded build.
const engines = (process.env.SEA_ENGINES ?? 'chromium,firefox,msedge').split(',');
const all = [
  { name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } },
  // Firefox refuses WebGL on GPU-less machines such as CI runners ("AllowWebgl2:false restricts context creation",
  // run 38097185474), so the 3D tests would only ever see the stills fallback. Forcing WebGL on gives it a software
  // context, as Chromium has; the stills fallback keeps its own tests (withoutWebgl).
  { name: 'firefox', use: { ...devices['Desktop Firefox'], launchOptions: { firefoxUserPrefs: { 'webgl.force-enabled': true } } } },
  { name: 'msedge', use: { ...devices['Desktop Edge'], channel: 'msedge' } },
];

const browsers = all.filter(project => engines.includes(project.name)).map(project => ({ ...project, testIgnore: /perf\.spec\.ts/ }));
// RQ-26 budgets are measured in Chromium, alone, after every other project has finished. No trace: its DOM
// snapshots run in the page on every action, inside the timed window (about 40 ms per click at 4x, G3 profile).
const perf = engines.includes('chromium')
  ? [{ name: 'perf', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], trace: 'off' as const }, testMatch: /perf\.spec\.ts/, dependencies: browsers.map(project => project.name) }]
  : [];

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: 'tests/e2e',
  // Refuse to test a dist/index.html older than the source (tests/e2e/fresh-build.ts).
  globalSetup: './tests/e2e/fresh-build.ts',
  outputDir: '.artifacts/test-results',
  fullyParallel: true,
  forbidOnly: !!process.env.CI,
  retries: 0,
  reporter: process.env.CI ? [['list'], ['github']] : [['list']],
  timeout: 120_000,
  // actionTimeout: a click or read that cannot happen fails within 60 s with its own message instead of hanging until the
  // test timeout (a lost Firefox click once held J1 for 10 minutes). Not shorter: renderers under parallel
  // load can stall for about 15 s and then recover (local verify, 2026-10-10).
  use: { viewport: { width: 1280, height: 720 }, actionTimeout: 60_000, trace: 'retain-on-failure' },
  projects: [...browsers, ...perf],
});
```

### playwright.perf-ref.config.ts

Paths: `playwright.perf-ref.config.ts`. SHA-256 `9701ff8901d80ebb3c26afc8a2a6d81e8015aa5a68203ea377b278156dabffde`, 2808 bytes.

```ts
// G3 `npm run perf:ref`: the MPES §14 reference-laptop proxy. Chromium and Edge forced onto this PC's Intel UHD 770
// with 4x CPU throttling (set inside the spec). Separate from playwright.config.ts on purpose: it is not part of
// `npm run verify`, and the existing `perf` project is untouched. The run refuses to measure unless the unmasked
// WebGL renderer says "UHD Graphics 770". Reports land in .artifacts/perf-ref/<timestamp>/.
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'node:path';

if (!process.env.CI && !process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH) {
  process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH = path.resolve('.artifacts/ms-playwright');
}

// One timestamp for the whole run, shared with the workers and the teardown through the environment.
const pad = (n: number) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
const now = new Date();
process.env.PERF_REF_STAMP ??= `${now.getFullYear()}${pad(now.getMonth() + 1)}${pad(now.getDate())}T${pad(now.getHours())}${pad(now.getMinutes())}${pad(now.getSeconds())}`;
process.env.PERF_REF_DIR ??= path.resolve('.artifacts/perf-ref', process.env.PERF_REF_STAMP);

/** The owner's launch flags, verbatim (the underscore form of the last one is Chromium's own spelling). */
const GPU_ARGS = ['--use-angle=d3d11', '--enable-gpu', '--ignore-gpu-blocklist', '--force_low_power_gpu', '--js-flags=--expose-gc'];

const engines = (process.env.SEA_ENGINES ?? 'chromium,msedge').split(',');
const launch = {
  args: GPU_ARGS,
  // Playwright's own defaults must not undo the flags above.
  ignoreDefaultArgs: ['--disable-gpu', '--disable-gpu-compositing', '--disable-software-rasterizer'],
  headless: !process.env.PERF_REF_HEADED,
};
const all = [
  // channel 'chromium' is the full Chromium in its new headless mode; the default headless shell has no real GPU path.
  { name: 'perf-ref-chromium', use: { channel: 'chromium', launchOptions: launch }, engine: 'chromium' },
  { name: 'perf-ref-msedge', use: { channel: 'msedge', launchOptions: launch }, engine: 'msedge' },
];

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: 'tests/perf-ref',
  testMatch: /perf-ref\.spec\.ts/,
  outputDir: '.artifacts/test-results-perf-ref',
  // One browser at a time, one test at a time: timings must not compete with each other.
  fullyParallel: false,
  workers: 1,
  // Stop at the first failure: a wrong GPU makes every later number meaningless.
  maxFailures: 1,
  forbidOnly: true,
  retries: 0,
  reporter: [['list']],
  // Three viewport profiles plus idle windows per browser; generous because the run is slow by design.
  timeout: 1_200_000,
  globalTeardown: './tests/perf-ref/teardown.ts',
  use: { actionTimeout: 60_000, trace: 'off' },
  projects: all.filter(project => engines.includes(project.engine)).map(project => ({ name: project.name, use: project.use })),
});
```

### scripts/archive-prep.ts

Paths: `scripts/archive-prep.ts`. SHA-256 `a14b5ddb8762b530f636b13bc19391147257399f9c00f39fbfab83df72868436`, 7893 bytes.

```ts
// Backup preparation (G2 item 8, AGENTS.md): the smallest project folder that still rebuilds, runs and is maintained
// the same. Usage: npm run archive:prep (dry run: lists what would go and what stays) or, only when the owner asks for
// a cleanup, npm run archive:prep -- --apply. Only the regenerable paths below are removed; everything else is kept:
// git history, source, content, renders, models, costly masters (.artifacts/renders, concepts, models), evidence and
// logs, and _archive/. Apply refuses any path that holds a tracked file or lies outside the project, unlinks links
// and junctions without following them, then writes RESTORE.md with the steps and the hashes to check.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync, lstatSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmdirSync, unlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { dirname, join, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

/** Everything removable: each one comes back from a command in RESTORE.md. */
export const REGENERABLE: readonly { readonly path: string; readonly how: string }[] = [
  { path: 'node_modules', how: '`npm ci`' },
  { path: 'dist', how: '`npm run build`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/ms-playwright', how: '`npm run browsers` (Edge: the copy installed with Windows)' },
  { path: '.artifacts/npm-cache', how: 'npm fills it again' },
  { path: '.artifacts/tools', how: 'Blender 5.2.2: download and unzip (art/README.md, URL and SHA-256 there)' },
  { path: '.artifacts/gallery', how: '`npm run gallery`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/packed', how: '`node art/tools/pack-models.ts .artifacts/models .artifacts/packed/models.glb`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/test-results', how: '`npm run e2e`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/test-results-sw', how: '`npm run e2e`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/coverage', how: '`npx vitest run --coverage`' },
  { path: '.artifacts/tmp', how: 'scratch folders of the unit tests, made again by `npm test`' },
  { path: 'test-results', how: '`npm run e2e`' },
  { path: 'playwright-report', how: '`npm run e2e`' },
  { path: 'coverage', how: '`npx vitest run --coverage`' },
];
/** Python bytecode caches, wherever they are outside the removed folders. */
const CACHE_DIR = '__pycache__';

const ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');

interface Entry { readonly path: string; readonly how: string; readonly bytes: number; readonly files: number }

/** Size of a tree, not following links (a junction counts as nothing: its target is elsewhere). */
function measure(path: string): { bytes: number; files: number } {
  const stat = lstatSync(path);
  if (stat.isSymbolicLink() || !stat.isDirectory()) return { bytes: stat.isSymbolicLink() ? 0 : stat.size, files: 1 };
  let bytes = 0, files = 0;
  for (const name of readdirSync(path)) { const m = measure(join(path, name)); bytes += m.bytes; files += m.files; }
  return { bytes, files };
}

/** Removes a tree; links and junctions are unlinked, never followed. */
function remove(path: string): void {
  const stat = lstatSync(path);
  if (stat.isSymbolicLink()) { try { unlinkSync(path); } catch { rmdirSync(path); } return; }
  if (stat.isDirectory()) { for (const name of readdirSync(path)) remove(join(path, name)); rmdirSync(path); return; }
  unlinkSync(path);
}

function pycaches(root: string, dir = root, found: string[] = []): string[] {
  for (const name of readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    if (!name.isDirectory() || name.name === '.git' || name.name === '_archive') continue;
    const rel = relative(root, join(dir, name.name)).split(sep).join('/');
    if (REGENERABLE.some(r => rel === r.path)) continue;
    if (name.name === CACHE_DIR) found.push(rel); else pycaches(root, join(dir, name.name), found);
  }
  return found;
}

export function plan(root = ROOT): Entry[] {
  const tracked = execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', '-z'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 26 }).split('\0').filter(Boolean);
  const targets = [...REGENERABLE, ...pycaches(root).map(path => ({ path, how: 'Python writes it again' }))];
  const entries: Entry[] = [];
  for (const { path, how } of targets) {
    const full = resolve(root, path);
    if (!full.startsWith(root + sep)) throw new Error(`${path}: outside the project`);
    // A link or junction above the target (say .artifacts itself) would lead removal outside the project.
    for (let up = dirname(full); up.length > root.length; up = dirname(up)) {
      if (lstatSync(up, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`${path}: ${relative(root, up).split(sep).join('/')} is a link, refusing`);
    }
    if (tracked.some(t => t === path || t.startsWith(`${path}/`))) throw new Error(`${path}: holds tracked files, refusing`);
    if (!existsSync(full)) continue;
    entries.push({ path, how, ...measure(full) });
  }
  return entries;
}

const sha256 = (data: Buffer) => createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex');

/** RESTORE.md: the steps back to a working project and the hashes that prove it. */
export function restoreText(root: string, removed: readonly Entry[]): string {
  const git = (...args: string[]) => execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as { gameVersion: string };
  const build = existsSync(join(root, 'dist', 'index.html')) ? sha256(readFileSync(join(root, 'dist', 'index.html'))) : '';
  const dirty = git('status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=no');
  return [
    '# Restore this project',
    '',
    `Written by \`npm run archive:prep -- --apply\` (scripts/archive-prep.ts) for SEA Game ${pkg.gameVersion}, commit \`${git('rev-parse', 'HEAD')}\`${dirty ? ' with uncommitted changes to tracked files' : ''}. It removed only what the commands below make again.`,
    '',
    '## Steps',
    '',
    '1. Install Node.js 22 or later (CI uses Node 24) and Git.',
    '2. `npm ci` installs the exact packages of package-lock.json.',
    '3. `npm run browsers` installs Chromium and Firefox into .artifacts/ms-playwright, where playwright.config.ts looks (plain `npx playwright install` would use the user cache); Edge is the copy installed with Windows.',
    '4. `npm run build` writes dist/index.html.',
    `5. Check it: its SHA-256 must be \`${build || 'not recorded: dist/ was absent at preparation'}\`.`,
    '6. `npm run verify` runs every check; it must pass.',
    '7. Only for art work: Blender 5.2.2 into .artifacts/tools/ (art/README.md gives the URL and SHA-256).',
    '',
    '## Removed',
    '',
    '| Path | Files | MB | Comes back from |',
    '|---|---:|---:|---|',
    ...removed.map(e => `| \`${e.path}\` | ${e.files} | ${(e.bytes / 1048576).toFixed(1)} | ${e.how} |`),
    '',
    'Kept: the git history, every tracked file, render masters, models, concept images, logs and evidence in .artifacts/, and _archive/.',
    '',
  ].join('\n');
}

export function prepare(root = ROOT, apply = false): { entries: Entry[]; restore?: string } {
  const entries = plan(root);
  if (!apply) return { entries };
  const restore = restoreText(root, entries);
  for (const e of entries) remove(resolve(root, e.path));
  writeFileSync(join(root, 'RESTORE.md'), restore);
  return { entries, restore };
}

if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const apply = process.argv.includes('--apply');
  const { entries } = prepare(ROOT, apply);
  const total = entries.reduce((n, e) => n + e.bytes, 0);
  for (const e of entries) console.log(`${(e.bytes / 1048576).toFixed(1).padStart(9)} MB  ${e.path}  (back from ${e.how.replace(/`/g, '')})`);
```

```ts
// Test browsers into the project (MPES C-13): npm run browsers [-- <engine> ...] (default chromium firefox). `npx
// playwright install` alone does not read playwright.config.ts, so it would install into the user's cache and the tests,
// which look in .artifacts/ms-playwright, would not find them. Edge is the copy installed with Windows. On CI, or when
// PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is already set, that setting is kept, as playwright.config.ts does.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');

/** The folder playwright.config.ts reads browsers from, or undefined when the environment decides. */
export function browsersPath(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env, root = ROOT): string | undefined {
  if (env.CI || env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH) return env.PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH;
  return resolve(root, '.artifacts', 'ms-playwright');
}

if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const engines = process.argv.slice(2).filter(a => !a.startsWith('-'));
  const path = browsersPath();
  const run = spawnSync(process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npx.cmd' : 'npx', ['playwright', 'install', ...(engines.length ? engines : ['chromium', 'firefox'])], {
    cwd: ROOT, stdio: 'inherit', shell: process.platform === 'win32',
    env: { ...process.env, ...(path ? { PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: path } : {}) },
  });
  process.exitCode = run.status ?? 1;
}
```

```ts
// docs/CODEBASE.md (G2 item 7): every tracked text file verbatim, each unique content once, with its paths and SHA-256;
// every binary file listed with its SHA-256, size and the command that regenerates it. Usage: npm run codebase
// [-- --check] (exit 1 when docs/CODEBASE.md is out of date). The output is deterministic: no dates, no commit hashes.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
export const OUTPUT = 'docs/CODEBASE.md';
/** Kept out of the codebase file: the specification is its own clean-room document, and this file cannot hold itself. */
export const SEPARATE: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  'docs/MPES.md': 'The specification, a clean-room document of its own (Omni 5.1.1 §333).',
  [OUTPUT]: 'This file.',
};

/** How each kind of binary file is made again; the first matching pattern applies. */
export const REGENERATE: readonly { readonly key: string; readonly pattern: RegExp; readonly how: string }[] = [
  {
    key: 'R', pattern: /^content\/renders\/.+\.avif$/,
    how: 'Render the masters with Blender 5.2.2 (art/README.md): `blender -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 -P art/blender/render.py -- --out .artifacts/renders/v3`, then encode them and write content/renders/manifest.json: `node art/tools/encode-renders.ts encode .artifacts/renders/v3 content/renders avif 65`. Cycles output varies slightly by GPU and driver, so new files match in look and size, not byte for byte.',
  },
  {
    key: 'M', pattern: /^content\/models\/.+\.glb$/,
    how: 'Export with Blender 5.2.2: `blender -b --factory-startup -P art/blender/export.py -- --out .artifacts/models`, pack: `node art/tools/pack-models.ts .artifacts/models .artifacts/packed/models.glb`, copy the result to content/models/showcase.glb and put its SHA-256 and size in content/models/manifest.json.',
  },
  {
    key: 'S', pattern: /^tests\/e2e\/visual\.spec\.ts-snapshots\/.+\.png$/,
    how: 'Visual test baselines, Chromium on Windows: `npm run build`, then `npx playwright test tests/e2e/visual.spec.ts --project=chromium --update-snapshots`; review every changed image before committing it.',
  },
];

const LANGUAGE: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = { ts: 'ts', mjs: 'js', js: 'js', json: 'json', md: 'markdown', py: 'python', yml: 'yaml', yaml: 'yaml', css: 'css', html: 'html', svg: 'xml', sh: 'sh' };

export const sha256 = (data: Buffer | string) => createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex');

/** Text means valid UTF-8 with no NUL byte; everything else is binary. */
export function isText(data: Buffer): boolean {
  return !data.includes(0) && Buffer.from(data.toString('utf8'), 'utf8').equals(data);
}

/** The fence: backticks, one more than the longest run in the content, at least three. */
export function fence(content: string): string {
  const longest = Math.max(0, ...[...content.matchAll(/`+/g)].map(m => m[0].length));
  return '`'.repeat(Math.max(3, longest + 1));
}

export function trackedFiles(root = ROOT): string[] {
  return execFileSync('git', ['ls-files', '-z'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 26 }).split('\0').filter(Boolean).sort();
}

export function codebase(root = ROOT): string {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as { gameVersion: string };
  // This file describes itself the same way whether or not it is tracked yet.
  const files = [...trackedFiles(root).filter(p => p !== OUTPUT), OUTPUT];
  const unique = new Map<string, { paths: string[]; content: string; bytes: number }>();
  const binaries: { path: string; hash: string; bytes: number; key: string }[] = [];
  const separate: { path: string; hash: string; bytes: number; why: string }[] = [];
  for (const path of files) {
    if (path === OUTPUT) { separate.push({ path, hash: '', bytes: 0, why: SEPARATE[path]! }); continue; }
    const data = readFileSync(join(root, path));
    const hash = sha256(data);
    if (path in SEPARATE) { separate.push({ path, hash, bytes: data.length, why: SEPARATE[path]! }); continue; }
    if (isText(data)) {
      const entry = unique.get(hash);
      if (entry) entry.paths.push(path); else unique.set(hash, { paths: [path], content: data.toString('utf8'), bytes: data.length });
      continue;
    }
    const rule = REGENERATE.find(r => r.pattern.test(path));
    if (!rule) throw new Error(`${path}: binary file with no regenerating command in scripts/codebase.ts`);
    binaries.push({ path, hash, bytes: data.length, key: rule.key });
  }
  const textCount = [...unique.values()].reduce((n, u) => n + u.paths.length, 0);
  const out: string[] = [
    '# SEA Game codebase',
    '',
    `Version ${pkg.gameVersion}. Written by \`npm run codebase\` (scripts/codebase.ts); do not edit by hand. It holds all ${files.length} tracked files of the repository: ${textCount} text files as ${unique.size} unique contents, ${binaries.length} binary files by hash with the command that regenerates them, and ${separate.length} documents kept separately. With docs/MPES.md it is enough to rebuild the project.`,
    '',
    '## How to rebuild the tree',
    '',
    '1. For each section under "Text files", write the fenced block to every path on its "Paths" line, byte for byte, in UTF-8 with LF line ends. The block is everything between the opening fence line and the closing fence line, which is the same run of backticks alone on a line.',
    '2. Each block ends with a line end, which belongs to the file unless the section says "no final line end"; then drop that one last LF. A section of 0 bytes has an empty block and makes an empty file.',
    '3. Check every file against the SHA-256 on its section.',
    '4. Make each binary file with the command of its key (table "Binary files"); check its hash when the command is deterministic.',
    '5. Then: `npm ci`, `npm run browsers` (Chromium and Firefox into .artifacts/ms-playwright; Edge is the copy installed with Windows), `npm run verify`.',
    '',
    '## Text files',
    '',
  ];
  for (const [hash, { paths, content, bytes }] of unique) {
    const ext = paths[0]!.includes('.') ? paths[0]!.split('.').pop()!.toLowerCase() : '';
    const final = content.length === 0 || content.endsWith('\n');
    const mark = fence(content);
    out.push(`### ${paths[0]}`, '', `Paths: ${paths.map(p => `\`${p}\``).join(', ')}. SHA-256 \`${hash}\`, ${bytes} bytes${final ? '' : ', no final line end'}.`, '',
      `${mark}${LANGUAGE[ext] ?? 'text'}`, ...(content ? [final ? content.slice(0, -1) : content] : []), mark, '');
  }
  out.push('## Binary files', '', 'Keys and the commands that make each kind again:', '');
  for (const rule of REGENERATE) if (binaries.some(b => b.key === rule.key)) out.push(`- **${rule.key}**: ${rule.how}`);
  out.push('', '| Path | Bytes | SHA-256 | Key |', '|---|---:|---|---|');
  for (const b of binaries) out.push(`| \`${b.path}\` | ${b.bytes} | \`${b.hash}\` | ${b.key} |`);
  out.push('', '## Documents kept separately', '', '| Path | Bytes | SHA-256 | Why |', '|---|---:|---|---|');
  for (const s of separate) out.push(s.path === OUTPUT ? `| \`${s.path}\` | | | ${s.why} |` : `| \`${s.path}\` | ${s.bytes} | \`${s.hash}\` | ${s.why} |`);
  return `${out.join('\n')}\n`;
}

if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  const current = (() => { try { return readFileSync(join(ROOT, OUTPUT), 'utf8'); } catch { return ''; } })();
  const next = codebase();
  if (process.argv.includes('--check')) {
    if (current !== next) { console.error(`${OUTPUT} is out of date: run npm run codebase.`); process.exitCode = 1; }
  } else {
    writeFileSync(join(ROOT, OUTPUT), next);
    console.log(`${OUTPUT}: ${(Buffer.byteLength(next) / 1048576).toFixed(2)} MB`);
  }
}
```

```ts
// Visual review gallery (G2 item 4, AGENTS.md visual check). Usage: npm run gallery [-- --since <tag>] [--notes <file>]
// Builds this checkout and the tag (default: the latest tag), captures every shot of scripts/gallery/shots.ts from
// both, and writes one offline captioned page, .artifacts/review/<gameVersion>.html: after beside before, changed
// shots first in each group. Nothing is fetched; the images are embedded.
import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, statSync, symlinkSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path';
import sharp from 'sharp';
import { reflow } from '../source/ui/reflow.ts';
import { DISPLAYS, shots, type Shot } from './gallery/shots.ts';

const ROOT = resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const WORK = join(ROOT, '.artifacts', 'gallery');
const arg = (name: string) => { const i = process.argv.indexOf(name); return i > 0 ? process.argv[i + 1] : undefined; };
const git = (...args: string[]) => execFileSync('git', args, { cwd: ROOT, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim();
const npx = process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npx.cmd' : 'npx';

/** The tag's game file, built once from `git archive` into .artifacts/gallery/<tag>/: with this checkout's packages when
 *  the tag's lockfile is the same, otherwise with the tag's own (`npm ci`), so the before-image is the tag as released. */
function buildTag(tag: string): string {
  const tree = join(WORK, tag);
  const out = join(tree, 'dist', 'index.html');
  if (existsSync(out)) return out;
  mkdirSync(tree, { recursive: true });
  const archive = execFileSync('git', ['archive', '--format=tar', tag], { cwd: ROOT, maxBuffer: 1 << 30 });
  // Windows' own tar: the Git Bash tar earlier on PATH cannot open drive-letter paths.
  const tar = process.platform === 'win32' ? join(process.env.SystemRoot ?? 'C:\\Windows', 'System32', 'tar.exe') : 'tar';
  execFileSync(tar, ['-x', '-C', tree], { input: archive });
  if (!existsSync(join(tree, 'node_modules'))) {
    const same = readFileSync(join(tree, 'package-lock.json'), 'utf8') === readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'package-lock.json'), 'utf8');
    if (same) symlinkSync(join(ROOT, 'node_modules'), join(tree, 'node_modules'), 'junction');
    else execFileSync(process.platform === 'win32' ? 'npm.cmd' : 'npm', ['ci', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: tree, stdio: 'inherit', shell: process.platform === 'win32' });
  }
  execFileSync(process.execPath, ['build/build.ts'], { cwd: tree, stdio: 'inherit' });
  return out;
}

/** Captures every shot of one game file; a shot that fails (a view an older tag lacks) leaves no fresh file. True when
 *  every shot was captured. */
function capture(dist: string, out: string): boolean {
  mkdirSync(out, { recursive: true });
  const run = spawnSync(npx, ['playwright', 'test', '--config', 'scripts/gallery/playwright.config.ts'], {
    cwd: ROOT, stdio: 'inherit', shell: process.platform === 'win32',
    env: { ...process.env, SEA_GALLERY_DIST: dist, SEA_GALLERY_OUT: out },
  });
  if (run.status !== 0) console.warn(`Some shots of ${dist} failed; they are marked missing in the gallery.`);
  return run.status === 0;
}

/** A capture written since `after` (ms); older files are left from earlier runs and count as missing. */
async function image(path: string, after = 0): Promise<{ uri: string; raw: Buffer; width: number; height: number } | null> {
  if (!existsSync(path) || statSync(path).mtimeMs < after) return null;
  const { data, info } = await sharp(path).removeAlpha().raw().toBuffer({ resolveWithObject: true });
  const webp = await sharp(path).webp({ quality: 80 }).toBuffer();
  return { uri: `data:image/webp;base64,${webp.toString('base64')}`, raw: data, width: info.width, height: info.height };
}

/** Changed when the size differs or more than 0.1 % of pixels differ noticeably. */
function changed(a: { raw: Buffer; width: number; height: number }, b: { raw: Buffer; width: number; height: number }): boolean {
  if (a.width !== b.width || a.height !== b.height) return true;
  let differing = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < a.raw.length; i += 3) {
    if (Math.abs(a.raw[i]! - b.raw[i]!) + Math.abs(a.raw[i + 1]! - b.raw[i + 1]!) + Math.abs(a.raw[i + 2]! - b.raw[i + 2]!) > 24) differing++;
  }
  return differing > 0.001 * a.width * a.height;
}

const escape = (s: string) => s.replace(/[&<>"]/g, c => ({ '&': '&amp;', '<': '&lt;', '>': '&gt;', '"': '&quot;' })[c]!);

async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(ROOT, 'package.json'), 'utf8')) as { gameVersion: string };
  const since = arg('--since') ?? git('describe', '--tags', '--abbrev=0');

  // The baseline is kept only when every shot of it was captured; otherwise it is captured again next time, so a failed
  // capture never passes for a view the tag lacked ("New since").
  if (!existsSync(join(before, '.complete')) && capture(buildTag(since), before)) writeFileSync(join(before, '.complete'), since);

    const status = !a ? 'missing' : !b ? 'new' : changed(a, b) ? 'changed' : 'same';
    const label = { changed: 'Changed', new: `New since ${since}`, same: `Unchanged since ${since}`, missing: 'Capture failed' }[status];
    const figure = (img: typeof a, name: string) => img
      ? `<figure><figcaption>${escape(name)}</figcaption><img src="${img.uri}" width="${img.width}" height="${img.height}" alt="${escape(`${shot.title}, ${name}`)}" loading="lazy" decoding="async"></figure>`
      : '';
    rows.push({ shot, status, html: `<article id="${shot.id}" class="shot ${status}"><h3>${escape(shot.title)} <span class="badge">${label}</span></h3>
<p>${escape(shot.caption)} <span class="muted">${escape(shot.display.name)}.</span></p>
<div class="pair">${figure(a, `After: ${pkg.gameVersion}`)}${status === 'changed' ? figure(b, `Before: ${since}`) : ''}</div></article>` });
  }
  const groups = [...new Set(list.map(s => s.group))];

  const count = (status: string) => rows.filter(r => r.status === status).length;
  const intro = notes ? reflow(readFileSync(notes, 'utf8')).map(b => b.kind === 'list'
    ? `<ul>${b.items.map(i => `<li>${escape(i)}</li>`).join('')}</ul>` : b.kind === 'heading' ? `<h3>${escape(b.text)}</h3>` : `<p>${escape(b.text)}</p>`).join('\n') : '';
  const page = `<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>SEA Game ${pkg.gameVersion} visual review</title>
<style>
:root { color-scheme: dark light; --bg: #0d1412; --panel: #15201c; --ink: #e6efe9; --muted: #9db3a8; --accent: #7fdcb0; --warn: #f0c060; --line: #2a3a33; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root { --bg: #f4f6f4; --panel: #ffffff; --ink: #14201b; --muted: #4c5f56; --accent: #0d5a3a; --warn: #8a5a00; --line: #cfd8d3; } }
* { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { margin: 0; background: var(--bg); color: var(--ink); font: 16px/1.5 system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif; }
header, main { max-width: 1500px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 16px; }
h1 { font-size: 1.6rem; margin: .5rem 0; } h2 { margin-top: 2rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); padding-bottom: .25rem; }

.badge { font-size: .75rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .05em; border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0 .4rem; margin-left: .5rem; color: var(--muted); }
```
