```ts
// Team inventory (MPES §6.5 win limits, §8.5 team object).
import { MAX_PURCHASES, MAX_WINS_PER_ROUND, ROUNDS, MAX_TEAMS, MIN_TEAMS, type MissionId, type Totals } from './data.ts';
import { ensure, fail } from './errors.ts';
import type { MarketCard } from './market.ts';
import { blankTotals, sumEffects } from './missions.ts';
import { add, price } from './money.ts';

export interface Purchase extends MarketCard { readonly paid: number }

/** Schema-3 team object. Totals, cost and purchasesByRound are always derived from purchases. */
export interface Team {
  readonly id: number;
  readonly mission: MissionId | null;
  readonly lockedMission: MissionId | null;
  readonly totals: Totals;
  readonly cost: number;
  readonly purchases: readonly Purchase[];
  readonly purchasesByRound: readonly number[];
  readonly profit: number;
  readonly submitted: boolean;
}

export function createTeams(count: number): Team[] {
  ensure(Number.isInteger(count) && count >= MIN_TEAMS && count <= MAX_TEAMS, 'team');
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({
    id: i + 1, mission: null, lockedMission: null, totals: blankTotals(), cost: 0,
    purchases: [], purchasesByRound: Array<number>(ROUNDS).fill(0), profit: 0, submitted: false,
  }));
}

/** Recompute derived fields from a purchase list, enforcing uniqueness and win limits. */
export function withPurchases(team: Team, purchases: readonly Purchase[]): Team {
  ensure(purchases.length <= MAX_PURCHASES, 'game-limit');
  const byRound = Array<number>(ROUNDS).fill(0), ids = new Set<string>(), slots = new Set<string>();
  let cost = 0;
  for (const purchase of purchases) {
    const slot = `${purchase.round}-${purchase.lot}`;
    if (ids.has(purchase.id) || slots.has(slot)) fail('duplicate');
    ids.add(purchase.id); slots.add(slot);
    const used = byRound[purchase.round - 1]!;
    if (used >= MAX_WINS_PER_ROUND) fail('limit');
    byRound[purchase.round - 1] = used + 1;
    cost = add(cost, price(purchase.start, purchase.paid));
  }
  add(cost, team.profit);
  return { ...team, purchases: [...purchases], purchasesByRound: byRound, cost, totals: sumEffects(purchases.map(p => p.e)) };
}

export function canWin(team: Team, round: number): boolean {
  return (team.purchasesByRound[round - 1] ?? 0) < MAX_WINS_PER_ROUND && team.purchases.length < MAX_PURCHASES;
}

/** Add a won card. Rejects off-step prices, duplicates, the 2-per-round and 14-per-game limits and overflow. */
export function acquire(team: Team, card: MarketCard, paid: number): Team {
  price(card.start, paid);
  if (team.purchases.length >= MAX_PURCHASES) fail('game-limit');
  if ((team.purchasesByRound[card.round - 1] ?? 0) >= MAX_WINS_PER_ROUND) fail('limit');
  return withPurchases(team, [...team.purchases, { ...card, title: { ...card.title }, e: { ...card.e }, paid }]);
}

export function removePurchase(team: Team, instance: string): Team {
  const index = team.purchases.findIndex(p => p.instance === instance);
  if (index < 0) fail('not-found');
  return withPurchases(team, team.purchases.filter((_, i) => i !== index));
}

export function bid(team: Team): number {
  return add(team.cost, team.profit);
}
```

```ts
// Entry point: route to the role chooser or a single role (MPES §5.3).
import { sessionStoragePort } from './app/ports.ts';
import { showAbout } from './ui/about.ts';
import { applyTheme, themeFrom, toggleTheme, withTheme } from './ui/theme.ts';
import { renders, VEHICLE, type Render } from './showcase/renders.ts';
import { missionName } from './ui/components.ts';
import type { MissionId } from './domain/data.ts';
import { startInstructor } from './ui/instructor.ts';
import { startStudent } from './ui/student.ts';
import { h, nameDocument, replaceChildren } from './ui/dom.ts';
import { detectLanguage, otherLanguage, translate, type Language, type StringKey } from './ui/i18n.ts';

export type Role = 'instructor' | 'student';

export function parseRole(search: string): Role | 'chooser' | 'unknown' {
  const role = new URLSearchParams(search).get('role');
  if (role === null) return 'chooser';
  return role === 'instructor' || role === 'student' ? role : 'unknown';
}

export function roleHref(role: Role | null, lang: Language): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams();
  if (role) params.set('role', role);
  params.set('lang', lang);
  return `?${withTheme(params).toString()}`;
}

/**
 * Chooser lineup (G2): the six mission vehicles as embedded pre-rendered stills, the selected one large, so no 3D
 * runs on the first screen (D-08). Toggle buttons; arrow keys, Home and End move along the lineup and select.
 */
function lineup(lang: Language): HTMLElement | null {
  const stills = (Object.keys(VEHICLE) as MissionId[]).flatMap(id => {
    const still = renders().get(`${VEHICLE[id]}-hero`);
    return still ? [{ id, still }] : [];
  });
  if (!stills.length) return null;
  const size = (still: Render) => ({ width: String(still.size.width), height: String(still.size.height) });
  const first = stills[0]!;
  const large = h('img', { class: 'hero-still', id: 'hero-still', src: first.still.src, alt: translate(lang, `chooser.still.${first.id}`), decoding: 'async', ...size(first.still) });
  const select = (index: number, focus: boolean) => {
    const { id, still } = stills[index]!;
    large.src = still.src;
    large.alt = translate(lang, `chooser.still.${id}`);
    buttons.forEach((button, i) => { button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(i === index)); button.tabIndex = i === index ? 0 : -1; });
    if (focus) buttons[index]!.focus();
  };
  const keys: Readonly<Record<string, (i: number) => number>> = {
    ArrowRight: i => (i + 1) % stills.length, ArrowDown: i => (i + 1) % stills.length,
    ArrowLeft: i => (i + stills.length - 1) % stills.length, ArrowUp: i => (i + stills.length - 1) % stills.length,
    Home: () => 0, End: () => stills.length - 1,
  };
  const buttons = stills.map(({ id, still }, index) => h('button', {
    type: 'button', class: 'lineup-pick', 'aria-pressed': String(index === 0), tabindex: index === 0 ? '0' : '-1',
    on: {
      click: () => select(index, false),
      keydown: event => {
        const move = keys[(event as KeyboardEvent).key];
        if (move) { event.preventDefault(); select(move(index), true); }
      },
    },
  }, h('img', { src: still.src, alt: '', decoding: 'async', loading: 'lazy', ...size(still) }), h('span', { text: missionName(id, lang) })));
  return h('div', { class: 'hero-lineup' }, large, h('div', { class: 'lineup', role: 'group', 'aria-label': translate(lang, 'chooser.lineup') }, ...buttons));
}

/** Projector or war-room theme, switched in place (MPES §7.1). */
export function themeButton(lang: Language): HTMLButtonElement {
  const label = () => translate(lang, themeFrom() === 'light' ? 'theme.dark' : 'theme.light');
  const hint = () => translate(lang, themeFrom() === 'light' ? 'theme.darkHint' : 'theme.lightHint');
  const button = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'btn ghost', id: 'theme-toggle', text: label(), title: hint(), on: { click: () => {
    toggleTheme(); button.textContent = label(); button.title = hint();
  } } });
  return button;
}

/** Links rebuild their URL when followed, so a theme switched after rendering is kept. */
const fresh = (href: () => string) => (event: Event) => { (event.currentTarget as HTMLAnchorElement).href = href(); };

function renderChooser(root: HTMLElement, lang: Language, unknownRole: boolean): void {
  const t = (key: StringKey, vars?: Record<string, string>) => translate(lang, key, vars);
  nameDocument(lang, t('app.title'));
  const roleCard = (role: Role, label: StringKey, description: StringKey) => h('section', { class: 'role-card' },
    h('a', { class: 'btn primary big', href: roleHref(role, lang), 'data-role': role, text: t(label), on: { click: fresh(() => roleHref(role, lang)) } }),
    h('p', { class: 'muted', text: t(description) }),
  );
  replaceChildren(root, h('main', { class: 'hero', id: 'main' },
    h('div', { class: 'hero-stage' }, lineup(lang)),
    h('div', { class: 'hero-panel stack' },
      h('div', { class: 'wordmark' }, h('span', { class: 'wordmark-sea', 'aria-hidden': 'true', text: 'SEA' }), h('h1', { class: 'wordmark-title', text: t('app.title') })),
      h('p', { class: 'lead', text: t('app.tagline') }),
      unknownRole ? h('p', { class: 'notice bad', role: 'alert', text: t('chooser.unknownRole') }) : null,
      h('h2', { text: t('chooser.heading') }),
      h('div', { class: 'roles' },
        roleCard('instructor', 'chooser.instructor', 'chooser.instructorDesc'),
        roleCard('student', 'chooser.student', 'chooser.studentDesc'),
      ),
      h('p', { class: 'small', text: `${t('chooser.handoff')} ${t('chooser.privacy')}` }),
      h('div', { class: 'cluster' },
        h('a', { class: 'btn', href: roleHref(null, otherLanguage(lang)), lang: otherLanguage(lang), 'aria-label': t('lang.switchLabel'), text: t('lang.switch'), on: { click: fresh(() => roleHref(null, otherLanguage(lang))) } }),
        h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'btn ghost', text: t('about.open'), on: { click: event => void showAbout(lang, event.currentTarget as HTMLElement) } }),
        themeButton(lang),
      ),
      h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: t('chooser.version', { version: __SEA_VERSION__ }) }),
    ),
  ));
}

/** Features every journey needs (MPES §9). */
export function supported(): boolean {
  return typeof HTMLDialogElement === 'function' && 'showModal' in HTMLDialogElement.prototype
    && typeof crypto === 'object' && typeof crypto.getRandomValues === 'function' && typeof BigInt === 'function';
}

export function start(root: HTMLElement): void {
  applyTheme();
  const lang = detectLanguage(location.search, navigator.language);
  if (!supported()) {
    replaceChildren(root, h('main', { class: 'chooser', id: 'main' }, h('h1', { text: translate(lang, 'app.title') }), h('p', { class: 'notice bad', role: 'alert', text: translate(lang, 'app.unsupported') })));
    return;
  }
  const route = parseRole(location.search);
  if (route === 'chooser' || route === 'unknown') renderChooser(root, lang, route === 'unknown');
  else if (route === 'instructor') startInstructor(root, lang, sessionStoragePort());
  else startStudent(root, lang, sessionStoragePort());
}

const root = document.getElementById('app');
if (root) start(root);
```

```ts
// Framing and zoom for the 3D showcase (MPES §10.2): the camera stands far enough back that the vehicle as fitted, however
// fully kitted out, stays in view at every turn, at whatever height the player drags to; the player zooms in and out
// from there in steps, within limits.
import { type Box3, PerspectiveCamera, Vector3 } from 'three';

/** The fitted kit reaches at most this far from the frame centre (1 = the frame edge). */
export const FIT_MARGIN = 0.92;
/** One zoom press moves the camera by this factor; the limits are multiples of the fitted distance. */
export const ZOOM_STEP = 1.25;
export const ZOOM_IN_LIMIT = 0.4;
export const ZOOM_OUT_LIMIT = 1.6;
/** Turns sampled when fitting: every 7.5 degrees. */
const AZIMUTHS = 48;

/** Unit vector from the target to the camera at this polar angle (from straight up) and azimuth. */
export function viewDirection(polar: number, azimuth: number): Vector3 {
  return new Vector3().setFromSphericalCoords(1, polar, azimuth);
}

function corners(box: Box3): Vector3[] {
  const { min, max } = box;
  return [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].map(i => new Vector3(i & 1 ? max.x : min.x, i & 2 ? max.y : min.y, i & 4 ? max.z : min.z));
}

const camera = new PerspectiveCamera();
const point = new Vector3();

/** How far the box's farthest corner projects from the frame centre, seen from `distance` along `direction`. */
export function extentAt(box: Box3, target: Vector3, direction: Vector3, distance: number, fov: number, aspect: number, points = corners(box)): number {
  camera.fov = fov;
  camera.aspect = aspect;
  camera.near = 0.01;
  camera.far = distance * 10 + 100;
  camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
  camera.position.copy(direction).multiplyScalar(distance).add(target);
  camera.lookAt(target);
  camera.updateMatrixWorld();
  let extent = 0;
  for (const corner of points) {
    point.copy(corner).project(camera);
    // A corner behind the camera has no meaningful projection: treat it as out of frame.
    extent = Math.max(extent, point.z > 1 ? Infinity : Math.abs(point.x), Math.abs(point.y));
  }
  return extent;
}

/**
 * The least camera distance from `target` at which every corner of `box` lies within FIT_MARGIN of the frame centre,
 * at every sampled turn and at each polar angle given (the default view and the drag limits).
 */
export function fitDistance(box: Box3, target: Vector3, polars: readonly number[], fov: number, aspect: number, margin = FIT_MARGIN): number {
  const points = corners(box);
  const radius = Math.max(...points.map(p => p.distanceTo(target)), 1e-3);
  let distance = radius * 1.01;
  for (const polar of polars) for (let i = 0; i < AZIMUTHS; i++) {
    const direction = viewDirection(polar, (i / AZIMUTHS) * Math.PI * 2);
    if (extentAt(box, target, direction, distance, fov, aspect, points) <= margin) continue;
    // Extent falls as the camera backs away: bisect between this distance and one known to fit.
    let near = distance, far = distance * 2;
    while (extentAt(box, target, direction, far, fov, aspect, points) > margin) far *= 2;
    for (let step = 0; step < 24; step++) {
      const mid = (near + far) / 2;
      if (extentAt(box, target, direction, mid, fov, aspect, points) > margin) near = mid; else far = mid;
    }
    distance = far;
  }
  return distance;
}

/** Fitted distances at evenly spaced heights between the drag limits: lower views need the camera less far back. */
export interface FitTable { readonly polars: readonly number[]; readonly distances: readonly number[] }

export function fitTable(box: Box3, target: Vector3, polarMin: number, polarMax: number, fov: number, aspect: number, steps = 8): FitTable {
  const polars = Array.from({ length: steps + 1 }, (_, i) => polarMin + ((polarMax - polarMin) * i) / steps);
  return { polars, distances: polars.map(polar => fitDistance(box, target, [polar], fov, aspect)) };
}

/** The fitted distance at any height between the table's, by linear interpolation (FIT_MARGIN absorbs the error). */
export function distanceAt(table: FitTable, polar: number): number {
  const { polars, distances } = table, last = polars.length - 1;
  if (polar <= polars[0]!) return distances[0]!;
  if (polar >= polars[last]!) return distances[last]!;
  const i = Math.min(last - 1, Math.floor(((polar - polars[0]!) / (polars[last]! - polars[0]!)) * last));
  const f = (polar - polars[i]!) / (polars[i + 1]! - polars[i]!);
  return distances[i]! + (distances[i + 1]! - distances[i]!) * f;
}

/** The zoom (a multiple of the fitted distance) after one press: `+1` zooms in, `-1` out. */
export function zoomed(zoom: number, press: 1 | -1): number {
  const next = press > 0 ? zoom / ZOOM_STEP : zoom * ZOOM_STEP;
  return Math.min(ZOOM_OUT_LIMIT, Math.max(ZOOM_IN_LIMIT, next));
}
```

```ts
// The embedded model holds every vehicle as a root node of one scene (art/tools/pack-models.ts). Parsing all of them
// would build six vehicles' geometry to show one, so the loader first narrows the scene to the vehicle it shows:
// GLTFLoader then reads only the meshes, materials and accessors that node references (MPES §14 model-ready budget).

const MAGIC = 0x46546c67; // 'glTF'
const JSON_CHUNK = 0x4e4f534a; // 'JSON'

interface Gltf { scene?: number; scenes?: { nodes?: number[] }[]; nodes?: { name?: string }[] }

/** A copy of `glb` whose only scene holds the root node named `vehicle`; null if there is none or it is not a GLB. */
export function vehicleGlb(glb: ArrayBuffer, vehicle: string): ArrayBuffer | null {
  if (glb.byteLength < 20) return null;
  const view = new DataView(glb);
  if (view.getUint32(0, true) !== MAGIC || view.getUint32(16, true) !== JSON_CHUNK) return null;
  const jsonLen = view.getUint32(12, true);
  let json: Gltf;
  try {
    json = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(new Uint8Array(glb, 20, jsonLen))) as Gltf;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
  const roots = json.scenes?.[json.scene ?? 0]?.nodes ?? [];
  const node = roots.find(i => json.nodes?.[i]?.name === vehicle);
  if (node === undefined) return null;
  json.scenes = [{ nodes: [node] }];
  json.scene = 0;
  const text = new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(json));
  const padded = Math.ceil(text.length / 4) * 4;
  const rest = new Uint8Array(glb, 20 + jsonLen); // the binary chunk, header included, unchanged
  const out = new Uint8Array(20 + padded + rest.length);
  const outView = new DataView(out.buffer);
  outView.setUint32(0, MAGIC, true);
  outView.setUint32(4, view.getUint32(4, true), true);
  outView.setUint32(8, out.length, true);
  outView.setUint32(12, padded, true);
  outView.setUint32(16, JSON_CHUNK, true);
  out.fill(0x20, 20, 20 + padded);
  out.set(text, 20);
  out.set(rest, 20 + padded);
  return out.buffer;
}
```

```ts
// Real-time vehicle showcase (MPES §10): the embedded glTF model on a slowly turning stage the player can drag.
// One renderer per page; it draws only while visible, in one paced animation frame (at most 30 a second and at
// most half the machine, MPES §10.3), and never turns by itself
// when the player prefers reduced motion. Without WebGL the caller shows the still renders instead.
import {
  ACESFilmicToneMapping, Box3, Color, DirectionalLight, Group, Mesh, MeshStandardMaterial, type Object3D,
  HalfFloatType, PCFShadowMap, PerspectiveCamera, PlaneGeometry, PMREMGenerator, Scene, ShadowMaterial, SRGBColorSpace,
  type Texture, Timer, Vector2, Vector3, WebGLRenderer, WebGLRenderTarget,
} from 'three';
import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js';
import { RoomEnvironment } from 'three/examples/jsm/environments/RoomEnvironment.js';
import { OutputPass } from 'three/examples/jsm/postprocessing/OutputPass.js';
import { vehicleGlb } from './glb.ts';
import { distanceAt, extentAt, fitTable, zoomed, type FitTable } from './frame.ts';
import { premultipliedOutput } from './resolve.ts';
import { FramePacer, INPUT_HOLD_MS, TIERS, nextTier, startTier } from './pace.ts';

/** Seconds per full turn when the stage turns by itself. */
export const TURN_SECONDS = 40;
const UP = new Vector3(0, 1, 0);
/** The opening view: three-quarter front, a little above (MPES §10.5 camera). */
const OPENING = new Vector3(0.62, 0.32, 0.72).normalize();
/** How far the player can drag the view up and down (polar angle from straight up). */
const POLAR_MIN = 0.6, POLAR_MAX = 1.45;
/** How often a lost graphics context is checked for a return its browser did not announce. */
const LOST_CHECK_MS = 1000;

let packed: Promise<ArrayBuffer | null> | null = null;
const libraries = new Map<string, Promise<Group | null>>();
const preparing = new Set<string>();

/** Base64 to bytes: the browser's own decoder where it has one (a quarter of the time), else atob. */
function base64Bytes(text: string): Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> {
  const native = (Uint8Array as unknown as { fromBase64?: (s: string) => Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> }).fromBase64;
  if (native) return native(text);
  const binary = atob(text);
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(binary.length);
  for (let i = 0; i < binary.length; i++) bytes[i] = binary.charCodeAt(i);
  return bytes;
}

/** The embedded model file (every vehicle): base64 of a raw-deflated GLB in an inert script block, inflated once. */
function embedded(): Promise<ArrayBuffer | null> {
  packed ??= (async () => {
    const text = document.getElementById('sea-models')?.textContent?.trim();
    if (!text) return null;
    const bytes = base64Bytes(text);
    return new Response(new Blob([bytes]).stream().pipeThrough(new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'))).arrayBuffer();
  })().catch(() => null);
  return packed;
}

/**
 * One vehicle's model: the group named by its file stem, holding its base and every part. Only that vehicle's
 * geometry is parsed (vehicleGlb), the first time it is shown; it is then reused.
 */
export function loadVehicle(vehicle: string): Promise<Group | null> {
  let library = libraries.get(vehicle);
  if (!library) {
    library = (async () => {
      const file = await embedded();
      const glb = file && vehicleGlb(file, vehicle);
      if (!glb) return null;
      const scene = (await new GLTFLoader().parseAsync(glb, '')).scene;
      performance.mark(`sea-model:${vehicle}`);
      return scene;
    })().catch(() => null);
    libraries.set(vehicle, library);
  }
  return library;
}

/**
 * Decodes and parses a vehicle's model in idle time, so the tracker opens with it ready (MPES §10.3). Called once the
 * team confirms its vehicle in planning; nothing happens without WebGL, where the tracker shows stills.
 */
export function prepareVehicle(vehicle: string): void {
  if (libraries.has(vehicle) || preparing.has(vehicle)) return;
  preparing.add(vehicle);
  const run = () => { if (webglAvailable()) void loadVehicle(vehicle); };
  // Idle time, but within two seconds even on a busy page.
  if ('requestIdleCallback' in globalThis) requestIdleCallback(run, { timeout: 2000 }); else setTimeout(run, 200);
}

/** Software renderers draw on the CPU, which a turning model would saturate (no GPU, remote desktop). */
const SOFTWARE = /swiftshader|llvmpipe|softpipe|basic render|software/i;

/** WebGL 2 on a hardware GPU. Without one the showcase shows its still renders (performance over looks). */
export function webglAvailable(): boolean {
  try {
    const gl = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('webgl2');
    if (!gl) return false;
    const info = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info');
    const renderer = String(gl.getParameter(info ? info.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL : gl.RENDERER));
    gl.getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context')?.loseContext();
    return !SOFTWARE.test(renderer);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/** The layer a vehicle's child node draws: 'base' or a part card ID (node extras; three.js de-duplicates names). */
export function layerOf(node: Object3D): string {
  return String(node.userData['layer'] ?? node.name);
}

/** Part card IDs in a vehicle group, and the mount slot each fills (node extras). */
export function partSlots(vehicle: Object3D): Map<string, string> {
  const slots = new Map<string, string>();
  for (const node of vehicle.children) if (layerOf(node) !== 'base') slots.set(layerOf(node), String(node.userData['slot'] ?? layerOf(node)));
  return slots;
}

export class ModelStage {
  readonly canvas: HTMLCanvasElement;
  #renderer: WebGLRenderer;
  #scene = new Scene();
  #camera = new PerspectiveCamera(30, 16 / 9, 0.1, 200);
  #controls: OrbitControls;
  #timer = new Timer();
  #vehicle: Object3D | null = null;
  #frame = 0;
  #pacer = new FramePacer();
  #dirty = true;
  /** A change the player asked for (a purchase, turn, zoom or resize) waiting to be drawn: it skips the pacer's wait. */
  #urgent = false;
  /** Index into TIERS: the resolution and edge smoothing this machine can draw in time (adaptive tiers). */
  #tier = 0;
  /** Where a multisampled tier draws the scene, then resolved to the canvas with tone mapping by #output; none on a
   *  tier without multisampling. The canvas itself has none, so a tier can drop it without a new context. */
  #target: WebGLRenderTarget | null = null;
  #output = resolvePass();
  #environment: Texture | null = null;
  #lost = false;
  /** While the context is lost, the check that notices its return (see the constructor). */
  #watch: ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | undefined;
  /** Removes every listener the stage added outside its controls when it is disposed (`tests/unit/stage-dispose.test.ts`). */
  readonly #listening = new AbortController();
  /** The player's input anywhere else on the page holds the paced turning draws (input first, MPES §10.3). */
  #input = (event: Event): void => { if (event.target !== this.canvas) this.#pacer.hold(performance.now() + INPUT_HOLD_MS); };
  #visible = true;
  #observer: IntersectionObserver;
  #resize: ResizeObserver;
  #motion = matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)');
  /** The bounds of the vehicle as fitted, the distance that frames them, and the player's zoom (a multiple of it). */
  #kit = new Box3();
  #fitted: FitTable = { polars: [0], distances: [1] };
  /** The aspect the fitted distance was found for; a showcase update re-attaches the canvas at the same size. */
  #fittedAspect = 0;
  #zoom = 1;
  /** Called after every draw with the camera's azimuth (radians), how far the kit reaches from the frame centre
   * (1 = the frame edge) and the zoom. */
  onView: ((azimuth: number, extent: number, zoom: number) => void) | null = null;
  /** Called after each draw has reached the canvas: what the player sees now matches the last `show`. */
  onDraw: (() => void) | null = null;

  constructor() {
    this.canvas = document.createElement('canvas');
    this.canvas.className = 'showcase-canvas';
    this.#renderer = new WebGLRenderer({ canvas: this.canvas, antialias: false, alpha: true, powerPreference: 'low-power' });
    this.#tierTo(0);
    this.#renderer.outputColorSpace = SRGBColorSpace;
    this.#renderer.toneMapping = ACESFilmicToneMapping;
    this.#renderer.toneMappingExposure = 0.85;
    this.#renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true;
    this.#renderer.shadowMap.type = PCFShadowMap;
    // Baked shadows: the sun and the vehicle stand still while the camera orbits, so the shadow map only changes with the
    // fitted parts; drawing it every frame doubled each turning draw (G3). show() asks for it again.
    this.#renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false;
    this.#environ();
    this.#scene.background = null;
    const sun = new DirectionalLight(new Color(1, 0.97, 0.92), 1.6);
    sun.position.set(6, 12, 5);
    sun.castShadow = true;
    sun.shadow.mapSize.set(1024, 1024);
    Object.assign(sun.shadow.camera, { left: -6, right: 6, top: 6, bottom: -6, near: 1, far: 30 });
    sun.shadow.bias = -0.0005;
    sun.shadow.radius = 4;
    this.#scene.add(sun);
    // Rim light from behind the vehicle as seen from the camera, whichever way it turns: a cool, unshadowed edge
    // that lifts each part's outline off the dark stage and off the parts behind it (MPES §10.5 legibility).
    const rim = new DirectionalLight(new Color(0.85, 0.9, 1), 0.5);
    rim.position.set(6, 5, -18);
    rim.target.position.set(0, 0, -10);
    this.#camera.add(rim, rim.target);
    this.#scene.add(this.#camera);
    const floor = new Mesh(new PlaneGeometry(30, 30), new ShadowMaterial({ opacity: 0.35 }));
    floor.rotation.x = -Math.PI / 2;
    floor.receiveShadow = true;
    this.#scene.add(floor);
    this.#controls = new OrbitControls(this.#camera, this.canvas);
    Object.assign(this.#controls, {
      enableDamping: true, enablePan: false, enableZoom: false, autoRotate: !this.#motion.matches,
      autoRotateSpeed: 60 / TURN_SECONDS, minPolarAngle: POLAR_MIN, maxPolarAngle: POLAR_MAX,
    });
    // OrbitControls sets touch-action none, which traps a finger swipe over the stage: give vertical swipes back to the
    // page (the stylesheet's pan-y), so only a sideways drag turns the vehicle (G3 touch safety).
    this.canvas.style.touchAction = '';
    this.#controls.addEventListener('change', () => this.#invalidate());
    this.#controls.addEventListener('start', () => this.#loop());
    const { signal } = this.#listening;
    this.#motion.addEventListener('change', () => { this.turning = !this.#motion.matches; }, { signal });
    this.#observer = new IntersectionObserver(([entry]) => { this.#visible = !!entry?.isIntersecting; this.#loop(); });
    this.#observer.observe(this.canvas);
    this.#resize = new ResizeObserver(() => this.#size());
    this.#resize.observe(this.canvas);
    document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => this.#loop(), { signal });
    for (const type of ['pointerdown', 'keydown', 'input']) document.addEventListener(type, this.#input, { capture: true, passive: true, signal });
    // A lost graphics context (driver reset, GPU switch, sleep) stops the stage; three.js rebuilds the context when it is
    // restored, but what was drawn into textures is gone: the environment and the shadow are made again, then one draw.
    // The context, not the events, says whether it is back: Firefox on a software renderer announced a restore while the
    // context was still lost, then restored it without a word (G3, CI run 38577929333). So an early announcement is
    // stopped before three.js rebuilds onto a dead context, and while lost a slow check notices a silent return and
    // announces it, which rebuilds three.js and the stage alike.
    this.canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextlost', () => {
      this.#lost = true;
      this.#stop();
      clearInterval(this.#watch);
      this.#watch = setInterval(() => {
        if (!this.#renderer.getContext().isContextLost()) this.canvas.dispatchEvent(new Event('webglcontextrestored'));
      }, LOST_CHECK_MS);
    }, { signal });
    this.canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextrestored', event => {
      if (this.#renderer.getContext().isContextLost()) { event.stopImmediatePropagation(); return; }
    }, { capture: true, signal });
    this.canvas.addEventListener('webglcontextrestored', () => {
      clearInterval(this.#watch);
      this.#lost = false;
      this.#environ();
      this.#renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true;
      this.#invalidate(true);
    }, { signal });
  }

  /** The lighting environment, drawn into a texture. A 64 px environment lights matte paint as well as the default
   *  256 px, with a sixteenth of the pixels to render and blur. */
  #environ(): void {
    const pmrem = new PMREMGenerator(this.#renderer);
    this.#environment?.dispose();
    this.#environment = pmrem.fromScene(new RoomEnvironment(), 0.04, 0.1, 100, { size: 64 }).texture;
    this.#scene.environment = this.#environment;
    pmrem.dispose();
  }

  /** Whether the stage turns by itself (off under reduced motion until the player turns it on). */
  get turning(): boolean { return this.#controls.autoRotate; }
  set turning(on: boolean) { this.#controls.autoRotate = on; if (!on) this.#halt(); this.#loop(); }

  /** Pause stops the model where it is: the controls' easing would carry the turn on, for seconds on a slow
   *  renderer. One update without damping clears what is left of it; the camera stays where it was. */
  #halt(): void {
    const at = this.#camera.position.clone();
    this.#controls.enableDamping = false;
    this.#controls.update();
    this.#camera.position.copy(at);
    this.#controls.update();
    this.#controls.enableDamping = true;
    this.#invalidate();
    this.#report();
  }

  /** Turns the vehicle by `radians` about the vertical axis (keyboard and button control). */
  turn(radians: number): void {
    const offset = this.#camera.position.clone().sub(this.#controls.target).applyAxisAngle(UP, radians);
    this.#camera.position.copy(this.#controls.target).add(offset);
    this.#controls.update();
    this.#invalidate(true);
    this.#report();
  }

  /** Zooms in (`+1`) or out (`-1`) one step, within the limits (MPES §10.2). */
  zoom(press: 1 | -1): void {
    this.#zoom = zoomed(this.#zoom, press);
    this.#place();
    this.#invalidate(true);
  }

  /**
   * Builds the vehicle and compiles every shader it can need, each part's material whether fitted or not, without
   * blocking the page where the browser compiles in parallel (KHR_parallel_shader_compile). The first draw and the
   * first draw of each purchase then have nothing left to compile (G3 profile: the first draw was one task of 0.3 to
   * 2.7 s on a software renderer). Draws nothing: the canvas is not on the page yet. False if there is no such vehicle.
   */
  async prepare(lib: Group, vehicle: string, size = { width: 640, height: 360 }): Promise<boolean> {
    if (!this.show(lib, vehicle, [])) return false;
    await this.#renderer.compileAsync(this.#scene, this.#camera);
    this.#calibrate(size);
    // Then every part, without delaying the first draw. three.js compiles only what is visible, but only the call itself
    // needs the parts shown: the browser finishes compiling them in parallel after they are hidden again.
    const parts = this.#vehicle!.children.filter(node => !node.visible);
    for (const node of parts) node.visible = true;
    void this.#renderer.compileAsync(this.#scene, this.#camera).catch(() => undefined);
    for (const node of parts) node.visible = false;
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Picks the starting tier from one timed draw per tier at the size the stage will have (pace.ts startTier), so a slow
   * machine starts where it can keep up instead of spending its first purchases at full quality (G3, CI run
   * 38571533524: about 170 ms a draw). Each draw is waited for by reading one pixel back. The first, at 1 px, only
   * prepares the resolve to the canvas, so no timed draw includes compiling it.
   */
  #calibrate(size: { width: number; height: number }): void {
    const gl = this.#renderer.getContext(), pixel = new Uint8Array(4);
    const timed = (): number => {
      const start = performance.now();
      this.#render();
      gl.readPixels(0, 0, 1, 1, gl.RGBA, gl.UNSIGNED_BYTE, pixel);
      return performance.now() - start;
    };
    this.#renderer.setSize(1, 1, false);
    this.#tierTo(0);
    timed();
    this.#renderer.setSize(size.width, size.height, false);
    this.#camera.aspect = size.width / size.height;
    this.#camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
    this.#refit();
    this.#tierTo(startTier(tier => { this.#tierTo(tier); return timed(); }));
    this.#renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true;
  }

  /** Shows one vehicle with the given part nodes; returns false if the library has no such vehicle. */
  show(lib: Group, vehicle: string, parts: readonly string[]): boolean {
    const source = lib.getObjectByName(vehicle);
    if (!source) return false;
    const fresh = this.#vehicle?.name !== vehicle;
    if (fresh) {
      if (this.#vehicle) this.#scene.remove(this.#vehicle);
      this.#vehicle = source.clone();
      this.#vehicle.traverse(o => {
        if (o instanceof Mesh) {
          o.castShadow = true;
          const m = o.material as MeshStandardMaterial;
          m.envMapIntensity = 0.9;
        }
      });
      this.#scene.add(this.#vehicle);
    }
    const shown = new Set(parts);
    for (const node of this.#vehicle!.children) node.visible = layerOf(node) === 'base' || shown.has(layerOf(node));
    this.#renderer.shadowMap.needsUpdate = true;
    this.#frameCamera(fresh);
    this.#invalidate(true);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Frames the vehicle as fitted, so every installed part stays in view at every turn and drag height however fully it
   * is kitted out (the whole catalogue spans 13 m, so framing every possible part would leave a bare vehicle tiny).
   * A new vehicle opens on the three-quarter view at full frame; a purchase keeps the player's view and zoom.
   */
  #frameCamera(fresh: boolean): void {
    if (!this.#vehicle) return;
    const kit = new Box3();
    for (const node of this.#vehicle.children) if (node.visible) kit.union(new Box3().setFromObject(node));
    if (!fresh && kit.equals(this.#kit)) { this.#invalidate(); return; }
    const offset = this.#camera.position.clone().sub(this.#controls.target);
    this.#kit.copy(kit);
    this.#kit.getCenter(this.#controls.target);
    if (fresh) { offset.copy(OPENING); this.#zoom = 1; }
    this.#camera.position.copy(this.#controls.target).add(offset);
    this.#refit();
  }

  /** The distance that frames the kit at this aspect, then the camera placed at the player's zoom of it. */
  #refit(): void {
    if (!this.#vehicle) return;
    this.#fittedAspect = this.#camera.aspect;
    this.#fitted = fitTable(this.#kit, this.#controls.target, POLAR_MIN, POLAR_MAX, this.#camera.fov, this.#camera.aspect);
    this.#place();
  }

  /** Moves the camera along its current direction to the zoomed distance. */
  #place(): void {
    this.#distance();
    this.#controls.update();
    this.#invalidate();
    this.#report();
  }

  /** Sets the camera's distance for its height (a drag up needs it farther back) at the player's zoom. */
  #distance(): void {
    const offset = this.#camera.position.clone().sub(this.#controls.target);
    if (offset.lengthSq() === 0) offset.copy(OPENING);
    const polar = Math.acos(Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, offset.y / offset.length())));
    this.#camera.position.copy(this.#controls.target).add(offset.setLength(distanceAt(this.#fitted, polar) * this.#zoom));
  }

  #size(): void {
    const { clientWidth: w, clientHeight: h } = this.canvas;
    if (!w || !h) return;
    this.#renderer.setSize(w, h, false);
    this.#fitTarget();
    this.#camera.aspect = w / h;
    this.#camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
    if (this.#camera.aspect !== this.#fittedAspect) this.#refit();
    this.#invalidate(true);
  }

  /**
   * Asks for a redraw: in the next paced frame, or, for a change the player asked for (`urgent`), in the next animation
   * frame whatever the pacer's wait. The pacer times a draw by the gap to the next frame, so the page work of a
   * purchase (its re-render) reads as drawing cost and stretched the wait to half a second (G3, CI showcase budget);
   * one draw per action cannot load the machine. Nothing draws synchronously.
   */
  #invalidate(urgent = false): void {
    this.#dirty = true;
    if (urgent) this.#urgent = true;
    this.#loop();
  }

  /** Draws at `tier`: the screen's pixel ratio, at most 1.5, at the tier's share, multisampled if the tier is. */
  #tierTo(tier: number): void {
    this.#tier = tier;
    this.#renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5) * TIERS[tier]!.scale);
    this.#fitTarget();
    this.canvas.setAttribute('data-tier', String(tier));
  }

  /** The multisampled target at the canvas's drawing size, or none on a tier without multisampling. */
  #fitTarget(): void {
    const samples = TIERS[this.#tier]!.samples, size = this.#renderer.getDrawingBufferSize(new Vector2());
    if (!samples) { this.#target?.dispose(); this.#target = null; return; }
    if (this.#target?.samples === samples) { this.#target.setSize(size.x, size.y); return; }
    this.#target?.dispose();
    // Half floats keep the scene linear and unclamped until the resolve tone-maps it, as drawing to the canvas does.
    this.#target = new WebGLRenderTarget(size.x, size.y, { samples, type: HalfFloatType });
  }

  /** Steps the quality down when the recent draws show this machine cannot draw in time (see nextTier). */
  #adapt(): void {
    const tier = nextTier(this.#tier, this.#pacer.floor);
    if (tier === this.#tier) return;
    this.#pacer.forget();
    this.#tierTo(tier);
    this.#dirty = true;
  }

  /** The scene to the canvas: straight, or through the multisampled target and its tone-mapping resolve. */
  #render(): void {
    if (!this.#target) { this.#renderer.render(this.#scene, this.#camera); return; }
    this.#renderer.setRenderTarget(this.#target);
    this.#renderer.render(this.#scene, this.#camera);
    this.#output.render(this.#renderer, null as unknown as WebGLRenderTarget, this.#target, 0, false);
  }

  #draw(): void {
    this.#dirty = false;
    this.#urgent = false;
    this.#distance();
    // Observable without reaching into the stage: the reference-laptop run brackets each draw's GPU time by these (§14.1).
    this.canvas.dispatchEvent(new Event('sea-drawing'));
    this.#render();
    this.#report();
    this.onDraw?.();
    // Observable without reaching into the stage: the reference-laptop run times real draws by this event (MPES §14).
    this.canvas.dispatchEvent(new Event('sea-draw'));
  }

  /** Tells `onView` where the camera is: each draw, and at once after a pause, turn, zoom or refit, so the reading never
   *  lags a player's action by a paced draw (or for good while the stage is off screen and not drawing). */
  #report(): void {
    if (this.onView) {
      const offset = this.#camera.position.clone().sub(this.#controls.target), distance = offset.length();
      const extent = extentAt(this.#kit, this.#controls.target, offset.divideScalar(distance), distance, this.#camera.fov, this.#camera.aspect);
      this.onView(this.#controls.getAzimuthalAngle(), extent, this.#zoom);
    }
  }

  #stop(): void {
    cancelAnimationFrame(this.#frame);
    this.#frame = 0;
    this.#pacer.pause();
  }

  /** Animates only while the stage is visible and turning or waiting to redraw; the pacer picks the frames that draw. */
  #loop(): void {
    const running = !this.#lost && this.#visible && document.visibilityState === 'visible' && this.canvas.isConnected;
    if (!running) { this.#stop(); return; }
    if (this.#frame) return;
    this.#timer.update();
    const tick = (now: number) => {
      this.#frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
      if (!this.#pacer.due(now) && !this.#urgent) return;
      this.#timer.update(now);
      const moved = this.#controls.update(this.#timer.getDelta());
      this.#adapt();
      if (this.#dirty) { this.#draw(); this.#pacer.drew(now); }
      if (!moved && !this.#controls.autoRotate && !this.#dirty) this.#stop();
    };
    this.#frame = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }

  /**
   * Restarts the loop after the canvas is re-attached to the page. The size is left to the ResizeObserver: it reports
   * after the next layout if the size changed. Reading it here would force a layout of the page being replaced
   * (G3 profile: about 15 ms per purchase at 4x).
   */
  attached(): void {
    this.#loop();
  }

  dispose(): void {
    cancelAnimationFrame(this.#frame);
    this.#listening.abort();
    clearInterval(this.#watch);
    this.#observer.disconnect();
    this.#resize.disconnect();
    this.#controls.dispose();
    this.#target?.dispose();
    this.#output.dispose();
    this.#environment?.dispose();
    this.#renderer.dispose();
  }
}

/** The resolve of a multisampled tier to the canvas: tone mapping and sRGB, aware of transparent edges (resolve.ts). */
function resolvePass(): OutputPass {
  const pass = Object.assign(new OutputPass(), { renderToScreen: true });
  pass.material.fragmentShader = premultipliedOutput(pass.material.fragmentShader);
  return pass;
}
```

### source/showcase/pace.ts

Paths: `source/showcase/pace.ts`. SHA-256 `4170eed2da54f3f90ba85a96210da60d6633242fc5d5d87f71606ed64a73016c`, 4653 bytes.

```ts
/** Fastest the showcase draws: 30 fps is smooth for a slow turn and halves the GPU work of 60 fps. */
export const FRAME_MS = 1000 / 30;
/** Slowest it draws while turning, so even a struggling machine shows movement. */
const CEILING_MS = 1000;
/** Animation frames arrive with a little jitter; a frame this close to due counts as due. */
const SLACK_MS = 2;
/** Draws behind `floor`: enough that one quiet frame among them shows what drawing alone costs. */
const RECENT = 8;

/** Paced draws wait this long after the player's input elsewhere on the page, so the answer to it draws first. */
export const INPUT_HOLD_MS = 1000;

/**
 * Drawing quality tiers (MPES §10.3 adaptive tiers), dearest first: the share of the full pixel ratio, and the
 * multisampling of edges. Multisampling goes before the last step of resolution: on a software renderer it made a
 * draw 3.6 times dearer, where halving the resolution saved less (G3 draw-cost probe).
 */
export const TIERS: readonly { scale: number; samples: number }[] = [
  { scale: 1, samples: 4 },
  { scale: 0.75, samples: 4 },
  { scale: 0.75, samples: 0 },
  { scale: 0.5, samples: 0 },
];

/**
 * The tier to draw at next: one step down when even the cheapest recent draw could not hold 30 fps (`floor` above
 * FRAME_MS), else unchanged. Never up within a session, so the picture cannot flicker between sizes; a hardware GPU
 * stays at full quality, a slow or software one drops until a draw fits (G3: a software renderer took about 60 ms
 * a draw, so each purchase waited on two of them).
 */
export function nextTier(tier: number, floor: number): number {
  return floor > FRAME_MS && tier < TIERS.length - 1 ? tier + 1 : tier;
}

/**
 * The tier to start at, from single timed draws (`measure` draws once at a tier and returns how long the renderer took,
 * in ms): the first that fits a 30 fps frame, else the cheapest. Before the stage is shown, so a slow machine does not
 * begin at full quality and spend seconds of turning stepping down. A tier that differs only in resolution is skipped
 * when its share of pixels could not bring the last cost within the frame even if a draw cost nothing else.
 */
export function startTier(measure: (tier: number) => number, budget = FRAME_MS): number {
  let last: { tier: number; cost: number } | null = null;
  for (let tier = 0; tier < TIERS.length; tier++) {
    if (last) {
      const [was, now] = [TIERS[last.tier]!, TIERS[tier]!];
      if (was.samples === now.samples && last.cost * (now.scale / was.scale) ** 2 > budget && tier < TIERS.length - 1) continue;
    }
    const cost = measure(tier);
    if (cost <= budget) return tier;
    last = { tier, cost };
  }
  return TIERS.length - 1;
}

/**
 * Decides which animation frames draw (MPES §10.3). A drawn frame is timed by the gap to the next animation
 * frame, which includes the GPU work the browser waited for; the next draw then waits at least twice that,
 * so the showcase never takes more than half the machine, however slow the graphics.
 */
export class FramePacer {
  #interval = FRAME_MS;
  #last = -Infinity;
  #drewAt = Number.NaN;
  #cost = 0;
  #recent: number[] = [];
  #held = -Infinity;

  /** Milliseconds the pacer currently waits between draws. */
  get interval(): number { return this.#interval; }

  /** The cheapest of the last few draws (page work only ever adds to a sample); NaN until there are enough. */
  get floor(): number { return this.#recent.length < RECENT ? Number.NaN : Math.min(...this.#recent); }

  /** No paced draw before `until` (the player's input comes first); urgent draws are the caller's and still go. */
  hold(until: number): void { this.#held = Math.max(this.#held, until); }

  /** Starts `floor` afresh, after the drawing itself changed (a new tier). */
  forget(): void { this.#recent = []; }

  /** Call on every animation frame; true when this frame may draw. */
  due(now: number): boolean {
    if (!Number.isNaN(this.#drewAt)) {
      const sample = now - this.#drewAt;
      this.#cost = this.#cost ? this.#cost * 0.6 + sample * 0.4 : sample;
      this.#recent.push(sample);
      if (this.#recent.length > RECENT) this.#recent.shift();
      this.#interval = Math.min(CEILING_MS, Math.max(FRAME_MS, 2 * this.#cost));
      this.#drewAt = Number.NaN;
    }
    return now >= this.#held && now - this.#last >= this.#interval - SLACK_MS;
  }

  /** Call after drawing in the frame stamped `now`. */
  drew(now: number): void {
    this.#last = now;
    this.#drewAt = now;
  }

  /** Call when the animation stops, so the idle gap is not mistaken for drawing time. */
  pause(): void { this.#drewAt = Number.NaN; }
}
```

### source/showcase/renders.ts

```ts
// Embedded photoreal renders (MPES §11): one inert JSON block written by the build, read once on demand.
import type { MissionId } from '../domain/data.ts';

export interface Render {
  readonly src: string;
  readonly kind: string;
  /** Camera distance of a build layer: the draw order, farthest first (MPES §10.2). */
  readonly depth?: number | null;
  /** Mount slot of a build layer: one part per slot is drawn (MPES §10.2). */
  readonly slot?: string;
  readonly frame: { readonly width: number; readonly height: number };
  readonly offset: { readonly left: number; readonly top: number };
  readonly size: { readonly width: number; readonly height: number };
}

let table: ReadonlyMap<string, Render> | null = null;

export function renders(): ReadonlyMap<string, Render> {
  if (table) return table;
  const block = document.getElementById('sea-renders')?.textContent ?? '';
  let parsed: Record<string, Render> = {};
  try { parsed = block ? JSON.parse(block) as Record<string, Render> : {}; } catch { parsed = {}; }
  table = new Map(Object.entries(parsed));
  return table;
}

/** File-name stem of each mission's vehicle (MPES §11). */
export const VEHICLE: Readonly<Record<MissionId, string>> = {
  COMBAT: 'combat', RECCE: 'recce', TROOP: 'troop-carrier', COMMAND: 'command-post', RECOVERY: 'recovery', MINE: 'mine-clearing',
};

export function cardRender(cardId: string): Render | undefined {
  return renders().get(`card-${cardId}`);
}
```

### source/showcase/resolve.ts

Paths: `source/showcase/resolve.ts`. SHA-256 `267570117c5ccd681fe6564fc05f2026e35959c434d35a3b7d583760a39dc3b7`, 1136 bytes.

```ts
/**
 * The tone-mapping resolve of a multisampled tier (MPES §10.3), made aware of transparency. The scene is drawn into a
 * target cleared to transparent, so an edge pixel holds its colour already multiplied by how much of it the vehicle
 * covers (premultiplied). Tone mapping and the sRGB curve are not linear: applied to that product they brighten the
 * edge into a pale fringe on the dark stage (Codex G3 review). So the colour is divided by its coverage first, mapped,
 * then multiplied again for the canvas, which expects premultiplied colour.
 */
const READ = 'gl_FragColor = texture2D( tDiffuse, vUv );';
const END = /\}\s*$/;

/** three.js's OutputShader fragment source with the division and multiplication added; throws if its shape changed. */
export function premultipliedOutput(fragment: string): string {
  if (!fragment.includes(READ) || !END.test(fragment)) throw new Error('OutputShader changed: review source/showcase/resolve.ts');
  return fragment
    .replace(READ, `${READ}\n\tif ( gl_FragColor.a > 0.0 ) gl_FragColor.rgb /= gl_FragColor.a;`)
    .replace(END, '\tgl_FragColor.rgb *= gl_FragColor.a;\n}');
}
```

```ts
// Vehicle showcase (MPES §10): the team's vehicle with its installed parts, as a slowly turning 3D model the
// player can drag, pause and turn by button. Without WebGL, or if the model cannot load, it stacks the still
// renders instead (base vehicle, then one layer per installed part; front, rear and a turntable). Both modes list
// the installed parts as text and show process cards as badges.
import type { Group } from 'three';
import type { MissionId } from '../domain/data.ts';
import { h } from '../ui/dom.ts';
import { loadVehicle, ModelStage, partSlots, webglAvailable } from './model.ts';
import { renders, VEHICLE, type Render } from './renders.ts';

export type ShowcaseView = 'front' | 'rear' | 'turntable';
export interface ShowcasePart { readonly id: string; readonly title: string; readonly category?: string }
export interface ShowcaseText {
  readonly title: string; readonly view: string; readonly front: string; readonly rear: string;
  readonly turntable: string; readonly rotate: string; readonly installed: string; readonly none: string;
  /** Text alternative and visible note for the turntable, which shows the base vehicle only. */
  readonly turntableLabel: string; readonly turntableNote: string;
  /** Heading of the SE_PROCESS badges, and the note shown when a mount holds more than one part. */
  readonly process: string; readonly slotNote: string;
  /** The 3D stage's hint and the names of its pause, turn and zoom buttons (each shows a sign, MPES §10.2). */
  readonly drag: string; readonly pause: string; readonly resume: string; readonly left: string; readonly right: string;
  readonly zoomIn: string; readonly zoomOut: string;
}

/** One press of a turn button turns the 3D vehicle by this much (radians). */
export const TURN_STEP = Math.PI / 8;

const VIEWS: readonly ShowcaseView[] = ['front', 'rear', 'turntable'];

function frames(vehicle: string): string[] {
  return [...renders().keys()].filter(k => k.startsWith(`${vehicle}-turntable-`)).sort();
}

/**
 * Parts drawn at this vehicle and angle, farthest from the camera first (MPES §10.2). Parts share mount
 * slots; only the most recently recorded part of each slot is drawn (`parts` is in purchase order).
 * The slot is read from either angle, so a part hidden behind the hull at one angle still replaces the
 * older part in its slot there.
 */
export function stackOrder<P extends ShowcasePart>(table: ReadonlyMap<string, Render>, vehicle: string, angle: string, parts: readonly P[]): P[] {
  const depth = (p: P) => table.get(`${vehicle}-${angle}-${p.id}`)?.depth ?? 0;
  return latestPerSlot(table, vehicle, parts).filter(p => table.has(`${vehicle}-${angle}-${p.id}`)).sort((a, b) => depth(b) - depth(a));
}

/** The most recently recorded part of each mount slot, in purchase order (parts with no slot are dropped). */
export function latestBySlot<P extends ShowcasePart>(parts: readonly P[], slotOf: (p: P) => string | undefined): P[] {
  const latest = new Map<string, P>();
  for (const p of parts) {
    const slot = slotOf(p);
    if (slot) { latest.delete(slot); latest.set(slot, p); }
  }
  return [...latest.values()];
}

/** latestBySlot for the still renders; the slot is read from either angle. */
export function latestPerSlot<P extends ShowcasePart>(table: ReadonlyMap<string, Render>, vehicle: string, parts: readonly P[]): P[] {
  return latestBySlot(parts, p => {
    const front = table.get(`${vehicle}-front-${p.id}`), rear = table.get(`${vehicle}-rear-${p.id}`);
    return front || rear ? front?.slot ?? rear?.slot ?? p.id : undefined;
  });
}

/**
 * Decoded still images, reused so no layer is ever decoded twice (MPES §10.3). Decoding runs off the main thread
 * and dominates update time on slow machines; a new <img> for an unchanged layer would decode it again. Never dropped:
 * an image on screen, or one in the prepared set (`keep`): a fully built vehicle has up to 20 layers and a base per
 * angle, and the next view is prepared on top of the shown one, so no fixed count covers both. `limit` bounds only the
 * rest, the most recently used images of views left behind.
 */
export class DecodedImages {
  readonly #images = new Map<string, HTMLImageElement>();
  #kept = new Set<string>();
  readonly limit: number;
  readonly #create: (src: string) => HTMLImageElement;
  constructor(limit = 24, create = (src: string) => h('img', { src, alt: '', decoding: 'async', draggable: 'false' })) {
    this.limit = limit;
    this.#create = create;
  }

  /** The image for this source, decoded once; the least recently used one neither on screen nor kept is dropped. */
  get(src: string): HTMLImageElement {
    let img = this.#images.get(src);
    if (img) this.#images.delete(src);
    else img = this.#create(src);
    this.#images.set(src, img);
    let spare = [...this.#images].filter(([key, old]) => !old.isConnected && !this.#kept.has(key)).length;
    for (const [key, old] of this.#images) {
      if (spare <= this.limit) break;
      if (!old.isConnected && !this.#kept.has(key)) { this.#images.delete(key); spare--; }
    }
    return img;
  }

  /** The images of the next views, held until the next call replaces the set; nearest first, as given. */
  keep(srcs: readonly string[]): HTMLImageElement[] {
    this.#kept = new Set(srcs);
    return srcs.map(src => this.get(src));
  }

  /** Decodes ahead of need; settles either way. */
  prepare(src: string): Promise<void> {
    return this.get(src).decode().catch(() => undefined);
  }

  get size(): number { return this.#images.size; }
}

const LAYER_ATTRS = ['data-layer', 'data-frame', 'data-angle'];

function place(img: HTMLImageElement, render: Render, attrs: Record<string, string>): HTMLImageElement {
  for (const name of LAYER_ATTRS) img.removeAttribute(name);
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(attrs)) img.setAttribute(name, value);
  // Placement through the CSSOM (allowed by the hash-pinned CSP; style attributes are not).
  img.style.left = `${(render.offset.left / render.frame.width) * 100}%`;
  img.style.top = `${(render.offset.top / render.frame.height) * 100}%`;
  img.style.width = `${(render.size.width / render.frame.width) * 100}%`;
  return img;
}

export class Showcase {
  readonly element: HTMLElement;
  #view: ShowcaseView = 'front';
  #frame = 0;
  #mode: 'pending' | '3d' | 'stills' = 'pending';
  #model: { stage: ModelStage; libraries: Map<string, Group>; element: HTMLElement } | null = null;
  #last: (() => void) | null = null;

  constructor() {
    this.element = h('section', { class: 'panel showcase stack', id: 'showcase', 'aria-labelledby': 'showcase-heading' });
  }

  /** `upcoming` is the card the player has loaded: the part most likely recorded next. */
  update(mission: MissionId, parts: readonly ShowcasePart[], label: string, text: ShowcaseText, upcoming: ShowcasePart | null = null): HTMLElement {
    this.#upcoming = upcoming;
    this.#last = () => this.update(mission, parts, label, text, upcoming);
    if (this.#mode === 'pending') this.#start(VEHICLE[mission]);
    return this.#mode === '3d' ? this.#update3d(mission, parts, label, text) : this.#updateStills(mission, parts, label, text);
  }

  /**
   * Decides the mode once: stills at first, then 3D once WebGL is confirmed and the team's vehicle model has
   * loaded. Only that vehicle is decoded (MPES §14 model-ready budget); another is decoded if the mission changes.
   */
  #start(vehicle: string): void {
    this.#mode = 'stills';
    if (!webglAvailable()) return;
    void loadVehicle(vehicle).then(async library => {
      if (!library) return;
      const stage = new ModelStage();
      // Stills stay up while the stage compiles its shaders, so the page never waits on the compiler.
      // The stills hold the place the stage takes, so their size is the size its starting tier is timed at (one layout read).
      const box = this.element.querySelector('.showcase-stage')?.getBoundingClientRect();
      if (!await stage.prepare(library, vehicle, box?.width && box.height ? { width: box.width, height: box.height } : undefined)) { stage.dispose(); return; }
      const element = h('div', { class: 'showcase-stage showcase-3d', role: 'img', 'data-mode': '3d', 'data-ready': 'false' });
      element.appendChild(stage.canvas);
      stage.onView = (azimuth, extent, zoom) => {
        element.setAttribute('data-azimuth', azimuth.toFixed(3));
        element.setAttribute('data-extent', extent.toFixed(3));
        element.setAttribute('data-zoom', zoom.toFixed(3));
      };
      // The parts the canvas actually shows: `data-layers` changes when a purchase is recorded, `data-drawn` only once
      // the next draw has put them on screen (the MPES §14 update and ready budgets end here, not at the request).
      stage.onDraw = () => {
        const layers = element.getAttribute('data-layers');
        if (layers !== null && element.getAttribute('data-drawn') !== layers) element.setAttribute('data-drawn', layers);
      };
      this.#model = { stage, libraries: new Map([[vehicle, library]]), element };
      this.#mode = '3d';
      if (this.element.isConnected) this.#last?.();
    });
  }

  #update3d(mission: MissionId, parts: readonly ShowcasePart[], label: string, text: ShowcaseText): HTMLElement {
    const { stage, libraries, element } = this.#model!;
    const vehicle = VEHICLE[mission];
    const library = libraries.get(vehicle);
    if (!library) {
      // A different mission: show its stills while its model decodes, then redraw (stills for good if it cannot load).
      void loadVehicle(vehicle).then(loaded => {
        if (loaded) libraries.set(vehicle, loaded); else this.#mode = 'stills';
        if (this.element.isConnected) this.#last?.();
      });
      return this.#updateStills(mission, parts, label, text);
    }
    const group = library.getObjectByName(vehicle);
    const slots = group ? partSlots(group) : new Map<string, string>();
    const physical = parts.filter(p => p.category !== 'SE_PROCESS');
    const shown = latestBySlot(physical, p => slots.get(p.id));
    if (!stage.show(library, vehicle, shown.map(p => p.id))) {
      this.#mode = 'stills';
      return this.#updateStills(mission, parts, label, text);
    }
    element.setAttribute('aria-label', label);
    element.setAttribute('data-layers', shown.map(p => p.id).sort().join(' '));
    element.setAttribute('data-ready', 'true');
    // Signs, not words: the name is the button's accessible name and its tooltip. The pause button keeps its name and
    // reports its state with aria-pressed; its sign and tooltip say what a press does next.
    const sign = (id: string, name: string, mark: string, click: (button: HTMLElement) => void) =>
      h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'btn sign', id, 'aria-label': name, title: name, text: mark, on: { click: e => click(e.currentTarget as HTMLElement) } });
    const paused = (button: HTMLElement) => {
      button.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(!stage.turning));
      button.textContent = stage.turning ? '‖' : '▷';
      button.title = stage.turning ? text.pause : text.resume;
    };
    const pause = sign('showcase-pause', text.pause, '', button => { stage.turning = !stage.turning; paused(button); });
    paused(pause);
    const controls = h('div', { class: 'cluster showcase-controls' }, pause,
      sign('showcase-left', text.left, '↺', () => stage.turn(-TURN_STEP)), sign('showcase-right', text.right, '↻', () => stage.turn(TURN_STEP)),
      sign('showcase-zoom-out', text.zoomOut, '−', () => stage.zoom(-1)), sign('showcase-zoom-in', text.zoomIn, '+', () => stage.zoom(1)));
    const slotNote = shown.length < physical.filter(p => slots.has(p.id)).length ? h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: text.slotNote }) : '';
    const focused = document.activeElement?.id;
    this.element.replaceChildren(h('h2', { id: 'showcase-heading', text: text.title }), element,
      h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: text.drag }), slotNote, controls, ...this.#lists(parts, text));
    stage.attached();
    if (focused?.startsWith('showcase-')) document.getElementById(focused)?.focus();
    return this.element;
  }

  /** The SE_PROCESS badges (process cards have no geometry, MPES §10.2) and the text list of installed parts. */
  #lists(parts: readonly ShowcasePart[], text: ShowcaseText): (HTMLElement | string)[] {
    const process = parts.filter(p => p.category === 'SE_PROCESS');
    const badges = process.length ? h('div', { class: 'stack' }, h('h3', { class: 'small', text: text.process }),
      h('ul', { class: 'badges' }, process.map(p => h('li', { class: 'badge' }, h('span', { class: 'mono', text: p.id }), ' ', p.title)))) : '';
    const installed = h('div', {}, h('h3', { class: 'small', text: text.installed }),
      parts.length ? h('ul', { class: 'installed' }, parts.map(p => h('li', {}, h('span', { class: 'mono small', text: p.id }), ' ', p.title)))
        : h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: text.none }));
    return [badges, installed];
  }

  /** The layers of one view, farthest first: a turntable frame, or the base and one part per mount at an angle. */
  #layers(vehicle: string, view: ShowcaseView, parts: readonly ShowcasePart[], frame: number): [Render, Record<string, string>][] {
    const table = renders();
    if (view === 'turntable') {
      const turntable = frames(vehicle);
      const key = turntable[(frame + turntable.length) % turntable.length];
      const render = key ? table.get(key) : undefined;
      return render ? [[render, { 'data-layer': 'base', 'data-frame': String((frame + turntable.length) % turntable.length) }]] : [];
    }
    const base = table.get(`${vehicle}-${view}-base`);
    return [
      ...(base ? [[base, { 'data-layer': 'base', 'data-angle': view }] as [Render, Record<string, string>]] : []),
      ...stackOrder(table, vehicle, view, parts).map(part =>
        [table.get(`${vehicle}-${view}-${part.id}`)!, { 'data-layer': part.id, 'data-angle': view }] as [Render, Record<string, string>]),
    ];
  }

  #draw(stage: HTMLElement, layers: [Render, Record<string, string>][]): void {
    const first = layers[0]?.[0];
    if (first) stage.style.aspectRatio = `${first.frame.width} / ${first.frame.height}`;
    stage.replaceChildren(...layers.map(([render, attrs]) => place(this.#images.get(render.src), render, attrs)));
  }

  /**
   * Prepares what the player can ask for next, nearest first: the loaded card's layers, at this angle and then the
   * other, so recording it never waits for a decode (CI run 38135172580: a fresh layer took 190 ms, budget 100); from
   * an angle, the other angle and the turntable frame shown on entry with the frames either side; when turning, the
   * frames ahead in the direction of travel, then behind. The images exist at once, so a step never creates one, and decode one at a time once the shown view has
   * decoded, so they never delay it. Not left for idle time: a busy machine may have none before the next step (CI run
   * 38106258905). `data-prepared` reports when it is done.
   */
  #prepare(stage: HTMLElement, vehicle: string, parts: readonly ShowcasePart[]): void {
    const generation = ++this.#generation;
    this.element.setAttribute('data-prepared', 'false');
    const d = this.#direction;
    const next: [Render, Record<string, string>][] = this.#view === 'turntable'
      ? [d, -d, 2 * d, -2 * d, 3 * d].flatMap(step => this.#layers(vehicle, 'turntable', parts, this.#frame + step))
      : [...this.#layers(vehicle, this.#view === 'front' ? 'rear' : 'front', parts, 0),
        ...[0, 1, -1].flatMap(step => this.#layers(vehicle, 'turntable', parts, this.#frame + step))];
    const id = this.#upcoming?.id, table = renders();
    const upcoming = id && this.#view !== 'turntable' && !parts.some(p => p.id === id)
      ? [this.#view, this.#view === 'front' ? 'rear' : 'front'].flatMap(view => table.get(`${vehicle}-${view}-${id}`) ?? []) : [];
    // Kept by the pool until the next view replaces them, so no prepared image is dropped and decoded again.
    const images = this.#images.keep([...upcoming, ...next.map(([render]) => render)].map(render => render.src));
    // One at a time, nearest first, stopping when the view changes: each background decode competes with the next
    // image the player waits for (CI run 38133130929: four at once made a purchase take 117 ms).
    void (async () => {
      await Promise.all([...stage.querySelectorAll('img')].map(img => img.decode().catch(() => undefined)));
      for (const img of images) {
        await this.#background; // a decode an earlier view started is still running
        if (generation !== this.#generation) return;
        this.#background = img.decode().catch(() => undefined);
        await this.#background;
      }
      if (generation === this.#generation) this.element.setAttribute('data-prepared', 'true');
    })();
  }

  #updateStills(mission: MissionId, parts: readonly ShowcasePart[], label: string, text: ShowcaseText): HTMLElement {
    const vehicle = VEHICLE[mission], table = renders();
    const turntable = frames(vehicle);
    if (this.#frame >= turntable.length) this.#frame = 0;
    const turning = this.#view === 'turntable';
    const stage = h('div', { class: 'showcase-stage', role: 'img', 'data-mode': 'stills', 'aria-label': turning ? text.turntableLabel : label });
    this.#draw(stage, this.#layers(vehicle, this.#view, parts, this.#frame));
    const views = h('fieldset', { class: 'cluster showcase-views' }, h('legend', { class: 'visually-hidden', text: text.view }),
      VIEWS.map(view => h('label', { class: 'choice' },
        h('input', { type: 'radio', name: 'showcase-view', id: `showcase-view-${view}`, value: view, checked: view === this.#view,
          on: { change: () => { this.#view = view; this.update(mission, parts, label, text); } } }),
        h('span', { text: text[view] }))));
    // Turntable scrubbing swaps one image without rebuilding the controls, so the slider keeps focus.
    const scrub = turning && turntable.length > 1
      ? h('div', { class: 'field' }, h('label', { for: 'showcase-turn', text: text.rotate }),
        h('input', { type: 'range', id: 'showcase-turn', min: '0', max: String(turntable.length - 1), step: '1', value: String(this.#frame),
          on: { input: e => {
            const frame = Number((e.target as HTMLInputElement).value), count = turntable.length;
            // Direction of travel on the ring: End from frame 0 is one step back.
            this.#direction = (frame - this.#frame + count) % count <= count / 2 ? 1 : -1;
            this.#frame = frame;
            this.#draw(stage, this.#layers(vehicle, 'turntable', parts, this.#frame));
            this.#prepare(stage, vehicle, parts);
          } } }))
      : null;
    const physical = parts.filter(p => p.category !== 'SE_PROCESS');
    const slotNote = !turning && latestPerSlot(table, vehicle, physical).length < physical.length ? h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: text.slotNote }) : '';
    const focused = document.activeElement?.id;
    const note = turning ? h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: text.turntableNote }) : '';
    this.element.replaceChildren(h('h2', { id: 'showcase-heading', text: text.title }), stage, note, slotNote, views, scrub ?? '', ...this.#lists(parts, text));
    if (focused?.startsWith('showcase-')) document.getElementById(focused)?.focus();
    this.#prepare(stage, vehicle, parts);
    return this.element;
  }

  readonly #images = new DecodedImages();
  #generation = 0;
  #direction: 1 | -1 = 1;
  #upcoming: ShowcasePart | null = null;
  #background: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();
}
```

```ts
import { showDialog } from './dialog.ts';
import { h } from './dom.ts';
import { translate, type Language, type StringKey } from './i18n.ts';
import { reflow } from './reflow.ts';

/** A licence file as reflowed text under its summary; a first heading that repeats the summary is dropped. */
function licenceText(summary: string, source: string): HTMLElement {
  const blocks = reflow(source).filter((b, i) => !(i === 0 && b.kind === 'heading' && b.text.toLowerCase() === summary.toLowerCase()));
  return h('details', {}, h('summary', { text: summary }), h('div', { class: 'licence-text' }, ...blocks.map(b =>
    b.kind === 'list' ? h('ul', {}, ...b.items.map(text => h('li', { text }))) : h(b.kind === 'heading' ? 'h3' : 'p', { text: b.text }))));
}

export function showAbout(lang: Language, opener: HTMLElement | null = null): Promise<string> {
  const t = (key: StringKey, vars?: Record<string, string>) => translate(lang, key, vars);
  return showDialog({
    title: t('about.title'),
    body: [
      h('p', { text: t('about.body', { version: __SEA_VERSION__ }) }),
      licenceText(t('about.licence'), __SEA_LICENSE__),
      licenceText(t('about.notices'), __SEA_NOTICES__),
    ],
    actions: [{ label: t('about.close'), value: 'close', kind: 'primary' }],
    cancelValue: 'close',
    opener,
  });
}
```

```ts
// Reusable views: cards, effects, mission minimums, gap meter, purchases (MPES §7.4).
import { CAPABILITIES, MISSIONS, mission as missionDef, type Capability, type MissionId, type Totals, type Effects } from '../domain/data.ts';
import type { MarketCard } from '../domain/market.ts';
import { compliant, score, shortfalls, sumEffects } from '../domain/missions.ts';
import type { Purchase } from '../domain/team.ts';
import { cardRender } from '../showcase/renders.ts';
import { h, type Child } from './dom.ts';
import { labelled, list, money, signed } from './format.ts';
import { translate, type Language, type StringKey } from './i18n.ts';

const tr = (lang: Language) => (key: StringKey, vars?: Readonly<Record<string, string | number>>) => translate(lang, key, vars);

export function missionName(id: MissionId, lang: Language): string {
  return missionDef(id).title[lang];
}

export function effectsList(effects: Effects, lang: Language): Child {
  const t = tr(lang);
  return h('ul', { class: 'effects' }, CAPABILITIES.filter(k => effects[k] !== undefined).map(k =>
    h('li', { class: (effects[k] ?? 0) < 0 ? 'penalty' : 'gain' },
      h('span', { class: 'num', text: signed(effects[k]!) }), ' ', `${t(`unit.${k}` as StringKey)} · ${t(`cap.${k}` as StringKey)}`)));
}

/** Stands for a card ID in a translated sentence, so `withId` can put the ID in a span that never breaks at its hyphen. */
export const ID_MARK = '\u0000';
export function withId(text: string, id: string): Child[] {
  return text.split(ID_MARK).flatMap((part, i) => i ? [h('span', { class: 'nowrap', text: id }), part] : [part]);
}

/** The same effects on one compact line (value, unit, capability), for lists of cards such as those leaving the game. */
export function effectsLine(effects: Effects, lang: Language): Child {
  const t = tr(lang);
  const items = CAPABILITIES.filter(k => effects[k] !== undefined).map(k =>
    h('span', { class: (effects[k] ?? 0) < 0 ? 'penalty' : 'gain' },
      h('span', { class: 'num', text: signed(effects[k]!) }), ' ', `${t(`unit.${k}` as StringKey)} ${t(`cap.${k}` as StringKey)}`));
  return h('span', { class: 'effects-line' }, items.flatMap((item, i) => i ? [', ', item] : [item]));
}

/** The card's photoreal render (MPES §11); every card and the practice card has one. */
export function cardImage(id: string, label: string): HTMLElement | null {
  const render = cardRender(id);
  return render ? h('img', { class: 'card-render', src: render.src, alt: label, decoding: 'async', width: String(render.size.width), height: String(render.size.height) }) : null;
}

export function cardDetails(card: MarketCard, lang: Language, headingLevel: 'h2' | 'h3' = 'h3'): HTMLElement {
  const t = tr(lang);
  return h('figure', { class: 'card-figure', 'data-card': card.id },
    cardImage(card.id, `${card.id} · ${card.title[lang]}`),
    h('figcaption', { class: 'stack' },
      h('p', { class: 'muted small' }, `${t(`cat.${card.cat}` as StringKey)} · `, h('span', { class: 'nowrap', text: card.id })),
      h(headingLevel, { text: card.title[lang] }),
      h('p', {}, labelled(t('common.startPrice'), lang), h('strong', { class: 'num', text: money(card.start, lang) })),
      effectsList(card.e, lang),
    ),
  );
}

export function missionTable(lang: Language, highlight?: MissionId | null): HTMLElement {
  const t = tr(lang);
  const keys: Capability[] = ['CAP', 'MOB', 'FP', 'PRO', 'COM', 'SA', 'REC', 'MC'];
  return h('div', { class: 'table-wrap' }, h('table', {},
    h('caption', { class: 'visually-hidden', text: t('planning.requirements') }),
    h('thead', {}, h('tr', {}, h('th', { scope: 'col', text: t('common.mission') }), keys.map(k => h('th', { scope: 'col', class: 'num', title: t(`cap.${k}` as StringKey), text: k })))),

      keys.map(k => h('td', { class: 'num', text: m.minimums[k] === undefined ? t('common.empty') : String(m.minimums[k]) })),
    ))),
  ));
}

/** Current totals against every minimum, with the shortfall in words (never colour alone). */
export function gapMeter(id: MissionId, totals: Totals, lang: Language, preview?: Totals): HTMLElement {
  const t = tr(lang);
  const minimums = missionDef(id).minimums;
  const rows = CAPABILITIES.filter(k => minimums[k] !== undefined).map(k => {
    const required = minimums[k]!, value = totals[k], after = preview?.[k];
    const scale = Math.max(required * 2, value, after ?? 0, 1);
    const fill = h('span', { class: 'fill' }), mark = h('span', { class: 'mark' });
    fill.style.width = `${Math.max(0, Math.min(100, (value / scale) * 100))}%`;
    mark.style.left = `${(required / scale) * 100}%`;
    const met = value >= required;
    return h('div', { class: `meter ${met ? '' : 'short'}`, role: 'group', 'aria-label': t(`cap.${k}` as StringKey) },
      h('span', { class: 'small', title: t(`cap.${k}` as StringKey), text: k }),
      h('span', { class: 'bar', 'aria-hidden': 'true' }, fill, mark),
      h('span', { class: 'small num' },
        `${value} / ${required} `,
        h('span', { class: met ? 'ok' : 'warn', text: met ? t('common.met') : t('common.short', { n: required - value }) }),
        after !== undefined && after !== value ? h('span', { class: 'muted', text: ` → ${after}` }) : null,
      ),
    );
  });
  const missing = shortfalls(id, totals).map(s => t(`cap.${s.capability}` as StringKey));
  return h('section', { class: 'stack', 'aria-label': t('strack.gap') },
    rows,
    h('p', { class: missing.length ? 'warn' : 'ok', text: missing.length ? t('common.notCompliant', { list: list(missing, lang) }) : t('common.compliant') }),
    h('p', {}, labelled(t('common.score'), lang), h('strong', { class: 'num', text: String(score(id, totals)) })),
  );
}

export interface PurchasesOptions {
  readonly action?: (p: Purchase) => Child;
  /** Adds "score it adds" per card: score with all purchases minus score without that card. */
  readonly mission?: MissionId;
}

export function purchasesTable(purchases: readonly Purchase[], lang: Language, options: PurchasesOptions = {}): HTMLElement {
  const t = tr(lang), { action, mission } = options;
  if (purchases.length === 0) return h('p', { class: 'muted', text: t('common.noPurchases') });
  const all = sumEffects(purchases.map(p => p.e));
  const value = (p: Purchase): Child => {
    if (!mission) return null;
    const without = sumEffects(purchases.filter(x => x !== p).map(x => x.e));
    const points = score(mission, all) - score(mission, without);
    const needed = compliant(mission, all) && !compliant(mission, without);
    return h('td', { class: 'num' }, signed(points), needed ? h('span', { class: 'small warn', text: ` · ${t('value.needed')}` }) : null);
  };
  return h('div', { class: 'table-wrap' }, h('table', {},
    h('caption', { class: 'visually-hidden', text: t('common.purchases') }),
    h('thead', {}, h('tr', {},
      h('th', { scope: 'col', text: t('strack.round') }), h('th', { scope: 'col', text: t('strack.lot') }),
      h('th', { scope: 'col', text: t('common.card') }), h('th', { scope: 'col', text: t('common.effects') }),
      h('th', { scope: 'col', class: 'num', text: t('common.price') }),
      mission ? h('th', { scope: 'col', class: 'num', text: t('value.points') }) : null,
      action ? h('th', { scope: 'col' }, h('span', { class: 'visually-hidden', text: t('sbuild.remove') })) : null,
    )),
    h('tbody', {}, purchases.map(p => h('tr', {},
      h('td', { class: 'num', text: String(p.round) }), h('td', { class: 'num', text: String(p.lot) }),
      h('td', {}, h('span', { class: 'mono small', text: p.id }), ' ', p.title[lang]),
      h('td', { class: 'small' }, effectsLine(p.e, lang)),
      h('td', { class: 'num', text: money(p.paid, lang) }),
      value(p),
      action ? h('td', {}, action(p)) : null,
    ))),
  ), mission ? h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: t('value.hint') }) : null);
}

export function complianceText(id: MissionId, totals: Totals, lang: Language): string {
  const t = tr(lang);
  if (compliant(id, totals)) return t('common.compliant');
  return t('common.notCompliant', { list: list(shortfalls(id, totals).map(s => t(`cap.${s.capability}` as StringKey)), lang) });
}

/** The original game's presentation questions (course source §18.18), asked of every team at the debrief. */
export function presentationQuestions(lang: Language): HTMLElement {
  const t = tr(lang);
  return h('section', { class: 'panel stack', 'aria-labelledby': 'questions-heading' },
    h('h2', { id: 'questions-heading', text: t('debrief.questions') }),
    h('p', { class: 'muted small', text: t('debrief.questionsHint') }),
    h('ol', { class: 'questions' }, ([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7] as const).map(n => h('li', { text: t(`debrief.q${n}`) }))));
}
```
